K00.titleEn: Container Fundamentals: VM vs Container, Image vs Container & Execution Lifecycle
K00.summaryEn: Understand Virtual Machines vs Containers, read-only Images vs running Container processes, the Docker/OrbStack/Podman ecosystem, and the pull, run, ps, stop, rm lifecycle.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
Whether you come from **Python (`FastAPI`, `Django`)**, **Node.js / TypeScript (`Express`, `Next.js`)**, or **Go / Java**, you have almost certainly heard the classic line that haunts every engineering team: *"Wait, it works fine on my machine!"*

- [>] On your personal macOS machine, you run **Python 3.12** (or **Node v22.12**), type the command, and everything runs smoothly without a single warning.
- [!] Push the code to an Ubuntu server (or send it to a colleague on Windows), and the app crashes right on startup: in Python it blows up with a missing system C library `libpq-dev` when installing `psycopg` or a `glibc` version mismatch; in Node.js it throws `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` on the `sharp` image-processing package, hits a `UTC` vs `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` timezone mismatch, or the server is still stuck on an outdated runtime!

Lockfiles like `uv.lock` / `requirements.txt` (Python) or `package-lock.json` (Node.js) only pin language-level package versions, leaving them **completely powerless** over the underlying OS and host C libraries. **Containers (under the open OCI standard)** were created to freeze the entire application + runtime + system libraries into a single unit: **ultra-lightweight**, **instant-starting**, and ==100% consistent everywhere==.

```visual
subtitle: Ba thực thể nền tảng biến mã nguồn (Python, Node.js, Go...) trên máy dev thành tiến trình chạy ổn định trên Production

    title: Container Image

    code: shop-api:1.4.2
    tone: cyan
    edge: docker pull / push
  - icon: cloud
    badge: Kho trung tâm
    title: Container Registry
    desc: Kho lưu trữ và phân phối Image theo tên & tag (Docker Hub, GHCR, AWS ECR)
```

steps.headingEn: Virtual Machines (VM) vs Containers, and Images vs Running Containers
steps.bodyEn:
Before typing any command, make sure you firmly grasp **the two most fundamental pairs of concepts** in the container ecosystem:

> [!NOTE] Virtual Machine (VM) vs Container
> - **Virtual Machine (VM):** A hypervisor emulates hardware so each VM boots a full guest operating system (a separate **Guest OS Kernel**, consuming gigabytes of RAM/disk and taking tens of seconds to minutes to boot).
> - **Container:** A regular Linux process isolated in visibility (`Namespaces`) and resource limits (`cgroups`), **sharing the host machine's existing Linux Kernel (Host Linux Kernel)**. By skipping the Guest OS layer, a container weighs only tens of MBs and starts in **~50–80 milliseconds**. Put simply: a VM is like building a standalone house with its own private power and water utilities, whereas Containers are private apartments sharing the entire building's core utility infrastructure.

> [!TIP] Container Image (Read-Only) vs Container (Running)
> - **Container Image:** An **immutable, read-only** frozen software package sitting on disk (similar to a `class` blueprint in object-oriented programming), containing source code, runtime, and system libraries.
> - **Container:** A **live executing process (`instance`) in RAM** instantiated from an Image, with **1 thin temporary writable layer (Read-Write layer)** mounted on top for ephemeral writes. From **1 single Image**, you can launch dozens of Containers in parallel without duplicating the underlying base layers on disk (just as a single mold can cast many independent instances).

```visual
kind: illustration
diagram: "kube:k00"
src: "/illustrations/kube/docker-vm-vs-container.jpg"
alt: "So sánh kiến trúc Máy ảo Hypervisor với Container chia sẻ Host Kernel và các lớp ảnh chỉ đọc OverlayFS"

subtitle: "Loại bỏ hoàn toàn nhân hệ điều hành khách (Guest OS) để bật tiến trình cô lập trong vài chục mili-giây"
caption: "Đối chiếu ngăn xếp Hypervisor/Guest OS của VM với Docker Container dùng chung Host Kernel và cơ chế xếp chồng Read-Only Image Layers"
callouts:
  - num: 1
    label: "Ngăn xếp Máy ảo (VM) — Kèm Guest OS riêng biệt"
    desc: "Mỗi VM phải gánh riêng một nhân Guest OS đầy đủ bên trên tầng Hypervisor giả lập phần cứng, tiêu tốn hàng GB RAM."
    tone: rose
  - num: 2
    label: "Container — Dùng chung Host Linux Kernel"
    desc: "Mọi tiến trình container gọi thẳng syscall vào nhân Linux sẵn có của máy chủ, cô lập gọn nhẹ bằng Namespaces và cgroups."
    tone: emerald
  - num: 3
    label: "Các lớp Image bất biến & Lớp ghi tạm mỏng"
    desc: "Hàng chục container dùng chung các Read-Only Layers bên dưới và chỉ gắn thêm 1 lớp R/W mỏng ở trên cùng khi chạy."
    tone: sky
```

| Familiar in Python & Node.js | Container Concept | Actual Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pyproject.toml` / `package.json` + OS setup guide | **`Dockerfile`** | Plain-text recipe describing step-by-step OS, runtime (Python/Node), and code copying |
| Frozen `.venv` / `node_modules` bundled with Linux | **Container Image** | **Read-only** OCI-standard packaging unit stacked from immutable layers |
| Live process `uvicorn main:app` / `node server.js` | **Container** | Linux process executing from an Image, with **1 thin writable layer** attached on top |
| `PyPI` (`uv add`) / `npm` (`npm install`) registry | **Container Registry** | Central repository (Docker Hub, GHCR, ECR) for `docker pull` / `docker push` |

steps.headingEn: Image Naming Structure & Popular Container Engines in 2026
steps.bodyEn:
When you encounter strings like `ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:1.4.2`, `python:3.12-slim`, or `redis:7-alpine`, their structure looks very much like the versioned package names you use every day:

```visual
kind: groups
title: "Cấu Trúc Tên Gọi Image — [registry]/[namespace]/[repo]:[tag]"
subtitle: "Ví dụ chuẩn: ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:1.4.2 hoặc viết gọn python:3.12-slim (= docker.io/library/python:3.12-slim)"
columns: 2
items:
  - num: 1
    title: Registry Host & Namespace
    badge: Kho lưu trữ
    tone: sky
    bullets:
      - "`ghcr.io/acme` chỉ định kho GitHub Container Registry của tổ chức `acme`"
      - "Nếu viết gọn `redis:7-alpine` hay `python:3.12-slim`, công cụ tự hiểu ngầm là **`docker.io/library/...`** trên Docker Hub chính thức"
  - num: 2
    title: Tag Phiên Bản & Biến Thể (-alpine vs -slim)
    badge: Bắt buộc ghim rõ
    tone: amber
    bullets:
      - "Nếu **bỏ trống `:tag`** (chỉ gõ `docker pull node` hay `docker pull python`), Docker tự gắn nhãn mặc định ==`:latest`== — **tuyệt đối tránh trên Production** vì hôm sau build lại có thể nhảy phiên bản gây sập app!"
      - "Với **Node.js / Go / Redis**, đuôi **`-alpine`** (Alpine Linux `musl`, ~5MB nền) rất được ưa chuộng; còn với **Python / AI / FastAPI**, cộng đồng ưu tiên **`python:3.12-slim`** (Debian `glibc` gọn nhẹ) để cài mượt các gói biên dịch C (`numpy`, `pydantic-core`, `psycopg`) không bị chậm!"
```

> [!NOTE] The 2026 Container Engine Ecosystem: It's Not Just Docker Desktop Anymore!
> Because the Image format is openly standardized (**OCI — Open Container Initiative**), all concepts and commands in this course are compatible across the 3 most popular engines today:
> - **Docker Desktop:** Most common on Windows (WSL2) and macOS, featuring an intuitive GUI for beginners.
> - **OrbStack (Recommended on macOS Apple Silicon):** A drop-in replacement for Docker Desktop on Mac — boots in **2 seconds**, uses far less RAM/battery, offers vastly faster file networking, and keeps 100% compatibility with `docker` and `docker compose` commands.
> - **Podman:** Enterprise-standard engine on Linux/RHEL with a **daemonless** architecture and **rootless** execution by default — just set `alias docker=podman` and type the exact same Docker commands!

steps.headingEn: The 4-Step Container Lifecycle & Your First Multi-Language Run
steps.bodyEn:
```visual
kind: flow
title: Vòng Đời Tiến Trình Container Trên Dòng Lệnh (CLI Lifecycle)
steps:
  - icon: upload
    badge: 1. Tải Image
    title: Pull
    code: docker pull redis:7-alpine
    tone: sky
    edge: tạo + bật
  - icon: play
    badge: 2. Chạy ngầm
    title: Run (Up)
    code: docker run -d --name cache
    tone: emerald
    edge: SIGTERM (10s)
  - icon: shield
    badge: 3. Dừng êm
    title: Stop (Exited)
    code: docker stop cache
    tone: amber
    edge: giải phóng tên
  - icon: trash
    badge: 4. Xóa bỏ
    title: Remove
    code: docker rm cache
    tone: rose
```

A huge practical advantage is that **your computer doesn't need Python 3.12, Node 22, or Redis pre-installed** — a single `docker run` line runs any language immediately in a clean, isolated environment:

```bash
# Chạy thử nhanh câu lệnh Python 3.12 ngay trong container rồi tự dọn sạch (--rm):
docker run --rm python:3.12-slim python -c "import sys; print('Hello from Python', sys.version.split()[0])"

# Hoặc chạy dịch vụ Redis / Node.js chạy ngầm lâu dài ở hậu cảnh (-d):
docker run -d --name cache-dev redis:7-alpine
```

```visual
kind: groups
title: Bảng Lệnh Điều Khiển Vòng Đời Hàng Ngày [!badge:emerald:Cheat Sheet]
columns: 2
items:
  - num: 1
    title: Tải & Chạy Container Mới
    badge: Pull & Run
    tone: emerald
    bullets:
      - "**`-d` (`--detach`):** Chạy ngầm ở hậu cảnh (background), trả lại dấu nhắc Terminal ngay"
      - "**`--name`:** Đặt tên cố định dễ nhớ (tránh tên ngẫu nhiên kiểu `sleepy_euler`)"
    code: |
      docker pull redis:7-alpine                # Tải các layer vào cache máy
      docker images                             # Xem danh sách Image đang có
      docker run -d --name cache-dev redis:7-alpine
    codeLang: shell
  - num: 2
    title: Quan Sát Trạng Thái Sống & Đã Tắt
    badge: Inspect Status
    tone: sky
    bullets:
      - "`docker ps` **chỉ hiện container ĐANG CHẠY** (`Up`)"
      - "Muốn thấy cả container **đã dừng (`Exited`)** bắt buộc thêm cờ ==`-a`=="
      - "`Exited (0)` = hoàn tất bình thường · `Exited (1)` / `(137)` = sập do lỗi code hoặc tràn RAM"
    code: |
      docker ps      # Chỉ hiện container đang chạy (running)
      docker ps -a   # Hiện TẤT CẢ (gồm cả Exited đã tắt)
    codeLang: shell
  - num: 3
    title: Dừng Lịch Sự (SIGTERM) vs Rút Phích (SIGKILL)
    badge: Graceful Shutdown
    tone: amber
    bullets:
      - "**`docker stop`** gửi ==`SIGTERM`== vào PID 1, cho FastAPI / Node.js tối đa 10 giây đóng kết nối DB êm ái trước khi thoát"
      - "**`docker kill`** bắn thẳng `SIGKILL` ngắt điện tức khắc — chỉ dùng khi tiến trình treo cứng"
    code: |
      docker stop cache-dev   # Gửi SIGTERM -> chờ 10s -> Graceful Shutdown
      docker kill cache-dev   # Bắn thẳng SIGKILL rút điện ngay lập tức
    codeLang: shell
  - num: 4
    title: Dọn Dẹp Container (Giữ Nguyên Image)
    badge: Cleanup
    tone: rose
    bullets:
      - "`docker rm` **chỉ xóa Container** (tiến trình và lớp ghi tạm), còn **Image gốc vẫn nằm nguyên** trong `docker images` để lần sau khởi tạo lại tức thì!"
      - "Thêm `-f` để vừa ép dừng vừa xóa gọn trong 1 lệnh ở máy dev"
    code: |
      docker rm cache-dev      # Xóa container đã dừng (giải phóng tên)
      docker rm -f cache-dev   # Ép dừng + xóa ngay lập tức
    codeLang: shell
```

steps.headingEn: Common Pitfalls & 2026 Immutable Infrastructure Mindset
steps.bodyEn:
```visual
kind: troubleshoot
title: Khắc Phục Nhanh Lỗi Kinh Điển Của Người Mới Học Container
items:
  - symptom: 'Conflict. The container name "/api" is already in use'
    badge: Bẫy số 1
    tone: amber
    cause: Container cũ bị lỗi thoát sau 0.1s nên không hiện trong `docker ps`, nhưng vỏ `Exited` của nó vẫn đang giữ tên `api`.
    fix: Liệt kê toàn bộ bằng `docker ps -a` để xem mã thoát, sau đó xóa bản cũ trước khi chạy lại.
    cmd: docker ps -a && docker rm -f api
  - symptom: Bản build hôm nay tự nhiên lỗi dù không sửa dòng code nào
    badge: Reproducibility
    tone: rose
    cause: Dùng `python:latest` hoặc `node:latest` khiến CI tự kéo phiên bản Major mới vừa phát hành trên Docker Hub.
    fix: Luôn ghim phiên bản cụ thể kèm biến thể gọn nhẹ (ví dụ `python:3.12-slim`, `node:22.12-alpine` hoặc `redis:7.4-alpine`).
```

> [!WARNING] Golden Rule of Immutable Infrastructure
> Never exec into a running container to run `pip install`, `npm install`, or manually edit code in Production — the next time the container is recreated from the base Image, all manual edits will vanish completely! To update code, always follow the proper cycle: **edit code → build a new Image (bump version tag) → replace the old container with the new container**.

> [!REMEMBER] Quick Pocket Summary (30-Second Recap)
> - **VM** = Boots a separate **Guest OS** (heavy, slow startup) · **Container** = Shares the **Host Linux Kernel**, starts in tens of milliseconds.
> - **Image** = **Read-only** packaging unit (`Read-only layers`) · **Container** = Live process + 1 thin writable layer (`docker rm` deletes the Container without deleting the Image!).
> - Omitting `:tag` = defaults to `:latest` · Node/Go favor **`-alpine`**, Python/FastAPI favor **`-slim`** · View stopped containers too with `docker ps -a`.

readings.noteEn: A hastily written Dockerfile very commonly seen in newly bootstrapped Node.js projects.
readings.taskEn: Read through the file and list at least 3 risks that make this build slow or dangerous on a server.
readings.answerEn: 1) Using the floating tag `FROM node:latest` without pinning a version can silently jump major versions and break the app; 2) Placing `COPY . .` before `RUN npm install` invalidates the layer cache on every 1-line code edit and skips `npm ci` which honors `package-lock.json`; 3) Running the process as default `root` and using the shell form of `CMD`, which swallows the `SIGTERM` signal.

readings.noteEn: Compare directly against a production-grade Node.js 22 Dockerfile built on Alpine Linux.
readings.taskEn: Compared to the flawed version above, what did this standard version change in the `FROM` line, the `COPY` order, and the final `CMD` instruction?
readings.answerEn: The standard version explicitly pins `FROM node:22-alpine`, moves `COPY package.json package-lock.json ./` ahead of `RUN npm ci --omit=dev` to preserve dependency caching, switches to the non-privileged `USER node`, and launches via JSON exec form `CMD ["node", "src/server.js"]`.

K00-Q1.qEn: Compared to the Node.js ecosystem, what does a **Container Image** most closely correspond to?
choicesEn: The actual running process in RAM when you type `node dist/server.js`
An immutable, read-only packaged blueprint (like a frozen snapshot bundling minimal OS + Node runtime + locked `node_modules`)
A VirtualBox VM with a full separate Guest OS Kernel installed
The `.env` environment variable file sitting on a developer's laptop
K00-Q1.explainEn: An Image is a read-only snapshot (read-only layers) freezing the entire environment and source code; a Container is the live process launched from that Image.

K00-Q2.qEn: Every Docker Container must boot its own separate Guest OS Kernel just like a traditional virtual machine, taking minutes to start up.
K00-Q2.explainEn: False! Containers on the same host share the Host Linux Kernel and use Namespaces + cgroups to isolate processes, so they start in tens of milliseconds.

K00-Q3.qEn: You just ran a container named `db-migrate` to create tables, and its process exited cleanly with code `0`. If you now run `docker ps` (with no extra flags), what happens?
choicesEn: The `db-migrate` container still appears in the list with status `Exited (0)`
`db-migrate` does not appear because `docker ps` only shows currently `running` containers by default
Docker automatically and permanently deletes every container as soon as its inner process finishes
The `docker ps` command throws a syntax error because the container name is missing
K00-Q3.explainEn: `docker ps` only lists running containers. To see stopped (`Exited`) containers like `db-migrate`, you must pass the `-a` flag (`docker ps -a`).

K00-Q4.qEn: What is the most important difference between `docker stop api` and `docker kill api` for an Express/Fastify server?
choicesEn: `docker stop` also deletes the Image from disk, whereas `docker kill` keeps the Image
`docker stop` sends `SIGTERM` so Node.js can gracefully close DB connections before a timeout, whereas `docker kill` immediately sends `SIGKILL` for abrupt termination
`docker kill` is safer because it waits for all in-flight HTTP requests to finish before shutting down
Both commands are completely identical at the OS signal level
K00-Q4.explainEn: `docker stop` sends `SIGTERM` first (waiting 10 seconds by default for the app to run Graceful Shutdown before falling back to `SIGKILL`), while `docker kill` sends `SIGKILL` immediately, which cannot be caught by `process.on`.

K00-Q5.qEn: When you run `docker rm hello-web` to remove the `hello-web` container, the underlying `nginx:1.27-alpine` Image on your machine is also deleted and must be re-downloaded from the Internet next time.
K00-Q5.explainEn: False! `docker rm` only deletes the Container instance (that process's temporary writable layer). The read-only layers of the `nginx:1.27-alpine` Image remain intact in your local cache (`docker images`).

K00-Q6.qEn: If you run the command below without specifying a tag after the colon `:`, what default tag name does Docker automatically append?
K00-Q6.explainEn: When `:tag` is omitted, Docker defaults to looking up `:latest` (`docker.io/library/node:latest`) — a habit to avoid in Production because versions can drift unexpectedly.

K00-Q7.qEn: A database migration script inside a container completes successfully with zero errors and stops on its own. In the `STATUS` column of `docker ps -a` (`Exited (N) 5 seconds ago`), what is the exit code `N`?
K00-Q7.explainEn: Following standard POSIX conventions and `process.exit(0)` in Node.js, exit code `0` indicates that the process completed its task successfully without errors.

K00-FC1.frontEn: What is the core difference between a **Container Image** and a **Container**?
K00-FC1.backEn: An **Image** is a read-only binary blueprint (read-only layers) stored on disk; a **Container** is a live process instantiated from that Image with a thin writable layer on top.

K00-FC2.frontEn: Why do Containers start hundreds of times faster than Virtual Machines (VMs)?
K00-FC2.backEn: Because Containers **directly share the Host OS Kernel** and only use Linux Namespaces + cgroups for process isolation, avoiding booting an entire separate Guest OS like a VM.

K00-FC3.frontEn: What problem does the `-d` (`--detach`) flag in `docker run -d` solve?
K00-FC3.backEn: It runs the container in the background and immediately returns terminal control instead of tying up your shell streaming output.

K00-FC4.frontEn: When must you use `docker ps -a` instead of `docker ps`?
K00-FC4.backEn: When you need to inspect **stopped (`Exited`)** containers that finished a task or crashed on startup (which are hidden from default `docker ps`).

K00-FC5.frontEn: Which OS signal does `docker stop` send to the PID 1 process first?
K00-FC5.backEn: **`SIGTERM`** (allowing a Node.js app to catch `process.on("SIGTERM")` and gracefully close DB connections before the grace period expires and `SIGKILL` is sent).

K00-FC6.frontEn: Why should you avoid `:latest` tags (e.g., `node:latest` or `python:latest`) in Production?
K00-FC6.backEn: Because `:latest` is a mutable tag that shifts over time — a future build can unexpectedly pull a new major version, breaking compatibility and destroying reproducibility.

K00-FC7.frontEn: What are the three popular OCI Container engines on developer machines in 2026?

kube-ex-k00-1.titleEn: Pull a Version-Pinned Image from the Registry
kube-ex-k00-1.promptEn: The current host only has the `alpine:3.20` image cached. Use `docker pull` to download the exact `redis:7-alpine` image into the local cache (avoid using `:latest`).
hintsEn: The syntax to pull an image with a specific tag is `docker pull <repository>:<tag>`.
Run exactly: `docker pull redis:7-alpine`

kube-ex-k00-2.titleEn: Run a Container in Detached Mode
kube-ex-k00-2.promptEn: Launch a background (`-d`) container named `hello-web` from the `nginx:1.27-alpine` image.
hintsEn: Place both `-d` (detached) and `--name hello-web` BEFORE the image name `nginx:1.27-alpine`.
Full command: `docker run -d --name hello-web nginx:1.27-alpine`

kube-ex-k00-3.titleEn: Find a Stopped Container Hidden from docker ps
kube-ex-k00-3.promptEn: A teammate says they just finished running a DB migration job named `old-migration`, but running `docker ps` only shows `api` running. Fix the command below to list **all** containers (including `exited` ones) so `old-migration` appears on screen.
hintsEn: `docker ps` hides `exited` containers by default.
Add the `-a` (or `--all`) flag: `docker ps -a`

kube-ex-k00-4.titleEn: Gracefully Stop a Running Container with SIGTERM
kube-ex-k00-4.promptEn: The background worker `legacy-worker` needs to be paused for maintenance while keeping the container around to inspect logs later. Use the graceful stop command (`docker stop`) on `legacy-worker` (do not remove the container).
hintsEn: Use `docker stop <container-name>` to transition status from `running` to `exited` with exit code `0`.
Run: `docker stop legacy-worker`

kube-ex-k00-5.titleEn: Clean Up an Exited Temporary Container
kube-ex-k00-5.promptEn: The seed-data container `temp-seed` has finished running and is currently in the `exited` state. Completely remove the `temp-seed` container to free up that name for the next run.
hintsEn: Since `temp-seed` is already `exited`, you only need to call `docker rm <name>`.
Run: `docker rm temp-seed`

K01.titleEn: Port Mapping, Environment Variables, Log Management & Container Exec
K01.summaryEn: Bind ports with -p HOST:CONTAINER, resolve port conflicts, inject config via -e like process.env, and diagnose issues using docker logs / exec.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
In `K00`, you successfully started `nginx:1.27-alpine` in the background (`Up`). Yet if you open a browser and visit `http://localhost:80`, you immediately hit **`ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`**! Why can't external requests reach a container that is clearly running?

Every container is created inside its own **isolated Network Namespace** with an independent internal IP address, completely cut off from external traffic by default. For traffic from your browser or an external client to reach the app inside, you must map a host port to the exact port the container is listening on.

```visual

footer: "Hai container khác nhau có thể cùng mở cổng 3000 (hoặc 8000) ở bên trong, miễn là Host Port bên trái khác nhau (-p 3001:3000 và -p 3002:3000)"
```

steps.bodyEn:

Always read the ==`-p HOST_PORT:CONTAINER_PORT`== (`--publish`) flag in the direction the packet travels **from outside the host into the container**:

```bash
# Mở cổng 8080 trên máy bạn (trái) -> nối dây vào cổng 80 của Nginx bên trong container (phải)
docker run -d --name shop-nginx -p 8080:80 nginx:1.27-alpine

# Mở http://localhost:9090 ngoài trình duyệt -> vẫn nối vào cổng 80 nội bộ của container thứ hai!
docker run -d --name web-ui -p 9090:80 nginx:1.27-alpine
```

- [>] **Left of `:` (`8080` or `9090`) — *Host Port*:** The listening port on the host machine (`http://localhost:8080`). On the same machine, **no two processes can occupy the same Host Port** simultaneously.
- [>] **Right of `:` (`80`, `3000`, or `8000`) — *Container Port*:** The actual port opened by the Python/Node server inside (`--port 8000` or `app.listen(3000)`). Because each container has its own Network Namespace, 10 containers can all open port `3000` or `8000` on the right side without conflict!

> [!WARNING] Common Connection Bug: Listening on `127.0.0.1` Instead of `0.0.0.0`
> Many developers run `uvicorn main:app` (Python FastAPI) or `vite dev` / `fastify` (Node.js) with the right `-p 8000:8000` syntax, yet browser requests still get refused. The culprit is which network interface the server binds to inside the container:
> - Inside a container's Network Namespace, there are **2 network interfaces**: the internal loopback **`127.0.0.1` (`localhost`)** and the virtual network adapter **`eth0`** connected to the Docker bridge.
> - If the server binds only to **`127.0.0.1`**, it only accepts connections originating from inside that same container — any packet forwarded through `-p` from the host arrives via `eth0` and gets rejected.
> - Configuring ==`0.0.0.0`== (listening on all available interfaces inside the container) opens `eth0` to receive forwarded `-p` traffic (think of `127.0.0.1` as an intercom inside a room, while `0.0.0.0` opens the front door to the hallway).

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Lỗi Thường Gặp Ở Python (Uvicorn/Flask) & Node.js (Fastify/Vite): 127.0.0.1 vs 0.0.0.0"
subtitle: "Tại sao đã truyền đúng -p 8000:8000 (hoặc 3000:3000) mà trình duyệt bên ngoài vẫn báo lỗi từ chối kết nối?"
left:
  badge: "CÁCH SAI · Chỉ nghe trên loopback"
  title: "Mặc định chỉ nghe trên 127.0.0.1"
  tone: rose
  code: |
    # Python Uvicorn mặc định bind 127.0.0.1!
    uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000

    # Hoặc Node.js Fastify / Vite mặc định:
    app.listen({ port: 3000, host: "127.0.0.1" });
  lang: shell
  bullets:
    - "`127.0.0.1` bên trong container **chỉ nhận gói tin sinh ra từ chính bên trong container đó**"
    - "Gói tin từ trình duyệt máy chủ đi qua cầu `-p` bước vào qua **`eth0`** nên bị chặn (`Empty reply` / `Connection reset`)!"
right:
  badge: "CÁCH CHUẨN · Lắng nghe trên mọi giao diện"
  title: "Bắt buộc lắng nghe trên 0.0.0.0"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    # Python FastAPI / Uvicorn chuẩn Container:
    uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

    # Node.js Express / Fastify chuẩn Container:
    app.listen({ port: 3000, host: "0.0.0.0" });
  lang: shell
  bullets:
    - "**`0.0.0.0`** cho phép HTTP server đón nhận kết nối từ mọi giao diện mạng bên trong container (bao gồm card mạng ảo `eth0`)"
    - "Tương tự với Flask (`--host=0.0.0.0`), Django (`0.0.0.0:8000`) hay Vite (`--host 0.0.0.0`)"
```

steps.headingEn: Injecting Dynamic Config via -e (os.environ & process.env)
steps.bodyEn:
> [!NOTE] 12-Factor App Philosophy — One Image Across All Environments
> You never want to hardcode a `localhost` Database URL inside an Image only to rebuild code when deploying to Staging! A proper Container Image stays identical and immutable across **Dev → Staging → Production**, while environment-specific settings (Database URL, log level, port) are injected at runtime via **environment variables (`-e`)**.

When you pass `-e` (`--env`), Docker injects `KEY=VALUE` pairs directly into the Linux process's environment table:

```bash
docker run -d --name order-api \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  -e NODE_ENV=production \
  -e LOG_LEVEL=info \
  -e PORT=3000 \
  node:22-alpine
```

- [x] **Read naturally in any language:** In **Python**, read via `os.environ["LOG_LEVEL"]` (or `pydantic-settings`); in **Node.js**, read via `process.env.LOG_LEVEL` — zero need to bake sensitive `.env` files into the Image!
- [x] **Keep local runs tidy:** When testing locally with 15 config variables, group them into an external file and load it once with `--env-file .env.local`.

steps.headingEn: Streaming stdout/stderr Logs with docker logs
steps.bodyEn:
In the container world, apps **do not write silently to a `logs/app.log` file on the internal writable layer** (because deleting the container wipes the error history, or log files grow unchecked and fill up server disk). Instead:

- [>] Print straight to standard streams: `logging.StreamHandler()` / `print(..., flush=True)` in Python or `console.log` / `pino` in Node.js → Docker Engine automatically captures all **`stdout`** and **`stderr`** output.
- [!] **Essential diagnostic tool when a container crashes immediately:** ==`docker logs` still reads the full error history even after a container has crashed (`Exited (1)`)==, as long as you haven't deleted it with `docker rm`!

```bash
docker logs payment-worker                # In toàn bộ lịch sử stdout/stderr từ lúc khởi chạy
docker logs -f --tail 50 payment-worker   # Xem trực tiếp (-f follow) 50 dòng mới nhất theo thời gian thực
```

> [!TIP] Quick Tip for Python Developers Reading `docker logs`
> By default, Python buffers output when not attached to an interactive TTY, causing `print()` lines to appear seconds late in `docker logs -f`. Setting `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1` when containerizing Python ensures every log line flushes immediately in real time!

steps.headingEn: Inspecting Inside a Running Container with docker exec
steps.bodyEn:
When you need to quickly check which user a process runs under, verify injected environment variables, or test network connectivity from inside, use ==`docker exec`==:

```bash
# Chạy 1 lệnh đơn lẻ rồi thoát ngay (KHÔNG cần -it, dùng rất gọn trong script CI/CD):
docker exec shop-api ps         # Kiểm tra PID 1, cột USER và COMMAND thực tế
docker exec shop-api printenv   # Liệt kê toàn bộ biến môi trường đang nạp
docker exec shop-api whoami     # Xem container đang chạy dưới tài khoản nào

# Mở phiên shell tương tác bên trong container tối giản (luôn ưu tiên "sh" thay vì "bash"):
docker exec -it shop-api sh
```

- **`-i` (`--interactive`):** Keeps keyboard `stdin` open so it receives every keystroke you type.
- **`-t` (`--tty`):** Allocates a pseudo-TTY terminal for a clean `/app $` prompt.

```visual
kind: groups
title: "Bộ Lệnh Giao Tiếp & Kiểm Tra Container [!badge:emerald:Cheat Sheet]"
columns: 2

      - "Bước kiểm tra đầu tiên luôn là đọc `stderr` lưu lại trước lúc thoát bằng `docker logs`"
    code: |
      docker ps -a              # Xem mã lỗi Exited (1)
      docker logs shop-api      # Đọc Traceback Python / Stack trace Node

      - "Hoạt động trên **cả container đang `Up` lẫn container đã `Exited`**"
    code: |
      docker inspect shop-api
    codeLang: shell
  - num: 3
    icon: terminal

    badge: Dùng docker exec
```

steps.headingEn: Common Pitfalls & 2026 Operational Best Practices
steps.bodyEn:
```visual
kind: troubleshoot
title: Ba Sự Cố Thực Tế Khi Vận Hành Cổng, Shell & Mật Khẩu
items:
  - symptom: 'Bind for 0.0.0.0:8080 failed: port is already allocated'
    badge: Trùng Host Port
    tone: amber
    cause: Cổng bên trái (`8080`) trên máy chủ đang bị một container cũ (`old-proxy`) hoặc tiến trình local khác chiếm giữ.
    fix: Kiểm tra bằng `docker ps`, xóa container cũ đang giữ cổng hoặc đổi vế trái sang cổng trống khác (`-p 8081:80`).
    cmd: docker ps && docker rm -f old-proxy
  - symptom: 'OCI runtime exec failed: executable file not found in $PATH ("bash")'
    badge: Image Alpine / Slim
    tone: sky
    cause: Các image tối giản hiện đại (`node:22-alpine`, `nginx:1.27-alpine`, `redis:7-alpine`) chỉ cài sẵn `/bin/sh`, không cài `bash`.
    fix: Đổi thói quen từ `bash` sang gọi `sh` khi mở shell tương tác trên nền tối giản.
    cmd: docker exec -it shop-api sh
  - symptom: Lộ mật khẩu DB trong lịch sử dòng lệnh (.zsh_history)
    badge: Bảo mật Secret
    tone: rose
    cause: Truyền trực tiếp mật khẩu nhạy cảm dạng rõ qua `-e DB_PASS=...` trên máy chủ dùng chung.
    fix: Chỉ dùng `-e` cho cấu hình không nhạy cảm hoặc máy dev; lên Production bắt buộc dùng Docker Compose Secrets hoặc Kubernetes Secrets.
```

> [!REMEMBER] Quick Pocket Summary
> - Always read **`-p HOST_PORT:CONTAINER_PORT`** (outside host before `:` → inside container after `:`), and ensure your Python/Node server binds to **`0.0.0.0`**.
> - Variables passed via **`-e KEY=VALUE`** populate `os.environ` / `process.env` directly · Logs written to `stdout`/`stderr` are read via **`docker logs`** even after `Exited`.
> - **`docker exec`** only works on `Up` containers (remember to use `sh` instead of `bash` on Alpine images)!

readings.noteEn: Understand deeply why each container has its own network namespace rather than sharing localhost with the host.
readings.taskEn: Read the `DATABASE_URL` config of the `api` service and explain why connecting to `localhost:5432` fails with `ECONNREFUSED`.
readings.answerEn: Every container has its own isolated `127.0.0.1` (`localhost`) loopback interface. From inside the `api` container, `localhost:5432` points back to `api` itself (where only Node.js listens on port 3000), not to the host machine or the `postgres` container.

readings.noteEn: Contrast runtime config injection (`docker run -e`) with the risk of baking secrets at Image build time.
readings.taskEn: Why must secrets never be baked statically into an Image, and instead be injected at runtime or via Secret Mounts?
readings.answerEn: Anything placed in `ARG` or `ENV` during build is permanently stored in the Image's metadata/history (`docker history --no-trunc`). Moving sensitive variables to runtime (`-e` / `--env-file` / K8s Secret) allows safely reusing a single Image across Dev, Staging, and Production.

K01-Q1.qEn: In `docker run -d -p 8080:3000 shop-api:1.0.0`, what does the pair `8080:3000` mean?
choicesEn: The app inside the container must listen on port `8080`, while external users connect to `localhost:3000`
Expose port `8080` on the Host and forward traffic to port `3000` where the app is listening inside the Container
Open the entire port range from `3000` through `8080` for the container
Limit traffic to `8080` connections within `3000` seconds
K01-Q1.explainEn: The rule is always `-p HOST_PORT:CONTAINER_PORT`: external clients hit port `8080` on the host, and Docker forwards packets to port `3000` inside the container.

K01-Q2.qEn: Inside a container, a Fastify app calls `app.listen({ port: 3000, host: "127.0.0.1" })`. Even though it was started with `docker run -p 3000:3000`, requests from the host browser fail. Why?
choicesEn: Because Fastify is incompatible with Docker Engine v27
Because binding to `127.0.0.1` inside a container only accepts connections originating inside that container; to accept `-p` bridged traffic, the server must bind to `0.0.0.0`
Because port `3000` is a privileged Linux OS port
Because the `-it` flag was omitted when starting the container
K01-Q2.explainEn: Traffic forwarded from the Host enters through the container's virtual `eth0` interface, not internal `127.0.0.1` loopback. Therefore the server inside must bind to `0.0.0.0`.

K01-Q3.qEn: If a container fails due to a missing environment variable and exits (`Exited (1)`), you can still run `docker logs <container-name>` to read the error message it printed to `stderr` before crashing.
K01-Q3.explainEn: True! As long as you haven't removed the container with `docker rm`, Docker preserves its full `stdout`/`stderr` output for `docker logs`.

K01-Q4.qEn: When the `worker` container is in `Exited (1)` state, what happens if you run `docker exec -it worker sh` to inspect it?
choicesEn: Docker automatically restarts `worker` and opens a shell prompt
The command errors because `docker exec` can only spawn a secondary process inside a **running** container
Docker opens a shell directly inside `worker`'s base Image
The command wipes all old logs from `worker`
K01-Q4.explainEn: `docker exec` injects a new process into an active container's Namespaces. When a container is `Exited`, those namespaces are not running, so you must use `docker logs` or `docker inspect` instead.

K01-Q5.qEn: When starting a container with `docker run -d -e NODE_ENV=production -e PORT=4000 app:1.0`, what is the most natural way for Node.js code inside to read these two values?
choicesEn: Read directly from `process.env.NODE_ENV` and `process.env.PORT`
You must install the `dotenv` package and call `fs.readFileSync(".env")`
Query the internal Docker socket API at `/var/run/docker.sock`
Pass them via command-line arguments `process.argv[2]`
K01-Q5.explainEn: Docker injects `-e` `KEY=VALUE` pairs straight into the Linux process environment table, making them immediately available on `process.env` in Node.js.

K01-Q6.qEn: The `web-ui` container is started with the command below (Nginx inside listens on port `80`). In your local web browser, which port `http://localhost:____` should you visit?
K01-Q6.explainEn: The number before the colon (`9090`) is the Host Port exposed on your machine; the number after (`80`) is the internal port inside the container.

K01-Q7.qEn: Two different containers running simultaneously on the same host can both listen on port `3000` inside their respective containers, provided their left-side Host Ports differ (e.g., `-p 3001:3000` and `-p 3002:3000`).
K01-Q7.explainEn: True! Each container has its own Network Namespace so internal port `3000` never collides; only the shared Host Port (`3001` vs `3002`) must be unique.

K01-FC1.frontEn: How should you read the order of the two numbers in `-p 8080:3000`?
K01-FC1.backEn: **`HOST_PORT:CONTAINER_PORT`** — external host port `8080` forwards traffic to port `3000` where the app listens inside the container.

K01-FC2.frontEn: Why must a Node.js server inside Docker listen on `0.0.0.0` instead of `127.0.0.1`?
K01-FC2.backEn: Because `127.0.0.1` inside a container only accepts connections from within that same container; `-p` forwarded traffic enters via the virtual `eth0` interface, requiring `0.0.0.0`.

K01-FC3.frontEn: What does the error `Bind for 0.0.0.0:8080 failed: port is already allocated` mean?
K01-FC3.backEn: Port `8080` on the host machine is already occupied by another running container (or a host process).

K01-FC4.frontEn: Which `docker run` flag injects environment variables into Node.js `process.env`?
K01-FC4.backEn: The **`-e KEY=VALUE`** flag (or `--env KEY=VALUE`, or `--env-file` for a whole file).

K01-FC5.frontEn: When a container crashes right on startup (`Exited (1)`), should you use `docker exec` or `docker logs` to find the cause?
K01-FC5.backEn: Use **`docker logs <name>`** (because `docker exec` only works while the container is `running`).

K01-FC6.frontEn: On Alpine-based images (`node:22-alpine`), should `docker exec -it` invoke `sh` or `bash` for an interactive shell?
K01-FC6.backEn: Invoke **`sh`** (`docker exec -it <name> sh`), because minimal Alpine Linux does not include `bash` by default.

kube-ex-k01-1.titleEn: Publish a Host Port to an Nginx Container
kube-ex-k01-1.promptEn: Launch a detached (`-d`) container named `shop-nginx` from the `nginx:1.27-alpine` image, exposing host port `8080` mapped to container port `80`.
hintsEn: The port mapping syntax is `-p HOST_PORT:CONTAINER_PORT`, i.e. `-p 8080:80`.
Full command: `docker run -d --name shop-nginx -p 8080:80 nginx:1.27-alpine`

kube-ex-k01-2.titleEn: Resolve a Port Conflict (port is already allocated)
kube-ex-k01-2.promptEn: The starter command below tries to launch `new-proxy` (`nginx:1.27-alpine`) on `8080:80`, but running it as-is fails with `port is already allocated` because an older container `old-proxy` already holds port `8080`. Remove (or stop) `old-proxy` first, then start `new-proxy` on `8080:80`.

K02.titleEn: Linux Namespaces, cgroups (OOM 137), Bridge Networks & Named Volumes
K02.summaryEn: Understand the two Linux Kernel pillars Namespaces & cgroups, decode Exit Code 137, create Bridge Networks with automatic DNS, and persist DB data using Named Volumes.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
A container is neither a virtual machine nor a separate hardware virtualization layer; under the hood, it relies on **two built-in Linux Kernel mechanisms**: ==Linux Namespaces== (isolating what a process can see) and ==Control Groups (`cgroups`)== (capping RAM/CPU consumption). Understanding these two fundamentals before using CLI flags will also make **Kubernetes** Pod internals click effortlessly later.

```visual

    tone: emerald
```

steps.headingEn: Container Isolation Mechanics: Linux Namespaces (Visibility) & cgroups (Resource Limits)
steps.bodyEn:
> [!NOTE] The Two Linux Kernel Pillars Powering Containers
> - **Linux Namespaces (Visibility Isolation):** The kernel gives each process isolated views of process lists (`PID`), network interfaces (`NET`), filesystem mounts (`MNT`), and hostnames (`UTS`). As a result, the app inside only sees its own assigned resources (`PID 1`, `eth0`, `/`) and cannot see processes on the host or in other containers.
> - **Control Groups — `cgroups` (Hardware Limits):** While Namespaces isolate visibility, `cgroups` enforce hard physical limits (RAM, CPU, I/O) per container, preventing a memory-leaking process from exhausting host resources and taking down the entire server.
> - Put simply: `Namespaces` are the walls separating apartments in a building, while `cgroups` are the dedicated circuit breakers and water meters installed for each unit.

steps.headingEn: Why Running Out of RAM Produces Exit Code 137 (OOMKilled)
steps.bodyEn:
> [!WARNING] `docker run` Default: Unlimited RAM
> When you run `docker run` **without `--memory`**, the container has **NO RAM limit (`no limit`)**! A Python worker accidentally loading a 10GB Pandas dataframe into RAM or a leaking Node.js reporting API can consume all server RAM, crashing the Database and even SSH access!

What happens when you set `--memory=512m` and the app tries to allocate past `512 MB`? Unlike **CPU** (exceeding `--cpus` only slows execution via *CPU Throttling* without killing the process), **RAM is an incompressible resource**. The instant memory hits the ceiling:
1. The Linux kernel's **OOM Killer** (*Out-Of-Memory Killer*) immediately terminates the process with a forced **`SIGKILL` (signal `9`)**.
2. By standard Unix/POSIX convention, when a process is killed by signal `N`, its exit code is `128 + N`. With `N = 9`, we get the most famous number in DevOps: ==`128 + 9 = Exit Code 137 (OOMKilled)`==!

```visual
kind: flow
title: "Cơ Chế Xảy Ra Sự Cố OOMKilled & Công Thức POSIX Tạo Ra Exit Code 137"
subtitle: "Chuyện gì xảy ra ở cấp độ nhân Linux ngay khoảnh khắc tiến trình vượt quá hạn mức --memory?"
footer: "Công thức chuẩn POSIX khi tiến trình chết bởi tín hiệu N: Exit Code = 128 + N -> 128 + 9 (SIGKILL) = 137!"
steps:
  - icon: flame
    badge: Bước 1 · Vượt hạn mức
    title: Tràn Bộ Nhớ RAM
    desc: Tiến trình Python / Node.js xin cấp phát RAM vượt quá trần cgroup (> 512m)
    code: "> 512m limit"
    tone: amber
    edge: cgroup từ chối
  - icon: shield-alert
    badge: Bước 2 · Nhân can thiệp
    title: Kernel OOM Killer
    desc: Linux Out-Of-Memory Killer lập tức ngắt tiến trình để bảo vệ máy chủ vật lý
    code: OOM Killer
    tone: rose
    edge: bắn tín hiệu số 9
  - icon: zap
    badge: Bước 3 · Tín hiệu cưỡng bức
    title: SIGKILL (Signal 9)
    desc: Ngắt điện tiến trình tức khắc, không thể try/catch hay trì hoãn trong code
    code: "SIGKILL = 9"
    tone: cyan
    edge: "128 + 9"
  - icon: alert
    badge: Bước 4 · Dấu vết để lại
    title: Exited (137)
    desc: Hiện rõ trong docker ps -a (hoặc K8s OOMKilled) báo hiệu chết do vượt trần RAM!
    code: "Exit Code 137"
    tone: rose
```

How to safely enforce a RAM ceiling via `cgroups` in practice:

```bash
# Khóa cứng trần RAM 512MB (với Node.js, đặt thêm V8 Heap ~75% trần để GC dọn rác kịp thời)
docker run -d --name worker-safe \
  --memory=512m \
  -e NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=384" \
  node:22-alpine
```

> [!TIP] Preventing `Exit 137` in Both Node.js and Python / AI Workloads
> - **For Node.js:** The V8 engine often inspects the host's large total RAM (e.g., 16GB) and delays garbage collection. When setting `--memory=512m`, pair it with `NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=384"` (~75% of the limit) to force GC before hitting the cgroup wall!
> - **For Python (`FastAPI` / `Gunicorn` / `Pandas`):** Every worker process duplicates its own memory footprint in RAM (e.g., `--workers 4` loading a 300MB ML model each = 1.2GB!). In Containers & Kubernetes, keep fewer workers per container (1–2 workers) and scale out by running more container replicas instead!

In `compose.yaml` (Docker Compose v2), declare these resource caps cleanly under `deploy.resources.limits`:

```yaml
services:
  api:
    image: node:22-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "0.50"    # Giới hạn tối đa 50% của 1 nhân CPU (vượt chỉ chậm, không chết)
          memory: 256M    # Giới hạn RAM cứng 256MB qua cgroups v2 (vượt -> Exit 137)
```

steps.headingEn: User-Defined Bridge Networks & Automatic DNS Discovery
steps.bodyEn:
Many engineers wonder why we shouldn't just leave containers on the default `bridge` network created when Docker installs. The answer comes down to **automatic DNS name resolution**:

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Mạng bridge Mặc Định vs Mạng User-Defined Bridge Tự Tạo"
subtitle: "Chỉ mất 1 lệnh docker network create nhưng giải phóng bạn khỏi cơn ác mộng nhớ địa chỉ IP động!"
left:
  badge: "HẠN CHẾ LỊCH SỬ · Default bridge"
  title: "Không gọi được nhau bằng tên Container"
  tone: rose
  code: |
    # Nằm trên mạng bridge mặc định:
    # KHÔNG THỂ gọi redis://redis-session:6379!
    # Phải mò IP nội bộ 172.17.0.3 (đổi liên tục khi bật lại)
    docker run -d --name redis-session redis:7-alpine
  lang: shell
  bullets:
    - "Các container trên mạng `bridge` mặc định **không tự phân giải được tên của nhau**"
    - "Mọi dự án trên cùng máy bị gom chung một rổ mạng, thiếu tính cô lập"
right:
  badge: "CHUẨN THỰC CHIẾN · User-Defined Bridge"
  title: "Bật sẵn Embedded DNS tự động"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    docker network create shop-net

    docker run -d --name redis-session --network shop-net redis:7-alpine
    docker run -d --name shop-api --network shop-net \
      -e REDIS_URL=redis://redis-session:6379 \
      shop-api:1.0.0

  bullets:
    - "Docker tự động nhúng **Embedded DNS** vào mạng riêng `shop-net`"
    - "Từ trong `shop-api`, tên ==`redis-session`== tự động phân giải thẳng ra IP hiện tại của container Redis!"
```

steps.headingEn: Persisting Data: Named Volumes vs Bind Mounts
steps.bodyEn:
The temporary *writable layer* atop each container is tied strictly to that container's lifespan: the moment you run `docker rm shop-db` to upgrade PostgreSQL from `16.2` to `16.4`, all customer records stored in the writable layer **vanish permanently**! To decouple persistent data from the container's ephemeral layer, choose the right storage mechanism:

```visual
kind: groups
title: "So Sánh 3 Cơ Chế Lưu Trữ Trong Docker [!badge:sky:Storage Guide]"
columns: 3
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: layers
    title: Writable Layer (Mặc định)
    badge: Tạm bợ · Mất khi xóa
    tone: slate
    bullets:
      - "Lớp mỏng nằm trên cùng mỗi container"
      - "**Bốc hơi sạch 100%** ngay khi gõ `docker rm`"
      - "Chỉ hợp chứa tệp nháp tạm thời không quan trọng"
    footer: Tuyệt đối cấm lưu Database tại đây!
  - num: 2
    icon: database
    title: Named Volume (Khuyên dùng)
    badge: Chuẩn Database bền vững
    tone: emerald
    bullets:
      - "Do **Docker Engine** tự quản lý ở vùng tối ưu (`/var/lib/docker/volumes/...`)"
      - "Hiệu năng đọc/ghi cực nhanh (kể cả trên macOS/Windows)"
      - "==Bền vững qua các lần `docker rm -f`== — chỉ xóa khi gọi rõ `docker volume rm` hoặc `compose down -v`"
    footer: Lựa chọn số 1 cho PostgreSQL, Redis, MinIO
  - num: 3
    icon: folder-git
    title: Bind Mount (Gắn thư mục Host)
    badge: Cẩn thận bẫy che khuất!
    tone: amber
    bullets:
      - "Ánh xạ thẳng một đường dẫn cụ thể trên máy chủ vào container (`./src:/app/src`)"
      - "Chậm trên Mac/Windows nếu đồng bộ hàng vạn tệp nhỏ"
      - "**Bẫy kinh điển:** `-v $(pwd):/app` sẽ **che khuất hoàn toàn `/app/node_modules` hoặc `/app/.venv`** đã cài sẵn trong Image!"
    footer: Nên ưu tiên compose watch thay cho mount cả /app
```

How to create and attach a proper **Named Volume** for PostgreSQL 16:

```bash
# 1. Tạo ổ đĩa định danh độc lập với vòng đời container
docker volume create pg-data

# 2. Gắn pg-data vào đúng đường dẫn lưu dữ liệu của PostgreSQL
docker run -d --name shop-db \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=dev-only-placeholder \
  -v pg-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data \
  postgres:16-alpine
```

From this point on, even if you run `docker rm -f shop-db` and launch a newer Postgres container attached back to ==`-v pg-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data`==, every table and transaction remains 100% intact!

> [!REMEMBER] Quick Pocket Summary
> - **Namespaces** = Visibility isolation (`PID`, `NET`, `MNT`) · **`cgroups`** = Resource limits (`--memory`, `--cpus`).
> - By default containers have no RAM cap; exceeding `--memory` triggers Kernel `SIGKILL (9)` → **`Exited (137)`** (`128 + 9`).
> - Always create a **User-Defined Bridge** (`docker network create`) for automatic container-name DNS, and use **Named Volumes** to preserve Database data across `docker rm` cycles.

readings.noteEn: Configuration sample locking down CPU/RAM limits and restart policy for a Node.js service.
readings.taskEn: Look at `api`'s `command` line and `limits.memory: 256M`. Why did the engineer set `--max-old-space-size=192` lower than `256M`?
readings.answerEn: Node.js V8 Heap is only part of the process's total RAM (which also includes Stack, C++ Buffers, and executable code). Capping V8 Heap at `192MB` forces the Garbage Collector to clean up aggressively BEFORE total process RAM hits the `256MB` ceiling and gets killed abruptly by the Linux OOM Killer (`Exit Code 137`).

readings.noteEn: Two real-world data disasters: wiping Postgres tables after compose down and losing node_modules due to a Bind Mount.
readings.taskEn: Explain why mounting `- .:/app` from the host machine can cause the containerized app to crash with `Cannot find module 'express'`.
readings.answerEn: The bind mount `- .:/app` overlays the host's current directory directly on top of `/app` inside the container, completely masking `/app/node_modules` installed during `docker build`. If the host hasn't run `npm install` (or contains OS-incompatible binaries), the app won't find its dependencies.

K02-Q1.qEn: In Linux Container architecture, how do **Namespaces** and **cgroups** divide responsibilities?
choicesEn: Namespaces encrypt network passwords, while cgroups compress Image size
Namespaces isolate visibility (PIDs, network, root filesystem), while cgroups meter and cap hardware resource usage (CPU, RAM)
cgroups assign container IP addresses, while Namespaces limit disk capacity
Both only exist in Kubernetes and are not used by Docker
K02-Q1.explainEn: Namespaces control what a process can *see* (scope isolation), while Control Groups (`cgroups`) control the *maximum* CPU/RAM/IO it can consume.

K02-Q2.qEn: A data-processing container exceeds its `--memory` cap and is terminated by the Linux Kernel with `SIGKILL` (`9`). What `Exit Code` appears in `docker ps -a`?
K02-Q2.explainEn: By POSIX convention: `128 + 9 (SIGKILL) = 137` — the classic exit code indicating Out-Of-Memory (`OOMKilled`) or forced immediate termination.

K02-Q3.qEn: Why should we create a custom network (`docker network create shop-net`) instead of leaving containers on the default `bridge` network?
choicesEn: Because the default `bridge` network does not support publishing `-p` ports to the host
Because a user-defined bridge includes built-in automatic DNS so containers can call each other directly by **container name** (e.g., `redis-session:6379`) instead of ephemeral IP addresses
Because the default `bridge` network automatically deletes containers after 1 hour
Because only custom networks can run Alpine Linux
K02-Q3.explainEn: User-defined bridge networks provide Embedded DNS for automatic container/service name resolution and isolate one project's services from another on the same host.

K02-Q4.qEn: If you store PostgreSQL data in a **Named Volume** (`-v pg-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data`), then even if you remove the container with `docker rm -f shop-db`, the data in `pg-data` stays safely preserved on the host.
K02-Q4.explainEn: True! Named Volumes have an independent lifecycle from containers; they are only deleted when you explicitly run `docker volume rm pg-data` or `docker compose down -v`.

K02-Q5.qEn: What happens if on a Mac you just ran `git clone` (without running `npm install` on the host) and start the container with a Bind Mount `-v $(pwd):/app` over the Image's `/app` directory?
choicesEn: Docker automatically merges the host's `/app` and the Image's `/app` directories
The host directory completely shadows `/app` inside the container (hiding `/app/node_modules` pre-installed in the Image), causing Node.js to throw `Cannot find module`
The container automatically runs `npm ci` from scratch every millisecond
Nothing happens because `node_modules` lives in RAM
K02-Q5.explainEn: In Linux mounts, mounting a host directory onto `/app` obscures everything previously at `/app` in the Image — the single most common Bind Mount pitfall.

K02-Q6.qEn: When setting a Node.js container's RAM limit to `--memory=512m`, which environment variable helps V8 proactively run Garbage Collection before the Kernel OOM Killer terminates it at 512MB?
choicesEn: `NODE_ENV=development`
`NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=384"`
`NPM_CONFIG_LOGLEVEL=silent`
`PORT=512`
K02-Q6.explainEn: Setting `--max-old-space-size` to roughly 70%–75% of the container memory cap leaves room for Stack/Buffers and forces V8 GC to run before breaching the cgroup limit.

K02-Q7.qEn: By default, when running `docker run` without `--memory`, Docker automatically locks every container to a maximum of `128MB` RAM.
K02-Q7.explainEn: False! By default, containers have no hard RAM limit (`no limit`) and can consume all available host memory if a memory leak occurs.

K02-FC1.frontEn: What are the two Linux Kernel mechanisms behind Containers and their roles?
K02-FC1.backEn:
- **Namespaces:** Isolate visibility (PID, Network, Mount, User).
- **cgroups (Control Groups):** Meter and cap hardware resources (CPU, RAM, I/O).

K02-FC2.frontEn: What does a container's **`Exit Code 137`** mean and how is it calculated?
K02-FC2.backEn: `128 + 9 (SIGKILL) = 137`: The process was forcibly killed, most commonly by the **Linux OOM Killer** after exceeding its `--memory` cap (`OOMKilled`).

K02-FC3.frontEn: What is the biggest advantage of a user-defined network (`docker network create`) over the default `bridge` network?
K02-FC3.backEn: It provides **automatic internal DNS**, letting containers reach each other by **container name** instead of changing IP addresses.

K02-FC4.frontEn: When should you choose a **Named Volume** instead of a **Bind Mount**?
K02-FC4.backEn: Choose a **Named Volume** for persistent data needing high I/O performance and host-directory independence, such as **PostgreSQL, MySQL, and Redis**.

K02-FC5.frontEn: In `compose.yaml`, under which key path are a service's RAM and CPU limits declared?

K02-FC6.frontEn: Why does attaching a Bind Mount `- .:/app` easily break a Node.js app inside a container?
K02-FC6.backEn: Because the host directory shadows `/app/node_modules` built for Linux inside the Image (or injects binaries compiled for macOS/Windows into Linux).

kube-ex-k02-1.titleEn: Cap Container RAM Usage with cgroups
kube-ex-k02-1.promptEn: To prevent a memory-leaking background worker from freezing the entire server, run a detached (`-d`) container named `worker-safe` from `node:22-alpine` with a hard RAM limit of `256m` (`--memory=256m`).
hintsEn: Pass `--memory=256m` (or `-m 256m`) before the image name `node:22-alpine`.
Full command: `docker run -d --name worker-safe --memory=256m node:22-alpine`

kube-ex-k02-2.titleEn: Recover a Container Killed by OOM (Exit Code 137)
kube-ex-k02-2.promptEn: The reporting container `report-gen` (`node:22-alpine`) just crashed with exit code `Exited (137)` because someone configured its RAM cap way too low (`16m`). Remove the failed `report-gen` container and relaunch a new detached (`-d`) container with the same name `report-gen` from `node:22-alpine` using a sensible `--memory=512m` limit.
hintsEn: The old `exited` container still holds the name `report-gen`, so run `docker rm report-gen` before recreating it.
After removing it, run: `docker run -d --name report-gen --memory=512m node:22-alpine`

kube-ex-k02-3.titleEn: Create a Custom Bridge Network with Automatic DNS

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
While `docker run` lets you pull ready-made community images like Nginx, Redis, or PostgreSQL, a **`Dockerfile`** is where you write your own **"automated recipe"** to turn your **Node.js (`Express`, `NestJS`)** or **Python (`FastAPI`, `Django`)** source code into an **immutable Container Image** that runs identically from your laptop to Kubernetes.

> [!NOTE] Layering Mechanism in a Dockerfile
> A `Dockerfile` is a declarative script that builds an application runtime environment step by step from an existing Base Image: each uppercase instruction line (`FROM`, `WORKDIR`, `COPY`, `RUN`, `CMD`) creates **a deterministic read-only layer** stacked on top of the image filesystem. This exact same rule applies whether you write in Node.js, Python, or Go.

```visual

title: Hành Trình Đóng Gói Ứng Dụng Từ Mã Nguồn Thành Image Chuẩn OCI

  - icon: folder-git
    badge: Thư mục dự án
    title: Build Context (.)
    desc: Mã nguồn + tệp lockfile (package-lock.json / uv.lock) + Dockerfile gửi sang BuildKit
    code: "."
    tone: sky
    edge: FROM -> WORKDIR
  - icon: layers
    badge: Build-time
    title: Lắp Ráp Từng Layer
    desc: Chép lockfile, khóa chặt cài đặt bằng npm ci hoặc uv sync --frozen
    code: RUN npm ci / uv sync
    tone: cyan
    edge: docker build -t
  - icon: package
    badge: Artifact bất biến
    title: Image Gắn Tag Rõ Ràng
    desc: Sẵn sàng chạy với tiến trình chính giữ trực tiếp ghế PID 1 (Exec Form)
    code: shop-api:1.0.0
    tone: emerald
```

steps.headingEn: Determinism: Locking Down Lockfiles & the CMD Shell Form vs Exec Form Trap
steps.bodyEn:
On your local machine when adding a new library, you typically run `npm install` or `pip install fastapi`. Inside a `Dockerfile`, however, the primary goal is ==determinism== — building today or 6 months from now must produce the exact same dependency bytes:

- [x] **For Node.js:** Use **`RUN npm ci --omit=dev`** instead of `npm install` — if `package-lock.json` is out of sync, the command fails immediately rather than silently upgrading package versions!
- [x] **For modern Python (2026):** Use the blazing-fast **`uv`** package manager with **`RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev`** (10–50x faster than `pip`, strictly locked to `uv.lock`)!

Next is the most common mistake on the final `CMD` line:

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Ảnh Hưởng Của Cách Viết CMD Tới PID 1 & Tín Hiệu Dừng SIGTERM"
subtitle: Chỉ khác nhau cặp ngoặc vuông JSON nhưng quyết định ứng dụng tắt êm hay làm đứt ngang giao dịch của khách hàng!
left:
  badge: "CÁCH SAI · Shell Form"
  title: Docker âm thầm bọc vào /bin/sh -c
  tone: rose
  code: |
    # Bị biến thành: /bin/sh -c "node src/index.js"
    CMD node src/index.js

    # Hoặc bên Python viết dạng chuỗi:
    CMD uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
  lang: dockerfile
  bullets:
    - "Tiến trình giữ **PID 1** là `/bin/sh` chứ **không phải** `node` hay `uvicorn`"
    - "Khi `docker stop` hay Kubernetes cuộn phiên bản gửi `SIGTERM` tới PID 1, `/bin/sh` **nuốt mất tín hiệu**, không chuyển tiếp xuống app!"
    - "Container treo đơ hết 10s rồi bị ngắt bằng **`SIGKILL (137)`**, cắt đứt mọi request đang xử lý dở"
right:
  badge: "CÁCH CHUẨN · JSON Exec Form"
  title: Trao trực tiếp PID 1 cho ứng dụng
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    # Mảng JSON hợp lệ dùng dấu nháy kép "..."
    CMD ["node", "src/index.js"]

    # Hoặc FastAPI / Uvicorn chuẩn Exec Form:
    CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
  lang: dockerfile
  bullets:
    - "Chính tiến trình **`node` / `uvicorn` giữ trực tiếp ==PID 1==** trong không gian tên container"
    - "Nhận thẳng tín hiệu `SIGTERM` từ nhân Linux để đóng HTTP server & trả kết nối DB êm ái (*Graceful Shutdown*)"
    - "Luôn dùng dấu nháy kép `\"...\"` đúng chuẩn JSON (dùng nháy đơn `'...'` sẽ bị coi lại thành lỗi Shell Form!)"
```

steps.headingEn: Two Complete Dockerfile Templates: Node.js 22 LTS & Python 3.12 (uv + FastAPI)
steps.bodyEn:
Compare the two standard recipes below — you will see that their underlying structure is **identical step by step**:

```dockerfile Dockerfile chuẩn cơ bản — Node.js 22 LTS (Express / Fastify)
FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
COPY . .
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "src/index.js"]
```

```dockerfile Dockerfile chuẩn hiện đại 2026 — Python 3.12 + uv + FastAPI
FROM python:3.12-slim
COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.6 /uv /uvx /bin/
WORKDIR /app
ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH"
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock ./
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project
COPY app/ ./app/
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
```

> [!TIP] Explaining 3 Key Settings in the Python Dockerfile
> - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`: Prevents Python from writing hundreds of useless `.pyc` junk files into the container's writable layer.
> - `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`: Flushes all `print()` / `logging` output directly to `docker logs` immediately without buffering delays.
> - `--host 0.0.0.0`: Required to bind to `eth0` so it can accept traffic from `-p 8000:8000` or from a Kubernetes Service!

steps.headingEn: Packaging the Image with docker build -t
steps.bodyEn:
Compile the `Dockerfile` in the current directory into an image tagged with a clear Semantic Versioning tag:

```bash
docker build -t shop-api:1.0.0 .   # Đừng quên dấu chấm "." ở cuối lệnh!
```

> [!WARNING] Watch out for the tiny dot `.` at the end of `docker build`!
> The ==`.`== at the end of the command is the **Build Context** path — the directory Docker CLI bundles and sends to the BuildKit engine to locate the `Dockerfile` and execute `COPY` instructions. Forgetting the `.` is the most common mistake when first typing `docker build`!

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - **Prefer `COPY` over `ADD`** · Lock down lockfiles with **`RUN npm ci --omit=dev`** (Node) or **`RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev`** (Python) · Pin explicitly to `FROM node:22-alpine` or `FROM python:3.12-slim`.
> - `EXPOSE` is only port documentation metadata; it does **not** publish ports to the host automatically.
> - Always write ==`CMD ["...", "..."]`== (JSON array with double quotes) so your app directly owns **PID 1** and handles the `SIGTERM` shutdown signal cleanly.

readings.noteEn: The PID 1 trap that completely breaks Graceful Shutdown in Express/Fastify.
readings.taskEn: Explain why `CMD npm start` causes a container to take exactly 10 seconds to stop and get forcibly killed with `SIGKILL` instead of closing connections gracefully.
readings.answerEn: Writing `CMD npm start` (Shell Form) makes Docker run `/bin/sh -c "npm start"` as PID 1. When receiving `SIGTERM` from `docker stop`, `/bin/sh` on Alpine does not forward the signal to `node`, so `process.on("SIGTERM")` is never invoked; after the 10s timeout, Docker sends `SIGKILL` (exit 137). Fix: `CMD ["node", "src/server.js"]`.

readings.noteEn: A clean single-stage Dockerfile template for pure JavaScript services on Node 22 Alpine.
readings.taskEn: Identify 3 technical decisions in this file that make the build deterministic and safe for long-running production workloads.
readings.answerEn: 1) Pinning the base image `FROM node:22-alpine` instead of `:latest`; 2) Installing via `RUN npm ci --omit=dev` strictly adhering to `package-lock.json`; 3) Dropping privileges with `USER node` and running directly via JSON array `CMD ["node", "src/server.js"]`.

K03-Q1.qEn: In a Node.js service `Dockerfile`, why is `RUN npm ci` always preferred over `RUN npm install`?
choicesEn: Because `npm install` cannot install the `express` package on Linux
Because `npm ci` strictly reads `package-lock.json`, guaranteeing identical versions on every build and failing immediately if `package.json` drifts from the lockfile
Because `npm ci` automatically compiles TypeScript to C++
Because `npm ci` does not require a `package-lock.json` file
K03-Q1.explainEn: `npm ci` (Clean Install) is purpose-built for automated/Docker environments: it is faster, never mutates the lockfile, and guarantees 100% determinism.

K03-Q2.qEn: What actually happens when you write `CMD node src/index.js` (Shell Form) instead of `CMD ["node", "src/index.js"]` (Exec Form)?
choicesEn: There is no difference at runtime inside the container
Docker wraps the command in `/bin/sh -c "node src/index.js"`, making `/bin/sh` hold PID 1 and fail to forward `SIGTERM` signals to the `node` process on container stop
Exec Form runs twice as slowly because it has to parse JSON
Shell Form automatically enables multi-core cluster mode for Node.js
K03-Q2.explainEn: With JSON Exec Form `["node", "src/index.js"]`, the `node` process itself holds PID 1 and receives `SIGTERM` directly to perform Graceful Shutdown.

K03-Q3.qEn: The `EXPOSE 3000` instruction inside a `Dockerfile` automatically opens port `3000` on the host's external network interface without needing the `-p` flag during `docker run`.
K03-Q3.explainEn: False! `EXPOSE 3000` is purely documentation metadata indicating that the application inside listens on port `3000`. To publish it to the host, you still need `-p 3000:3000` when running `docker run`.

K03-Q4.qEn: In the Exec Form syntax for `CMD` or `ENTRYPOINT`, which of the following lines is valid without syntax errors?
choicesEn: `CMD ['node', 'src/index.js']` (using single quotes)
`CMD ["node", "src/index.js"]` (using a standard JSON array with double quotes)
`CMD [node, src/index.js]` (without quotes)
`CMD ("node", "src/index.js")` (using parentheses)
K03-Q4.explainEn: Exec Form is parsed by the Dockerfile parser as a strict JSON array, so it requires square brackets `[...]` and double quotes `"..."`.

K03-Q5.qEn: Between `COPY` and `ADD` in a `Dockerfile`, what does Docker's official documentation recommend for copying normal source files?
choicesEn: Always use `ADD` because its name is 1 character shorter

Always prefer `COPY` because its behavior is transparent and predictable (local file copying only); `ADD` has implicit `.tar` auto-extraction and URL fetching features that can introduce unintended risks
`COPY` was removed in Docker v27
`COPY` can only copy 1 file at a time, whereas `ADD` is needed to copy directories
K03-Q5.explainEn: Docker Best Practices state clearly: always default to `COPY`; only use `ADD` when you intentionally want automatic local archive extraction.

K03-Q6.qEn: In the image build command below, what character is missing at `____` to specify the current directory as the **Build Context**?
K03-Q6.explainEn: The dot `.` passes the current working directory as the Build Context so Docker can locate the `Dockerfile` and source files for `COPY` instructions.

K03-Q7.qEn: A container is built with `CMD ["node", "src/index.js"]`. Inside that container, what process ID (`PID`) will the `node` process have?
K03-Q7.explainEn: By using JSON Exec Form without an intermediate shell, the `node` process becomes the root init process inside the PID Namespace with `PID 1`.

K03-FC1.frontEn: What is the execution-time difference between **`RUN`** and **`CMD`** in a Dockerfile?
K03-FC1.backEn:
- **`RUN`** executes once **during image build (`docker build`)** to create a new layer (e.g., installing `npm ci`).
- **`CMD`** specifies the default command executed **when starting a container (`docker run`)**.

K03-FC2.frontEn: Why should you write `CMD ["node", "src/index.js"]` (Exec Form) instead of `CMD node src/index.js` (Shell Form)?
K03-FC2.backEn: So the `node` process directly holds **PID 1** and receives **`SIGTERM`** on container shutdown, rather than having `/bin/sh -c` block it and break Graceful Shutdown.

K03-FC3.frontEn: Why should `WORKDIR /app` always be declared before `COPY` and `RUN` instructions?
K03-FC3.backEn: It automatically creates `/app` (if missing) and sets it as the working directory for all subsequent instructions, avoiding cluttering the OS root directory `/`.

K03-FC4.frontEn: What are the three core advantages of the `node:22-alpine` base variant over full `node:22`?

K03-FC5.frontEn: What is the role of the trailing dot `.` in `docker build -t shop-api:1.0.0 .`?
K03-FC5.backEn: It specifies the **Build Context** path — the root directory Docker reads files from and sends to BuildKit for `COPY` instructions.

K03-FC6.frontEn: What benefits does setting `ENV NODE_ENV=production` in a Dockerfile provide for a Node.js app?
K03-FC6.backEn: It enables memory and performance optimizations in Express/Fastify/React, hides sensitive stack traces from HTTP error responses, and enforces production behavior across libraries.

K03-FC7.frontEn: Why does the community in 2026 prefer `python:3.12-slim` + `uv` over `-alpine` when packaging **Python / FastAPI**?
K03-FC7.backEn: Because `python:3.12-slim` uses standard **`glibc`**, letting `uv sync --frozen --no-dev` download prebuilt `manylinux` binary wheels (`pydantic-core`, `numpy`, `psycopg`) rapidly instead of compiling from C source as required on Alpine's `musl`.

kube-ex-k03-1.titleEn: Pin the Base Image to node:22-alpine instead of :latest

kube-ex-k03-2.titleEn: Set working directory WORKDIR /app before copying code

K04.titleEn: Optimizing Build Speed with Docker Layer Cache & .dockerignore
K04.summaryEn: Order COPY/RUN to preserve dependency cache (npm ci / uv sync), write .dockerignore with !README.md exceptions, distinguish ARG vs ENV, and keep system package layers clean.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
You wrote your first working `Dockerfile` in `K03`. Yet just a few days later, the team starts complaining: *"Every time I fix a single typo in `src/routes/health.js` (or `app/routers/health.py`), running `docker build` takes almost 2 minutes re-downloading every library!"* — not to mention the image ballooned to nearly 900 MB and accidentally leaked your personal `.env` password file!

This lesson solves all three pain points completely using BuildKit's ==Layer Cache== (**20–50x faster builds**), the ==`.dockerignore`== shield (**preventing secret leaks & virtual-env junk**), and separating **Build-time `ARG`** from **Run-time `ENV`** parameters.

steps.headingEn: How Docker Layer Cache Works and Instruction Ordering
steps.bodyEn:
> [!NOTE] Layer Reuse & Cascading Cache Invalidation
> Every `FROM`, `WORKDIR`, `COPY`, and `RUN` instruction in a `Dockerfile` produces a sequential layer. BuildKit checks the cache from top to bottom: if a single layer at position `k` has changed inputs, every subsequent layer `k+1, k+2...` below it loses its cache and must re-execute from scratch. Therefore, rarely changing steps (OS setup, copying lockfiles, installing dependencies) go near the top, while the most frequently changing step (`COPY`ing source code) goes at the very bottom (just like stacking bricks from foundation to roof: replacing a roof tile leaves the foundation untouched).

When you run `docker build`, BuildKit evaluates layers sequentially from top to bottom:

- [x] **SHA256 Hash Matching:** For `COPY`, BuildKit computes a checksum of all copied source files. If not a single byte changed, it immediately reuses the cached layer — reporting **`CACHED` (`0.0s`)**!
- [!] **Cascading *Cache Invalidation* Rule:** The moment **layer `k` misses cache** (because a source file changed), ==EVERY layer `k+1, k+2...` below it is forced to rebuild from scratch==, even if those commands didn't change a single character!

```visual
kind: layers
title: "Ảnh Hưởng Của Thứ Tự Chỉ Thị Tới Cache Khi Sửa 1 Dòng Code"
```

See how the exact same Layer Cache principle applies seamlessly to both **Node.js** and **Python (`uv` + `FastAPI`)**:

```dockerfile Dockerfile tối ưu Layer Cache — Node.js 22 LTS
FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app

# Bước ít đổi: chép riêng manifest & cài thư viện trước
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev

# Bước đổi liên tục mỗi phút: đặt ở dưới cùng!
COPY . .
CMD ["node", "src/index.js"]
```

```dockerfile Dockerfile tối ưu Layer Cache — Python 3.12 + uv + FastAPI
FROM python:3.12-slim
COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.6 /uv /uvx /bin/
WORKDIR /app
ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH"

# 1. Chỉ chép 2 tệp khóa gói trước -> giữ nguyên Cache khi sửa code trong app/!
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock ./
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project

# 2. Chép mã nguồn Python ở tầng cuối cùng (build lại mất < 1 giây)
COPY app/ ./app/
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
```

steps.headingEn: The .dockerignore File: Filtering Build Context for Speed and Security
steps.bodyEn:
> [!WARNING] Docker does NOT automatically read `.gitignore`!
> When you run `docker build -t shop-api:1.0.0 .`, Docker packages the entire `.` directory (**Build Context**) and sends it to BuildKit. If you forget to create **`.dockerignore`**, your local `node_modules` (500 MB), `.venv` (400 MB), `.git`, and `.env` secrets will all be sent straight into the image!

```visual

title: "Ba Vấn Đề Được Ngăn Chặn Nhờ Tệp .dockerignore"
columns: 3
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: cpu

    badge: Tránh lệch kiến trúc
    tone: amber
    bullets:

      - "Tránh việc `COPY . .` chép đè binary macOS làm hỏng `node_modules` hoặc `.venv` Linux vừa cài trong Image!"
  - num: 2
    icon: folder-git
    title: "Chặn .git & __pycache__"
    badge: Giữ vững Cache
    tone: sky
    bullets:
      - "Mỗi lần bạn gõ `git commit` hay chạy pytest, dữ liệu trong `.git/`, `__pycache__/`, `coverage/` lại thay đổi"
      - "Chặn chúng giúp lệnh `COPY . .` không bị vỡ cache oan uổng"
  - num: 3
    icon: shield-alert
    title: "Chặn Tuyệt Đối .env & *.pem"

    tone: rose

      - "Ngăn khóa bí mật `.env`, `.env.local`, `*.pem` trên ổ cứng lọt vào các lớp Image"
      - "**Nhớ kỹ:** Đã lỡ `COPY .env` ở layer 2 thì `RUN rm -f .env` ở layer 3 **KHÔNG xóa được** dữ liệu thật vẫn nằm trong bản chụp layer 2!"
```

### Multi-Language Exclusion Patterns & the `!` Negation Rule in `.dockerignore`

`.dockerignore` is evaluated top to bottom; **later rules override earlier rules**, allowing you to prefix a line with an exclamation mark ==`!`== to keep an exception file:

```dockerignore
# Thư mục môi trường gói của Node.js & Python:
node_modules
.venv
venv
__pycache__
.pytest_cache

# Lịch sử Git, báo cáo test & bí mật cục bộ:
.git
.env
.env.*
coverage
dist

# Chặn toàn bộ tài liệu Markdown nội bộ, NHƯNG giữ lại duy nhất README.md:
*.md
!README.md
```

- [!] **Beware over-broad exclusions:** Never blindly add `*.json` or `*.toml` to `.dockerignore`, or you will accidentally exclude `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, or `pyproject.toml`, breaking `docker build` immediately!

steps.bodyEn:
