steps.headingEn: Installing System Packages (apk / apt-get) Cleanly in 1 Layer
steps.bodyEn:
Sometimes your app needs extra C libraries or small utilities like `curl`, `libpq5`, or `tzdata`. Because each `RUN` instruction creates an immutable additive layer (deleting files in a later `RUN` does not shrink an earlier `RUN` layer!), always combine installation and cleanup into **a single `RUN` instruction**:

```dockerfile
# Trên nền Alpine Linux (apk): cờ --no-cache tải chỉ mục trên RAM, không lưu rác vào /var/cache/apk/
RUN apk add --no-cache curl

# Trên nền Debian Slim như python:3.12-slim (apt-get): nối update + install + xóa lists trong CÙNG 1 dòng RUN
RUN apt-get update \
  && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates libpq5 \
  && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```

> [!TIP] BuildKit Secret Mounts for private package registries during `docker build`
> If during `RUN npm ci` or `RUN uv sync` you need an auth token for a private company registry, never pass it via `ARG NPM_TOKEN`! Use BuildKit's `RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc,target=/root/.npmrc npm ci` so the token is mounted temporarily in RAM only during installation and **never leaves a trace in any image layer**.

```visual
kind: troubleshoot
title: Hai Cái Bẫy Phình Dung Lượng & Lộ Bí Mật Giữa Các Layer
items:
  - symptom: Lỡ COPY .env ở dòng trên rồi chạy RUN rm -f .env ở dòng dưới
    badge: Bất biến Layer
    tone: rose
    cause: Mỗi layer là một bản chụp chỉ đọc độc lập. Lệnh `rm` ở layer 3 chỉ đặt một dấu ẩn (whiteout) lên bề mặt, còn nội dung thật của `.env` vẫn nằm nguyên vẹn trong layer 2!
    fix: Xóa bỏ dòng COPY nhạy cảm, chặn `.env` bằng `.dockerignore` và xoay vòng (rotate) ngay khóa bí mật đã lộ.
  - symptom: Tách rời 2 dòng RUN apk update và RUN apk add curl trên Alpine
    badge: Lỗi Stale Cache 404
    tone: amber
    cause: Dòng `RUN apk update` vừa để lại rác chỉ mục làm nặng Image, vừa bị kẹt trong cache cũ nhiều tuần khiến `RUN apk add curl` sau đó tải nhầm bản gói đã xóa trên kho Alpine (lỗi 404).
    fix: Luôn gộp thành 1 dòng chuẩn duy nhất `RUN apk add --no-cache curl`.
    cmd: RUN apk add --no-cache curl
```

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - **Golden order for Layer Cache:** Copy lockfiles (`package*.json` or `pyproject.toml uv.lock`) → install packages (`RUN npm ci` / `RUN uv sync --frozen`) → `COPY` source code last.
> - Always create **`.dockerignore`** to exclude `node_modules`, `.venv`, `__pycache__`, `.git`, and `.env` (use leading **`!`** like `!README.md` for exceptions).
> - **`ARG`** lives only during `docker build` · **`ENV`** persists into the running container · On Alpine always use ==`RUN apk add --no-cache <package>`==.

readings.noteEn: A real-world .dockerignore template for any Node.js / TypeScript service.
readings.taskEn: Look at the last two lines `*.md` and `!README.md`. What happens if you reverse their order and put `!README.md` above `*.md`?
readings.answerEn: In `.dockerignore`, later rules override earlier rules. If `!README.md` appears before `*.md`, the `*.md` rule overrides it and still excludes `README.md` from the Build Context!

readings.noteEn: A sloppy .dockerignore that leaks .env while accidentally excluding app configuration files.
readings.taskEn: Identify the 2 critical bugs in this file and how to fix each one.
readings.answerEn: 1) Missing exclusions for `.env`, `.env.*`, and `.git`, leaking local secrets into image layers; 2) Broadly ignoring `*.json` excludes `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, and `src/config/*.json` — remove the `*.json` line.

readings.noteEn: A classic lesson on how splitting package update and cleanup commands bloats image size.
readings.taskEn: Why does adding a separate `RUN rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*` line below NOT reduce the image size bloated by the line above?
readings.answerEn: Every `RUN` instruction creates an immutable read-only layer. Files written in layer 2 remain permanently in layer 2's tarball; deleting them in layer 3 only writes a whiteout marker without reclaiming space from the previous layer. You must combine them into a single `RUN` instruction!

K04-Q1.qEn: In a `Dockerfile`, why do we copy `COPY package.json package-lock.json ./` and run `RUN npm ci` **BEFORE** running `COPY . .`?
choicesEn: Because `COPY . .` is not allowed to copy `.json` files
To leverage Layer Cache: when a developer only edits code in `src/` without changing dependencies, the slowest step `RUN npm ci` stays cached (0 seconds)
Because Node.js requires creating `node_modules` before the `src` directory can exist
To encrypt the `src/` directory with SHA256
K04-Q1.explainEn: Putting rarely changing steps (`package*.json` -> `npm ci`) at the top and the most frequently changing step (`COPY . .`) at the bottom is rule #1 for optimizing Docker build speed.

K04-Q2.qEn: When a layer in the middle of a `Dockerfile` misses the cache, Docker only re-runs that single line and then continues reusing cached layers for all `RUN` instructions below it.
K04-Q2.explainEn: False! Once layer `k` changes and must re-run, all subsequent layers `k+1, k+2...` depend on the new filesystem state and suffer cascading cache invalidation.

K04-Q3.qEn: What happens if you forget to create a `.dockerignore` file in a Node.js project developed on an M3 MacBook (`darwin-arm64`) and run `COPY . .`?
choicesEn: Docker automatically reads `.gitignore` instead of `.dockerignore`
Your entire local `node_modules` (containing macOS binaries), `.git`, and even your `.env` file on the Mac get sent into the Build Context and copied straight into the Linux image!
Docker refuses to run `docker build`
Nothing bad happens because Docker automatically filters out all hidden dotfiles
K04-Q3.explainEn: Docker does NOT automatically read `.gitignore`! Without `.dockerignore`, `.env`, `.git`, and heavy host `node_modules` all leak into the image.

K04-Q4.qEn: What is the exact difference between `ARG` and `ENV` in a `Dockerfile`?
choicesEn: `ARG` exists while the container is running (`process.env`), whereas `ENV` only exists during `docker build`
`ARG` is only available during `docker build` (and disappears when the container runs), whereas `ENV` is baked into the image and available in `process.env` at container runtime
`ARG` securely encrypts secrets so they never appear in `docker history`, whereas `ENV` does not
The two instructions are completely identical
K04-Q4.explainEn: `ARG` is for build-time parameters (`--build-arg`); to let a Node.js app read that value via `process.env` at runtime, assign `ENV APP_VERSION=$APP_VERSION`. And remember: NEITHER should ever hold secrets!

K04-Q5.qEn: On Alpine Linux (`node:22-alpine`), what is the cleanest way to install `curl` without leaving package index junk that bloats the layer?
choicesEn: Write 2 separate lines: `RUN apk update` followed by `RUN apk add curl`
Write a single line: `RUN apk add --no-cache curl`
Use `RUN apt-get install curl`
Use `RUN npm install -g curl`
K04-Q5.explainEn: Alpine uses the `apk` package manager; the `--no-cache` flag fetches the latest index without writing cached index files to `/var/cache/apk/`.

K04-Q6.qEn: In `.dockerignore`, to create an exception that **keeps** `README.md` after blocking all `*.md` files above (`____README.md`), what special character goes at the start of the line?
K04-Q6.explainEn: A leading exclamation mark `!` in `.dockerignore` represents negation (an exception) — bringing matching files back into the Build Context.

K04-Q7.qEn: If in layer 2 you accidentally `COPY .env ./` into the image and then in layer 3 run `RUN rm -f .env`, anyone who can pull that image can still extract the intact `.env` file from layer 2.
K04-Q7.explainEn: 100% true! Running `rm` in a later layer only hides the file in the final merged filesystem; the actual `.env` contents remain intact inside layer 2's tarball when inspected.

K04-FC1.frontEn: What is the golden 3-step order in a `Dockerfile` to preserve the `npm ci` cache for a Node.js project?
K04-FC1.backEn:
1) `COPY package.json package-lock.json ./`
2) `RUN npm ci`
3) `COPY . .` (place frequently edited source code last).

K04-FC2.frontEn: What are the three most important goals of a **`.dockerignore`** file?

K04-FC3.frontEn: How do you ignore all Markdown files while still keeping `README.md` in `.dockerignore`?
K04-FC3.backEn:
Write them in exact top-to-bottom order:
```
*.md
!README.md
```

K04-FC4.frontEn: How do you pass a version from `docker build --build-arg` so `process.env` can read it at runtime?
K04-FC4.backEn:
Combine both instructions:
```dockerfile
ARG APP_VERSION=1.0.0
ENV APP_VERSION=$APP_VERSION
```

K04-FC5.frontEn: Why must you never pass a private `NPM_TOKEN` via `ARG` in a `Dockerfile`?
K04-FC5.backEn: Because `ARG` values are recorded in image history metadata — anyone running `docker history --no-trunc` can read them (use BuildKit `--mount=type=secret` instead).

K04-FC6.frontEn: What is the clean syntax to install packages on Alpine Linux (`apk`) without leaving cache junk?
K04-FC6.backEn: **`RUN apk add --no-cache <package-name>`** (do not split out a separate `RUN apk update` line).

kube-ex-k04-1.titleEn: Reorder COPY and RUN to enable Layer Caching
kube-ex-k04-1.promptEn:
The `Dockerfile` below places `COPY . .` before `RUN npm ci`, breaking the cache and reinstalling all dependencies on every 1-line edit in `src/`. Reorder it so that:
1. Only `COPY package.json package-lock.json ./` is copied first.
2. `RUN npm ci` runs next.
3. The rest of the source code is copied afterward with `COPY . .`.
hintsEn: Split the copy into 2 steps: first copy only `package.json package-lock.json ./`, run `RUN npm ci`, and then run `COPY . .`.
Correct order: `COPY package.json package-lock.json ./` -> `RUN npm ci` -> `COPY . .`.

kube-ex-k04-2.promptEn: Create a `.dockerignore` file that prevents `node_modules`, `.git`, and the secret `.env` file from entering the Build Context, while still keeping `package.json` and source files in `src/server.ts`.
hintsEn: Each line in `.dockerignore` is a directory name or glob pattern similar to `.gitignore`.

kube-ex-k04-3.titleEn: Use ! negation in .dockerignore to keep README.md
kube-ex-k04-3.promptEn:
Update `.dockerignore` to:
1. Ignore the test coverage directory `coverage`.
2. Ignore all `*.md` documentation files (such as `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/architecture.md`), **EXCEPT** keep `README.md` using the `!README.md` negation rule.

kube-ex-k04-4.titleEn: Chain build-time ARG to runtime ENV for app version
kube-ex-k04-4.promptEn:

2. Immediately below it, pass it into `ENV APP_VERSION=$APP_VERSION`.

`ARG APP_VERSION=1.0.0`
`ENV APP_VERSION=$APP_VERSION`

kube-ex-k04-5.titleEn: Install Alpine packages cleanly in 1 layer with --no-cache
kube-ex-k04-5.promptEn: The current `Dockerfile` splits `RUN apk update` and `RUN apk add curl` into two lines, storing index junk in a layer and risking stale cache. Merge them into **a single `RUN` instruction** using `apk add --no-cache curl`.

kube-ex-k04-6.titleEn: Diagnose & overhaul a 1.18GB Dockerfile with broken cache
kube-ex-k04-6.promptEn:
The dev team complains that the local `shop-api:latest` image weighs **1180 MB** and every code edit takes nearly 2 minutes to rebuild! You can run `docker images` in the diagnostic terminal pane to confirm, then overhaul the `Dockerfile` in the editor to meet all **4 standards**:
1. Switch `FROM` to `node:22-alpine`.
2. Copy `COPY package.json package-lock.json ./` before installing dependencies.
3. Replace `npm install` with `RUN npm ci`, then run `COPY . .`.
4. Convert `CMD` to JSON Exec Form `CMD ["node", "src/server.js"]`.
hintsEn: Update each line from top to bottom: `FROM node:22-alpine` -> `WORKDIR /app` -> `COPY package.json package-lock.json ./` -> `RUN npm ci` -> `COPY . .`.
On the last line, change `CMD node src/server.js` to `CMD ["node", "src/server.js"]`.

K05.titleEn: Multi-stage Builds, Non-Root Users & Production HEALTHCHECK
K05.summaryEn: Separate the build stage (AS builder) from a lean runtime stage (AS runner) for both Node.js & Python, prune devDependencies, drop root privileges, and configure HEALTHCHECK.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
When packaging real-world projects (**TypeScript / NestJS / Next.js** or **Python FastAPI with C/Rust-compiled packages**), you always face a classic dilemma:

- [>] **During build & install (`builder`):** You must have `typescript`, `esbuild`, `uv`/`pip`, or C compilers like `gcc`, `build-essential`, and `libpq-dev` — consuming **700 MB to 1.2 GB**.
- [>] **At runtime in Production (`runner`):** The app only needs the compiled **`dist/`** directory (or a clean `.venv`) plus production runtime libraries!

Packing all the build machinery into one image slows down image pulls by 5x when Kubernetes scales Pods, while handing attackers compilers and `root` access! ==Multi-stage Builds== (**cutting size by up to 85%**), **Non-Root execution (`UID 1000`)**, and **self-probing `HEALTHCHECK`** are the golden production trio in 2026.

steps.headingEn: Shrinking Image Size with Multi-stage Dockerfiles (builder → runner)
steps.bodyEn:
> [!NOTE] How Multi-stage Builds Work: Separating Build Time from Runtime
> A single `Dockerfile` can contain **multiple `FROM` instructions**. Each `FROM` starts an independent stage: all compilers, raw source code, and heavy build tools live only in the build stage (**`AS builder`**), and then you use `COPY --from=builder` to copy only the compiled artifacts into a clean runtime stage (**`AS runner`**) for Production (think of separating a messy prep kitchen from the clean plated dish served to the table).


### Template 1: Production Multi-stage for **Node.js 22 / TypeScript**

```dockerfile Dockerfile Multi-stage chuẩn Production (Node 22 LTS)
# ==================== STAGE 1: builder (Biên dịch) ====================
FROM node:22-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app

# 1. Cài đầy đủ cả dependencies lẫn devDependencies để có trình biên dịch tsc
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci

# 2. Chép cấu hình + mã nguồn TypeScript và biên dịch ra /app/dist
COPY tsconfig.json ./
COPY src ./src
RUN npm run build

# 3. Gọt bỏ toàn bộ devDependencies theo chuẩn npm 10+ hiện đại
RUN npm prune --omit=dev

# ==================== STAGE 2: runner (Runtime tối giản) ====================
FROM node:22-alpine AS runner
ENV NODE_ENV=production
WORKDIR /app

# Chỉ gắp thành phẩm từ stage "builder" sang và gán quyền sở hữu rõ ràng
COPY --from=builder --chown=node:node /app/package.json ./package.json
COPY --from=builder --chown=node:node /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=builder --chown=node:node /app/dist ./dist

USER node
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/main.js"]
```

### Template 2: Production Multi-stage for **Python 3.12 + `uv` + `FastAPI`**

With Python, the `builder` stage uses an image containing `uv` (and compilers if building C extensions), while `runner` copies over only the `/app/.venv` virtual environment — the final image doesn't even need `pip` or `uv`, making it both tiny and highly secure:

```dockerfile Dockerfile Multi-stage chuẩn Production (Python 3.12 + uv + FastAPI)
# ==================== STAGE 1: builder ====================
FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.12-bookworm-slim AS builder
ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 UV_LINK_MODE=copy
WORKDIR /app

COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock ./
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project
COPY app ./app

# ==================== STAGE 2: runner ====================
FROM python:3.12-slim AS runner
WORKDIR /app
ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH"

# Tạo tài khoản phi đặc quyền appuser (UID 1000) vì python:3.12-slim chưa tạo sẵn như Node
RUN useradd --create-home --uid 1000 appuser

COPY --from=builder --chown=appuser:appuser /app/.venv /app/.venv
COPY --from=builder --chown=appuser:appuser /app/app /app/app

USER appuser
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
```

> [!TIP] Modern 2026 syntax for pruning dev dependencies
> In Node.js 22 (npm 10+), always write ==`npm prune --omit=dev`== (`--omit=dev` replaces the deprecated npm v6 flags). In Python `uv`, simply pass `--no-dev` to `uv sync` to strip `pytest`, `ruff`, and `mypy` cleanly from `.venv`!

steps.headingEn: Dropping Root Privileges with USER (UID 1000): Mandatory Security Practice
steps.bodyEn:
A fact that surprises many newcomers: ==without a `USER` instruction, every Docker container runs by default as the all-powerful `root` (`UID 0`)!==

```visual

title: "Chạy Mặc Định Dưới Quyền root (UID 0) vs Hạ Quyền Non-Root (UID 1000)"
subtitle: "Hạ quyền bảo vệ máy chủ khỏi nguy cơ leo thang đặc quyền khi ứng dụng chẳng may dính lỗ hổng RCE!"

  badge: "RỦI RO NGHIÊM TRỌNG · Mặc định UID 0 (root)"
  title: "Bỏ quên chỉ thị USER trong Dockerfile"
  tone: rose
  code: |
    # Không có dòng USER -> chạy thẳng bằng root (UID 0)!
    EXPOSE 80
    CMD ["node", "dist/main.js"]
  lang: dockerfile
  bullets:
    - "`UID 0` trong container ánh xạ thẳng với `UID 0` của nhân Linux trên nhiều cấu hình máy chủ"
    - "Nếu dính lỗ hổng RCE hoặc Container Escape, kẻ tấn công chiếm trọn quyền tối cao"
    - "Bị cụm Kubernetes bật **Pod Security Admission `restricted`** từ chối thẳng thừng không cho chạy!"
right:
  badge: "CHUẨN PRODUCTION · Non-Root UID 1000"
  title: "Chuyển sang USER node / appuser + Cổng >= 1024"

    COPY --from=builder --chown=node:node /app/dist ./dist
    USER node
    EXPOSE 3000
    CMD ["node", "dist/main.js"]

  bullets:
    - "Image `node:22-alpine` đã tạo sẵn ==`USER node`== (`UID 1000`); với `python:3.12-slim` chỉ cần thêm `useradd -u 1000 appuser` rồi gọi `USER appuser`"
    - "**Lưu ý cổng Linux:** Tài khoản thường (`UID >= 1000`) **không được mở cổng đặc quyền `< 1024`** (cố mở cổng `80` hay `443` sẽ sập ngay với lỗi `EACCES` / `PermissionError`!)"
    - "Luôn để ứng dụng lắng nghe ở cổng cao như **`3000`**, **`8000`** hoặc **`8080`**"
```

steps.headingEn: Monitoring Container Health with HEALTHCHECK (No curl Needed)
steps.bodyEn:
Picture the most insidious production failure: a Redis connection hangs or an event loop hits a *deadlock*, causing every incoming request to hang with `504 Timeout`, yet the `node` or `python` process **never exits** so `docker ps` cheerfully reports `Up 3 days`!

The ==`HEALTHCHECK`== instruction teaches Docker Engine to actively probe an internal HTTP endpoint periodically — and the cleanest approach is **using the built-in standard library of Node 22 / Python 3.12** so you never have to install `curl` in `runner`:

```dockerfile
# Cách 1 — Trên Node.js 22 (tận dụng hàm fetch() toàn cục có sẵn):
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=10s --retries=3 \
  CMD ["node", "-e", "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3000/healthz').then(r => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1)).catch(() => process.exit(1))"]

# Cách 2 — Trên Python 3.12 (tận dụng urllib.request có sẵn trong stdlib):
# HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=10s --retries=3 \
#   CMD ["python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/healthz', timeout=2)"]
```

```visual
kind: anatomy
title: "Cấu Trúc Chỉ Thị HEALTHCHECK Không Cần Cài curl / wget"
subtitle: "Giữ Image cuối sạch bóng công cụ tải mạng dư thừa để tăng cường bảo mật tối đa"
items:
  - keyword: "--interval & --timeout"
    role: Nhịp kiểm tra & Hạn giờ
    tone: sky
    summary: "Cứ mỗi `30s` Docker gửi yêu cầu kiểm tra 1 lần; nếu quá `3s` không phản hồi thì tính là 1 lần thất bại."
    bullets:
      - "`--start-period=10s` ân xá 10 giây đầu lúc ứng dụng đang khởi động kết nối DB"
      - "`--retries=3` cho phép trượt liên tiếp 3 lần trước khi chính thức gắn nhãn `(unhealthy)`"
  - keyword: "Native fetch / urllib"
    role: Không cần cài thêm curl
    tone: emerald
    summary: "Tận dụng `fetch()` của Node 22 hoặc `urllib.request` của Python 3.12 thay vì chạy `apk add curl` / `apt-get install curl`."
    bullets:
      - "**Lợi ích bảo mật kép:** Không có `curl` / `wget` ở stage `runner` khiến kẻ tấn công không có công cụ tải mã độc về nếu ứng dụng lỡ dính lỗi RCE!"
  - keyword: "exit 0 vs exit 1"
    role: Quy ước mã thoát chuẩn
    tone: amber
    summary: "Docker phán quyết sức khỏe container hoàn toàn dựa vào mã thoát của lệnh kiểm tra."
    bullets:
      - "==`exit 0`== → **Khỏe mạnh (`healthy`)**: cột `STATUS` trong `docker ps` hiện rõ `Up 2 minutes (healthy)`"
      - "**`exit 1`** → **Bất ổn (`unhealthy`)**: báo động cho Docker Compose (`condition: service_healthy`) hoặc hệ thống giám sát xử lý kịp thời"
```

> [!WARNING] Why can `HEALTHCHECK` call `127.0.0.1`?
> In `K01`, we learned the host cannot reach a container's `127.0.0.1`. However, `HEALTHCHECK` commands are executed by Docker **inside that container's own Network Namespace**, so probing `http://127.0.0.1:3000/healthz` (or `:8000/healthz`) is completely valid and fast!

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - **Multi-stage Build:** Compile in `FROM ... AS builder`, strip dev packages (`RUN npm prune --omit=dev` or `uv sync --no-dev`), and copy artifacts into `runner` via **`COPY --from=builder`**.
> - Containers run as `root` (`UID 0`) by default → always drop privileges with **`USER node`** / **`USER appuser`** (`UID 1000`) and listen on ports **`>= 1024`** (`3000` / `8000` / `8080`).
> - **`HEALTHCHECK`** uses `node -e "fetch(...)"` or `python -c "import urllib.request..."` cleanly without `curl`: exit **`0`** = `healthy` · non-zero = `unhealthy`.

readings.noteEn: The 2-stage golden blueprint for any TypeScript / NestJS / Fastify project in 2026.
readings.taskEn: Check whether the final `runner` stage contains the raw `src/` directory or `tsconfig.json`, and explain what benefits that brings.
readings.answerEn: Neither `src/` nor `tsconfig.json` exists in `runner` — only `package.json`, `node_modules` pruned with `npm prune --omit=dev`, and compiled `dist/`. This keeps the image ultra-light and avoids shipping TypeScript source code or build tools.

readings.noteEn: Expanding to a 3-stage build (`deps` -> `builder` -> `runner`) for Next.js App Router Standalone.
readings.taskEn: Why does Next.js create a dedicated `nextjs` user with UID `1001` in the `runner` stage instead of leaving the default?
readings.answerEn: To enforce Least Privilege: the web process running as UID `1001` cannot overwrite system files, has no login shell, and passes Kubernetes Pod Security Admission `restricted` checks out of the box.

readings.noteEn: High-security tier: the final stage uses Distroless without `/bin/sh` or any package manager.
readings.taskEn: Why does completely removing `/bin/sh` and `apk`/`apt` from the final image effectively neutralize Reverse Shell attacks?
readings.answerEn: If an attacker exploits an RCE vulnerability and invokes `child_process.exec("/bin/sh -c ...")`, the call fails because `/bin/sh` does not exist, and there is no `curl`/`wget` to download exploit payloads.

K05-Q1.qEn: What is the biggest benefit of a **Multi-stage Build** (`FROM ... AS builder` then `FROM ... AS runner`) for a TypeScript application?
choicesEn: It automatically load-balances the application across 2 physical servers
It lets you install `typescript` and heavy build tools in `builder` to compile `dist/`, while the final `runner` image only receives the clean build artifacts without carrying extra tools
It lets you skip writing a `package.json` file
It lets you run both Windows and Linux in the same process
K05-Q1.explainEn: Multi-stage builds separate the build environment (which needs dev tooling) from the runtime environment (which only needs the runtime and compiled code), dramatically shrinking image size and attack surface.

K05-Q2.qEn: On Node.js 22 (npm 10+), which modern command cleanly removes all `devDependencies` from `node_modules` after running `npm run build`?
choicesEn: `npm prune --production` (legacy deprecated flag)
`npm prune --omit=dev`
`rm -rf node_modules`
`npm uninstall typescript`
K05-Q2.explainEn: Since npm v8.x and into 2026, `--omit=dev` is the standard syntax completely replacing the legacy `--production` flag.

K05-Q3.qEn: If you do not declare a `USER` instruction in your `Dockerfile`, processes inside the container run by default with superuser `root` privileges (`UID 0`).
K05-Q3.explainEn: True! Docker runs as `UID 0` (`root`) by default. On official Node images, always switch to `USER node` (`UID 1000`) in the final stage.

K05-Q4.qEn: To copy `/app/dist` from the first stage (`AS builder`) into `./dist` in the second stage (`AS runner`), which syntax should you use?
choicesEn: `COPY /app/dist ./dist`
`COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist`
`ADD builder:/app/dist ./dist`
`MOVE --stage=builder /app/dist ./dist`
K05-Q4.explainEn: The `--from=<stage-name>` flag tells `COPY` to pull files from a previous stage's filesystem instead of the external Build Context.

K05-Q5.qEn: When switching to an unprivileged user (`USER node`, UID 1000), which network port below will the Linux kernel reject with `EACCES: permission denied` if the app tries to bind to it directly?
choicesEn: Port `3000`
Port `8080`
Port `80` (in the privileged port range `< 1024`)
Port `5000`
K05-Q5.explainEn: On Linux, ports below `1024` (like `80` and `443`) are privileged ports reserved for elevated processes. Non-root accounts should listen on ports `>= 1024` such as `3000` or `8080`.

K05-Q6.qEn: In the official `node:22-alpine` image, what is the name of the pre-created non-root user account (UID 1000) (`USER ____`)?
K05-Q6.explainEn: All official `node` image variants pre-create the `node` group and `node` user (`UID 1000`) so you can immediately use `USER node`.

K05-Q7.qEn: In a `HEALTHCHECK` probe command, exiting with code `0` (`exit 0`) marks the container as `healthy`, while exiting with `1` (`exit 1`) marks it as `unhealthy`.
K05-Q7.explainEn: True! The `HEALTHCHECK` convention is `0` = healthy (success) and `1` = unhealthy (failure).

K05-FC1.frontEn: What is the syntax to copy build artifacts from the `builder` stage to the `runner` stage in a Multi-stage Dockerfile?

K05-FC2.frontEn: What is the 2026 standard command to strip `devDependencies` after running `npm run build` in the `builder` stage?
K05-FC2.backEn: **`RUN npm prune --omit=dev`** (never use the legacy `--production` flag).

K05-FC3.frontEn: Why should you add `USER node` near the end of a `Dockerfile` before deploying to Production Kubernetes?
K05-FC3.backEn: It prevents the process from running as `root` (`UID 0`), limits blast radius in an RCE exploit, and satisfies Kubernetes Pod Security Admission's `runAsNonRoot: true` policy.

K05-FC4.frontEn: Why write `HEALTHCHECK` on `node:22-alpine` with `node -e "fetch(...)"` instead of installing `curl`?
K05-FC4.backEn: Node 22 includes global `fetch()` out of the box, so you avoid installing `curl`—keeping the image smaller and denying attackers a download tool.

K05-FC5.frontEn: When running as a non-root user (`UID >= 1000`), which port range should the application bind to?
K05-FC5.backEn: Listen on ports **`>= 1024`** (such as `3000` or `8080`), because ports `< 1024` (like `80`) are privileged ports on Linux.

K05-FC6.frontEn: In a Multi-stage Dockerfile with 3 `FROM` instructions, which stage does `docker build` output by default?

kube-ex-k05-1.titleEn: Declare a 2-stage Dockerfile structure (builder and runner)
kube-ex-k05-1.promptEn:
Split the single-stage `Dockerfile` below into a **2-stage (Multi-stage)** architecture using `node:22-alpine`:
- Alias Stage 1 as `AS builder` (containing dependency installation and `RUN npm run build`).
- Alias Stage 2 as `AS runner` (setting `WORKDIR /app` and `CMD ["node", "dist/main.js"]`).
hintsEn: Change the first line to `FROM node:22-alpine AS builder`.
After `RUN npm run build`, start the second stage with `FROM node:22-alpine AS runner`, add `WORKDIR /app`, and keep `CMD ["node", "dist/main.js"]` at the end.

kube-ex-k05-2.titleEn: Copy compiled directories across stages with COPY --from=builder
kube-ex-k05-2.promptEn: In the `runner` stage below, writing `COPY /app/dist ./dist` without `--from` tells Docker to look on the host instead of the `builder` stage! Complete the two `COPY --from=builder` lines in `runner` to copy `/app/node_modules` to `./node_modules` and `/app/dist` to `./dist`.
hintsEn: Place the `--from=builder` flag right after `COPY`.

K06.titleEn: Local Multi-Service Orchestration with Docker Compose v2
K06.summaryEn: Write modern compose.yaml without the version: key, network via service names, persist Postgres data with Named Volumes, and wait for DB readiness with service_healthy.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
A real-world system rarely runs in isolation: your API service (whether written in **FastAPI**, **Node.js**, or **Go**) needs **PostgreSQL 16** to store orders, and **Redis 7** for session storage and background job queues (Celery / BullMQ). If every morning you have to manually type 4 commands to create networks and volumes along with dozens of scattered `-e`, `-p`, and `-v` flags, the team's configurations will quickly drift apart.

**Docker Compose v2** packages the entire multi-container architecture (**services**, **internal DNS networking**, **persistent volumes**, **startup readiness order**) into a single declarative YAML file named ==`compose.yaml`== — the ideal mental stepping stone before moving to Kubernetes Manifest YAML in lesson `K07`!

steps.headingEn: Docker Compose v2 Standard in 2026: Goodbye Legacy Syntax!
steps.bodyEn:
When reading older tutorials from 2018–2021 online, you will encounter syntax from the legacy v1 branch that has been officially deprecated and discontinued. Upgrade immediately to the modern **Compose v2** standard (built directly into **Docker Desktop**, **OrbStack**, and `podman compose`):

```visual

subtitle: "Compose v2 được viết lại hoàn toàn bằng Go và tích hợp sẵn làm plugin chính thức bên trong Docker CLI!"
left:
  badge: "ĐÃ LOẠI BỎ · Compose v1 (2018–2021)"
  title: "Binary rời gạch ngang & Khóa version dư thừa"
  tone: rose
  code: |
    # Tên tệp cũ: docker-compose.yml
    version: "3.8"   # <- Đã bị loại bỏ (obsolete)!
    services:
      api:
        links:       # <- Thủ công lỗi thời
          - postgres
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Công cụ rời `docker-compose` (có dấu gạch ngang của bản v1 cũ) đã ngừng phát triển"
    - "Nếu vẫn cố viết `version: \"3.8\"` ở đầu tệp, Compose v2 sẽ cảnh báo vàng `the attribute 'version' is obsolete`"

  badge: "CHUẨN NĂM 2026 · Docker Compose v2"

  tone: emerald

    # Tên tệp ưu tiên số 1: compose.yaml (KHÔNG có version:)
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
      api:
        build: .
    # Lệnh chuẩn Go plugin: docker compose up -d
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Gọi lệnh ==`docker compose up -d`== (cách nhau bởi dấu cách)"
    - "Tên tệp chuẩn ưu tiên số 1 theo Compose Specification là **`compose.yaml`**"
    - "**Bỏ hoàn toàn khóa `version:`** ở đầu tệp; tự động tạo mạng chung & DNS theo tên dịch vụ"
```

steps.headingEn: Internal DNS Rule: Connect by Service Name Instead of localhost
steps.bodyEn:
> [!WARNING] The trap behind 80% of connection errors for `compose.yaml` beginners
> Inside the `api` container, `localhost` (`127.0.0.1`) **points only to the `api` container's own Network Namespace** — never to your Mac/Windows host and certainly not to the `postgres` container! Setting `DB_HOST: localhost` (or `postgresql://...@localhost:5432` in FastAPI/SQLAlchemy) will inevitably throw **`Connection refused 127.0.0.1:5432`**.

When you run `docker compose up -d`, Compose automatically creates a dedicated Bridge network for the project (for example `myshop_default`) and registers **the exact key names under `services:`** in its internal DNS server:

```yaml compose.yaml — Giao tiếp chuẩn qua Service Name DNS (Đa ngôn ngữ)
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: shop
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: dev-only-placeholder
      POSTGRES_DB: shop_db

  cache-redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine

  api:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      # SAI LẦM KINH ĐIỂN: dùng localhost -> lỗi Connection Refused 127.0.0.1:5432!
      # ĐÚNG CHUẨN: Dùng chính xác tên khóa dưới "services:" làm hostname DNS!
      DB_HOST: postgres
      DB_PORT: "5432"
      REDIS_HOST: cache-redis
      # Nếu api là Python FastAPI / SQLAlchemy, chuỗi kết nối cũng dùng đúng tên dịch vụ:
      DATABASE_URL: "postgresql+psycopg://shop:dev-only-placeholder@postgres:5432/shop_db"
```

steps.headingEn: Persisting Database Data Across down / up Cycles with volumes:
steps.bodyEn:
To prevent PostgreSQL data from vanishing every time you shut down your environment at the end of the day, you must declare it in **2 places** in `compose.yaml`: mount the volume inside the `postgres` service **AND** register the volume name in the **top-level `volumes:`** block at the bottom of the file!

```visual
kind: groups
title: "Bản Đồ Mạng & Vòng Đời Dữ Liệu Trong Docker Compose v2 [!badge:emerald:Cheat Sheet]"
columns: 3
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: globe
    title: "Từ Ngoài Máy Chủ Gọi Vào"
    badge: Dùng localhost + Host Port
    tone: sky
    bullets:
      - "Khi mở trình duyệt hoặc phần mềm DBeaver / TablePlus trên Mac/Windows"
      - "Kết nối qua **`localhost:<HOST_PORT>`** (khi dịch vụ đó có khai báo `ports:`)"
    footer: "Ví dụ: http://localhost:3000"
  - num: 2
    icon: network
    title: "Giữa Hai Container Với Nhau"
    badge: Dùng Service Name + Cổng Nội Bộ
    tone: emerald
    bullets:
      - "Khi `api` hoặc `worker` gọi sang Database / Redis trong cùng mạng Compose"
      - "Bắt buộc dùng ==tên dịch vụ== làm hostname (`postgres:5432`, `cache-redis:6379`)"
    footer: "Không phụ thuộc vào việc DB có mở ports: ra ngoài hay không!"
  - num: 3
    icon: database
    title: "down vs down -v (Cẩn Trọng!)"
    badge: Bảo vệ Named Volume
    tone: amber
    bullets:
      - "**`docker compose down`:** Xóa container & mạng, nhưng **GIỮ AN TOÀN 100%** dữ liệu trong `pgdata`"
      - "**`docker compose down -v`:** **XÓA SẠCH** luôn các Named Volume — chỉ gõ `-v` khi muốn làm mới DB trắng tinh!"
    footer: "Nhớ khai báo pgdata: ở khối volumes: cuối tệp"
```

steps.headingEn: Proper Readiness Startup Order: healthcheck + service_healthy
steps.bodyEn:
If you only write a simple `depends_on: [postgres]`, Compose by default only waits until the `postgres` container process **has just started (`service_started`)**, then immediately launches `api`! Meanwhile, PostgreSQL takes another 2–4 seconds initializing its data files before actually opening port `5432` to accept SQL queries → SQLAlchemy / Prisma in `api` connects too early and crashes immediately!

The production-standard solution is to combine PostgreSQL's built-in ==`pg_isready`== utility with ==`condition: service_healthy`==:

```visual
kind: flow
title: "Trình Tự Khởi Động Không Bao Giờ Sập Với pg_isready & service_healthy"
subtitle: "Đảm bảo API (Python / Node.js) chỉ kết nối sau khi PostgreSQL đã thực sự sẵn sàng nhận câu lệnh SQL trên cổng 5432"
steps:
  - icon: database
    badge: Bước 1 · Bật DB trước
    title: Container postgres Up
    desc: Tiến trình khởi chạy nhưng đang nạp tệp dữ liệu, cổng 5432 chưa sẵn sàng
    code: "starting..."
    tone: sky
    edge: mỗi 5s kiểm tra
  - icon: doctor
    badge: Bước 2 · Kiểm tra sẵn sàng
    title: Chạy lệnh pg_isready
    desc: Tiện ích chuẩn của Postgres kiểm tra trạng thái nhận kết nối thực tế
    code: "pg_isready -U shop"
    tone: amber
    edge: trả về exit 0
  - icon: shield-check
    badge: Bước 3 · Đạt chuẩn
    title: Trạng thái (healthy)
    desc: Docker đánh dấu dịch vụ postgres đã khỏe mạnh hoàn toàn
    code: service_healthy
    tone: emerald
    edge: mở khóa depends_on
  - icon: rocket
    badge: Bước 4 · Khởi chạy êm ái
    title: Bật dịch vụ api
    desc: Prisma / SQLAlchemy kết nối postgres:5432 thành công 100% ngay lần đầu!
    code: "DB_HOST: postgres"
    tone: cyan
```

```yaml compose.yaml hoàn chỉnh chuẩn Production-Ready cho Local Dev
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: shop
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: dev-only-placeholder
      POSTGRES_DB: shop_db
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U shop -d shop_db"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5

  api:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      DB_HOST: postgres
      DB_PORT: "5432"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy   # Chờ tới khi pg_isready báo healthy mới bật api!

volumes:
  pgdata:   # Top-level Named Volume giữ an toàn dữ liệu qua các lần compose down
```

steps.headingEn: Modern Compose v2 Features: develop.watch & profiles
steps.bodyEn:
> [!TIP] Smooth hot-reload for both FastAPI and Node.js with `docker compose watch`
> Instead of using a Bind Mount `- .:/app` that easily wipes out `.venv` or `node_modules` inside the container, `develop.watch` automatically hot-syncs only your source code directory (`./app` or `./src`) into the container whenever you hit `Ctrl+S`, and only triggers an image `rebuild` when you modify `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`!

```visual
kind: groups
title: "Hai Tính Năng Hiện Đại Thay Đổi Trải Nghiệm Dev Năm 2026 [!badge:sky:Compose v2.22+]"
columns: 2
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: refresh
    title: "develop.watch (Thay thế Bind Mount thô bạo)"
    badge: Sync nóng thông minh
    tone: emerald
    bullets:
      - "Tránh hẳn lỗi mount `- .:/app` đè mất `.venv` hoặc `node_modules` biên dịch riêng cho Linux"
      - "**`action: sync`:** Tự chép nóng riêng `./src` (hoặc `./app`) vào container tức thì khi lưu file"
      - "**`action: rebuild`:** Tự build lại Image chỉ khi `package.json` / `pyproject.toml` thay đổi!"
    code: |
      # Bật chế độ theo dõi: docker compose watch
      develop:
        watch:
          - action: sync
            path: ./src
            target: /app/src
          - action: rebuild
            path: package.json
    codeLang: yaml
  - num: 2
    icon: layers
    title: 'profiles: ["debug"] (Bật công cụ theo nhu cầu)'
    badge: Tiết kiệm RAM Laptop
    tone: cyan
    bullets:
      - "Gắn nhãn tùy chọn cho các dịch vụ phụ trợ nặng như **Prometheus, Grafana, pgAdmin**"
      - "Bình thường gõ `docker compose up -d` sẽ **tự động bỏ qua** chúng cho nhẹ máy"
      - "Khi cần đo đạc mới gọi tường minh kèm cờ `--profile debug`"
    code: |
      # Chỉ bật thêm Grafana/Prometheus khi cần thiết:
      docker compose --profile debug up -d
    codeLang: shell
```

> [!REMEMBER] Quick Takeaways
> - **Compose v2 standard (2026)**: file named **`compose.yaml`**, **omit the `version:` key**, run **`docker compose up -d`** (space-separated).
> - Between containers on a Compose network, **always address each other by service name** (`postgres`, `cache-redis`), never `localhost`.
> - **`docker compose down`** preserves Named Volume data (`down -v` deletes it) · Use **`pg_isready`** + **`condition: service_healthy`** so `api` waits until the DB is truly ready.

readings.noteEn: A canonical Fullstack Compose v2 template combining Node.js API + PostgreSQL 16 + Redis 7.
readings.taskEn: Inspect how `api` connects to Postgres/Redis under `environment` and how it ensures it does not start before the databases open their ports.
readings.answerEn: `api` connects via service names `@postgres:5432` and `redis://redis:6379` (without `localhost`), while using `depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy` paired with `pg_isready` and `redis-cli ping`.

readings.noteEn: Spot legacy Compose v1 patterns so you do not copy them by mistake from older articles.
readings.taskEn: Identify 3 outdated details in this `docker-compose-v1.yml` file.
readings.answerEn: 1) Declaring `version: "2.4"` at the top of the file (removed in the modern Compose Spec); 2) Using manual `links:` (Compose networks now resolve DNS automatically by service name); 3) Using list-form `depends_on: [db]` without waiting for `service_healthy`.

readings.noteEn: The modern `docker compose watch` workflow replacing classic Bind Mounts.
readings.taskEn: When does Compose Watch use the `sync` action, and when does it automatically trigger a `rebuild`?
readings.answerEn: When editing code inside `./src`, it performs a fast `sync` of changed files to `/app/src`; when `package.json` or `package-lock.json` changes, it automatically triggers a `rebuild` of the image to install new Linux-compatible dependencies.

K06-Q1.qEn: Under the modern **Docker Compose v2** standard in 2026, which filename, file header, and CLI invocation is the most compliant?
choicesEn: File `docker-compose.yml`, starting with `version: "3.8"`, running `docker-compose up -d`
File `compose.yaml`, **no `version:` key** at the top of the file, running `docker compose up -d` (no hyphen)
File `Composefile.json` and running `npm run compose`
Requires installing Python `pip install docker-compose` before it can run
K06-Q1.explainEn: In Compose v2 (built into the Docker CLI in Go), the command is `docker compose` (space-separated), the preferred filename is `compose.yaml`, and the `version:` key is officially obsolete.

K06-Q2.qEn: In a `compose.yaml` file with two services `api` and `postgres`, what happens at runtime if you set `DB_HOST=localhost` inside `api`'s environment variables?
choicesEn: It connects to `postgres` successfully because both run on your same machine
It fails with `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432` because `localhost` inside the `api` container points to the `api` container itself — it must be changed to `DB_HOST=postgres`
Docker automatically rewrites `localhost` to the IP address of `postgres`
It works on Windows but fails on Linux
K06-Q2.explainEn: Between containers on the same Compose network, always use the **service name (`postgres`)** as the DNS hostname!

K06-Q3.qEn: When you run `docker compose down` (WITHOUT passing the `-v` flag), Docker Compose stops and removes the containers while safely preserving data stored in Named Volumes such as `pgdata`.
K06-Q3.explainEn: Correct! Named Volumes are only deleted when you explicitly pass the `-v` flag (`docker compose down -v` / `--volumes`).

K06-Q4.qEn: Why does a short `depends_on: [postgres]` declaration (without a `healthcheck`) often still cause a Node.js `api` service to crash during simultaneous startup?
choicesEn: Because `depends_on` reverses the startup order (starting `api` before `postgres`)

Because `depends_on` by default only waits until the `postgres` container process starts (`service_started`), not until PostgreSQL finishes initializing and opens port `5432` for connections (`service_healthy`)
Because `depends_on` only supports Redis and not PostgreSQL
Because Compose v2 completely removed the `depends_on` keyword
K06-Q4.explainEn: To ensure `api` starts only after PostgreSQL is genuinely ready to accept SQL queries, combine a `healthcheck` (`pg_isready`) on `postgres` with `depends_on.postgres.condition: service_healthy` on `api`.

K06-Q5.qEn: In the `compose.yaml` below, the `worker` service wants to connect to Redis on port `6379`. What is the correct hostname value to fill into `REDIS_HOST: ____`?
K06-Q5.explainEn: The internal DNS hostname in a Compose network is the exact key name declared under `services:` — in this case `cache-redis`.

K06-Q6.qEn: How does attaching `profiles: ["debug"]` to the `prometheus` and `grafana` services in `compose.yaml` help developers?
choicesEn: It automatically deploys Prometheus to AWS cloud
By default `docker compose up -d` skips starting them to save laptop RAM; only when metrics are needed do you enable them via `docker compose --profile debug up -d`
It enables line-by-line debugging mode for Prometheus's Go source code
It limits Grafana's RAM to 10MB
K06-Q6.explainEn: Compose Profiles let you maintain a single `compose.yaml` with full observability/auxiliary tools without forcing every developer's laptop to run every service all the time.

K06-Q7.qEn: What is the name of the CLI utility included inside the `postgres:16-alpine` image commonly invoked in `healthcheck.test` to verify that the PostgreSQL server is ready to accept connections?
K06-Q7.explainEn: `pg_isready` is the standard utility bundled with PostgreSQL to check connection readiness without opening a heavy query session.

K06-FC1.frontEn: What are the three most recognizable differences of **Docker Compose v2** compared to legacy v1?

K06-FC2.frontEn: On a Docker Compose network, what address does the `api` container use to call the `postgres` container?

K06-FC3.frontEn: What is the difference between `docker compose down` and `docker compose down -v`?
K06-FC3.backEn:
- `docker compose down`: Removes containers & networks, **preserves** Named Volume data.
- `docker compose down -v`: **Deletes Named Volumes as well** (wipes all local DB data!).

K06-FC4.frontEn: What configuration guarantees `api` only starts after `postgres` has actually opened its port to accept connections?
K06-FC4.backEn:
Add a `healthcheck` (`pg_isready`) to `postgres`, and in `api` declare:
```yaml
depends_on:
  postgres:
    condition: service_healthy
```

K06-FC5.frontEn: What are the two mandatory places to declare a Named Volume `pgdata` in `compose.yaml`?
K06-FC5.backEn:
1) Inside the service: `services.postgres.volumes: ["pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data"]`
2) At the top level at the bottom of the file: `volumes: { pgdata: }`

K06-FC6.frontEn: What annoying Bind Mount problem in Node.js projects does `docker compose watch` solve?
K06-FC6.backEn: It hot-syncs only `./src` source code into the container **without overwriting the Linux-built `/app/node_modules`**, while automatically triggering a `rebuild` when `package.json` changes.

kube-ex-k06-1.titleEn: Upgrade to modern v2 compose.yaml (drop version:, declare api & redis)

The `compose.yaml` file below uses an obsolete `version: "3.8"` key and is missing a cache service. Update it so that:
1. The `version` key at the top of the file is **completely removed**.
2. The `api` service uses image `node:22-alpine` and exposes port `"3000:3000"`.
3. A `redis` service is added using image `redis:7-alpine`.

kube-ex-k06-2.titleEn: Fix ECONNREFUSED caused by mistakenly calling localhost between containers
kube-ex-k06-2.promptEn: The `api` application keeps crashing with `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432` and `127.0.0.1:6379` because its environment variables point to `localhost` and `127.0.0.1`. Update `DB_HOST` and `REDIS_HOST` in `services.api.environment` to the proper internal DNS names of the two corresponding services.

kube-ex-k06-3.titleEn: Attach Named Volume pgdata to persist PostgreSQL data
kube-ex-k06-3.promptEn:
Every time a teammate runs `docker compose down`, all database tables in `postgres` get wiped! Protect the data by:
1. Declaring a Named Volume named `pgdata` in the top-level `volumes:` block (at the bottom of the file).
2. Mounting `pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` under the `postgres` service's `volumes:` section.
hintsEn: Inside `postgres:`, add a `volumes:` section containing `- pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`.

At the left margin at the bottom of the file (same level as `services:`), add:
```yaml
volumes:
  pgdata:
```

kube-ex-k06-4.titleEn: Combine pg_isready healthcheck with depends_on service_healthy
kube-ex-k06-4.promptEn:
Upgrade the `compose.yaml` below so `api` never starts before PostgreSQL opens its port for queries:
1. Add a `healthcheck` block to the `postgres` service using the check command `pg_isready -U shop -d shop_db` (e.g., `test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U shop -d shop_db"]`).
2. Change `api`'s `depends_on` to object form requiring `condition: service_healthy` on `postgres`.
hintsEn: Under `postgres`, add `healthcheck:` with `test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U shop -d shop_db"]`, `interval: 5s`, `timeout: 3s`, `retries: 5`.

Under `api`, change `depends_on:` from the array `- postgres` to:

```yaml
depends_on:
  postgres:
    condition: service_healthy
```

kube-ex-k06-5.titleEn: Launch the entire Stack in detached mode using Compose v2 CLI
kube-ex-k06-5.promptEn: The `compose.yaml` file is ready in the project directory. Instead of the deprecated hyphenated v1 command, enter the **Docker Compose v2** command to start the entire service stack in detached mode (`-d`).

K07.titleEn: Kubernetes Architecture, 6-Layer Map, Control Loop & Manifest YAML
K07.summaryEn: Understand when K8s is needed, the Container -> Pod -> Deployment -> Service -> Ingress hierarchy, Control Plane vs Worker Node, Reconciliation Loop, and the 4 root YAML fields.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
In the first 7 lessons (`K00`–`K06`), you mastered packaging and running multiple services on a **single server** with Docker Compose. But what happens when your product scales up to hundreds of thousands of concurrent users?

- [!] Your single server suffers a disk failure or runs out of RAM at 3 AM — who automatically moves 15 containers to another healthy server within seconds without waking an engineer?
- [>] How do you roll out a new version of your payment API across 12 servers simultaneously without dropping a single transaction?

**Kubernetes (`K8s` — the `8` stands for the 8 letters between `K` and `s`)** was built to be the ==Operating System for an entire multi-server cluster==: you simply submit a **desired-state blueprint**, and K8s continuously monitors and self-heals the system 24/7!

steps.headingEn: When You Don't Need Kubernetes Yet, and When You Should Use It
steps.bodyEn:
> [!NOTE] Infrastructure Selection Principles in 2026
> Not every project needs Kubernetes on day one. Choose the tool that fits your actual scale and operational needs:
> - **No K8s needed yet (Single VPS / Small internal project):** **`Docker Compose v2`** on one Linux host easily handles thousands of users with near-zero operational overhead.
> - **No self-managed K8s needed (Startup MVP / Web & AI APIs needing fast autoscaling):** Serverless container platforms such as **`Google Cloud Run`**, **`AWS App Runner`**, or **`Fly.io`** take your Docker image directly and handle HTTPS + autoscaling (even scaling to zero during idle periods).
> - **When Kubernetes truly shines:** Polyglot multi-service systems (Node.js, Python FastAPI, Go, Workers) requiring **multi-host self-healing (`Self-Healing`)**, strict internal routing & firewalling, hardware cost optimization at large scale, and **avoiding single-cloud lock-in (`Cloud-Agnostic`)**.

When entering the K8s world, beginners often feel overwhelmed by all the resource names (`Pod`, `Deployment`, `Service`, `Ingress`...). Look at the **6-Layer Object Hierarchy** below first — you will see every piece click together naturally:


steps.headingEn: Kubernetes Cluster Architecture: Control Plane (Orchestration) and Worker Nodes (Execution)
steps.bodyEn:
```visual
kind: illustration
diagram: "kube:k07"
src: "/illustrations/kube/k8s-control-plane-brain.jpg"
alt: "Kiến trúc tổng thể cụm Kubernetes gồm Control Plane (API Server, etcd, Scheduler, Controller) và Worker Node (kubelet, containerd, kube-proxy)"
title: "Kiến Trúc Cụm Kubernetes: Control Plane (Điều Phối) & Worker Node (Thực Thi)"
subtitle: "Luồng phối hợp giữa cổng trung tâm kube-apiserver, sổ cái etcd, các đại lý trên Node và vòng lặp đối soát trạng thái 24/7"
caption: "Kiến trúc phân tách giữa Control Plane ra quyết định với các Worker Node chạy Pod qua containerd và vòng lặp tự phục hồi Reconciliation Loop"
callouts:
  - num: 1
    label: "Control Plane — Thành phần điều phối & Sổ cái etcd"
    desc: "Mọi thao tác đều đi qua cổng HTTPS duy nhất là kube-apiserver; chỉ thành phần này được phép đọc/ghi trực tiếp vào kho dữ liệu etcd."
    tone: cyan
  - num: 2
    label: "Worker Node — Bộ ba kubelet, containerd & kube-proxy"
    desc: "kubelet nhận chỉ thị từ API Server để ra lệnh cho containerd bật Pod, trong khi kube-proxy duy trì bảng định tuyến mạng trên Node."
    tone: emerald
  - num: 3
    label: "Vòng lặp Đối soát (Reconciliation Loop) 24/7"
    desc: "Controller Manager liên tục so sánh trạng thái thực tế với YAML mong muốn để tự động đẻ bù Pod mới ngay khi có máy chủ gặp sự cố."
    tone: cyan
```

A Kubernetes **Cluster** is always divided into two distinct groups of components: the **Control Plane** (which orchestrates, stores the ledger, and makes scheduling decisions) and **Worker Nodes** (the actual servers providing CPU/RAM to run your application containers). Think of the Control Plane as central operations headquarters, and Worker Nodes as the factory floors executing the work:

```visual
kind: layers
title: "Kiến Trúc Một Cụm Kubernetes Chuẩn — Control Plane vs Worker Nodes"
subtitle: "Nguyên tắc bảo mật cốt lõi: Chỉ duy nhất kube-apiserver được phép đọc/ghi trực tiếp vào kho dữ liệu etcd!"
columns:
  - title: Control Plane (Thành phần điều phối)
    badge: Quản trị & Ra quyết định
    tone: cyan
    layers:
      - label: kube-apiserver
        sub: Cổng giao tiếp REST API (HTTPS) duy nhất của toàn cụm — mọi lệnh kubectl đều gửi YAML/JSON tới đây
        note: Cửa ngõ trung tâm
        tone: sky
      - label: etcd
        sub: Cơ sở dữ liệu phân tán dạng Key-Value lưu nguồn sự thật duy nhất (Single Source of Truth) của cụm
        note: Sổ cái trạng thái
        tone: amber
      - label: kube-scheduler
        sub: Quan sát Pod mới chưa có chỗ (Pending), tính toán CPU/RAM trống rồi gán Pod về Worker Node phù hợp
        note: Người xếp chỗ
        tone: cyan
      - label: kube-controller-manager
        sub: Các vòng lặp tuần tra 24/7 — thấy yêu cầu 3 bản sao mà thực tế còn 2 là lập tức yêu cầu tạo bù bản thứ 3
        note: Tuần tra tự động
        tone: cyan
    footer: Trên Cloud (EKS, GKE, AKS), nhà cung cấp quản lý sẵn toàn bộ Control Plane cho bạn!
  - title: Worker Node (Máy chủ chạy ứng dụng)
    badge: Thực thi Workload
    tone: emerald
    layers:
      - label: kubelet
        sub: Đại lý quản đốc cắm chốt trên từng Worker Node — nhận chỉ thị từ apiserver, báo cáo sức khỏe Node/Pod
        note: Quản đốc tại chỗ
        tone: emerald
      - label: containerd (Container Runtime)
        sub: Bộ máy chuẩn CRI trực tiếp kéo OCI Image và khởi chạy tiến trình Linux Container
        note: Chạy tiến trình
        tone: sky
      - label: kube-proxy (hoặc Cilium eBPF)
        sub: Duy trì bảng định tuyến mạng trên mỗi Node để dẫn gói tin từ Service tới đúng IP của Pod khỏe mạnh
        note: Định tuyến mạng
        tone: cyan
    footer: Có thể co giãn linh hoạt từ 2 máy đến hàng nghìn Worker Node theo tải thực tế
```

steps.headingEn: Core Mechanism of K8s: The Reconciliation Loop
steps.bodyEn:
The ==Reconciliation Loop== is the core mechanism that powers Kubernetes' **Declarative** model: instead of issuing imperative step-by-step commands, you submit a declaration of your **Desired State** (for example `replicas: 3`) into `etcd`. Controllers continuously watch the **Current State** on the cluster — whenever `Current != Desired`, the system automatically creates replacements or adjusts Pods back to the declared state (just like an air conditioner set to `24°C`: a sensor constantly measures room temperature and turns the compressor on/off to maintain `24°C`).

```visual
kind: compare
title: Chuyển Dịch Tư Duy — Mệnh Lệnh (Imperative) vs Khai Báo (Declarative)
subtitle: Sự khác biệt cốt lõi giữa việc tự gõ docker run trên máy lẻ và điều phối tự động bằng Kubernetes
left:
  badge: "CÁCH CŨ · Imperative (Mệnh lệnh)"
  title: Ra lệnh từng bước thủ công
  tone: amber
  code: |
    # Bắt máy chủ làm ngay hành động này 1 lần:
    docker run -d --name shop-api -p 3000:3000 app:1.0
  lang: bash
  bullets:
    - "Bạn chỉ định **cách làm từng bước**: chạy lệnh xong là CLI kết thúc trách nhiệm"
    - "Nếu 2 giờ sáng ổ cứng máy chủ hỏng làm sập tiến trình, **không ai tự chuyển sang máy khác**"
    - "Sửa tay lâu ngày dẫn đến lệch cấu hình (*Configuration Drift*)"
right:
  badge: "CHUẨN K8S · Declarative (Khai báo)"
  title: Giao trạng thái đích cho Vòng lặp Đối soát
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    # Nộp bản thiết kế trạng thái mong muốn:
    kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml   # replicas: 3
  lang: bash
  bullets:
    - "Bạn chỉ mô tả **trạng thái mong muốn** (`Desired State: replicas: 3`) trong tệp YAML lưu trên Git"
    - "Controller chạy vòng lặp đối soát liên tục 24/7 với **trạng thái hiện tại** (`Current State`)"
    - "Tự động chữa lành (**Self-Healing**): hễ `Current != Desired` là tự tạo bù Pod sang Node khỏe mạnh!"
```

```visual
kind: flow
title: Vòng Lặp Đối Soát Tự Phục Hồi (Reconciliation / Control Loop)
subtitle: Điều gì diễn ra tự động lúc 3 giờ sáng khi Worker Node #2 bất ngờ mất điện?
steps:
  - icon: file-code
    badge: 1. Desired State
    title: Khai Báo Đích
    desc: Bạn nộp YAML yêu cầu duy trì replicas là 3 vào etcd qua kube-apiserver
    code: "replicas: 3"
    tone: sky
    edge: quan sát 24/7
  - icon: eye
    badge: 2. Observe & Diff
    title: Phát Hiện Lệch
    desc: Node #2 sập làm chết 1 Pod — Controller thấy thực tế chỉ còn 2 Pod sống
    code: "Current (2) != Desired (3)"
    tone: amber
    edge: tạo bù 1 Pod
  - icon: cpu
    badge: 3. Schedule
    title: Xếp Chỗ Mới
    desc: kube-scheduler tìm thấy Node #3 còn dư CPU/RAM và gán Pod mới sang đó
    code: "Pending -> Node #3"
    tone: cyan
    edge: kubelet kéo Image
  - icon: shield-check
    badge: 4. Self-Healing
    title: Hội Tụ Đủ Quân Số
    desc: kubelet trên Node #3 bảo containerd bật Pod mới — dịch vụ lành lặn 100%
    code: "2 + 1 === 3 Ready"
    tone: emerald
```

steps.headingEn: Four Mandatory Root Fields in Every Kubernetes YAML Manifest
steps.bodyEn:
Whether you write a tiny 12-line `Pod` or a large 200-line `Deployment`, **100% of standard Kubernetes resources** start with the exact same ==4 root fields (`apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata`, `spec`)== at the left margin:

```visual
kind: anatomy
title: Cấu Trúc 4 Trường Gốc Trong Mọi Manifest YAML Của Kubernetes
subtitle: Khác với Docker Compose (services/volumes), mọi đối tượng K8s đều tuân thủ khuôn mẫu 4 khóa gốc đồng nhất này
items:
  - keyword: apiVersion
    role: Nhóm & Phiên bản API
    tone: sky
    summary: Xác định nhóm chuẩn API mà kube-apiserver dùng để kiểm tra lược đồ tài nguyên.
    bullets:
      - "Nhóm cốt lõi (`Pod`, `Service`, `ConfigMap`, `Secret`, `Namespace`, `PersistentVolumeClaim`): dùng **`v1`**"
      - "Nhóm quản lý workload (`Deployment`, `StatefulSet`, `DaemonSet`, `ReplicaSet`): dùng ==`apps/v1`=="
    example: "apiVersion: apps/v1"
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: kind
    role: Loại đối tượng
    tone: cyan
    summary: Tên kiểu tài nguyên Kubernetes mà bạn muốn khởi tạo hoặc cập nhật (viết PascalCase).
    bullets:
      - "Ví dụ phổ biến: `Pod`, `Deployment`, `Service`, `Ingress`, `ConfigMap`, `Secret`"
    example: "kind: Deployment"
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: metadata
    role: Định danh & Nhãn
    tone: amber
    summary: Chứa tên định danh (`name`), không gian tên (`namespace`) và bộ nhãn phân loại (`labels`).
    bullets:
      - "Nếu bỏ trống `metadata.namespace`, tài nguyên mặc định rơi vào namespace `default`"
    example: "metadata:\n  name: hello-k8s\n  labels:\n    app: hello-k8s"
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: spec
    role: Đặc tả trạng thái đích
    tone: emerald
    summary: Mô tả chi tiết trạng thái mong muốn (Desired State) mà bạn giao cho K8s duy trì.
    bullets:
      - "Cấu trúc bên trong `spec` thay đổi tùy theo từng `kind` (ví dụ `containers` cho Pod, `replicas` + `selector` + `template` cho Deployment)"
    example: "spec:\n  containers:\n    - name: web\n      image: nginx:1.27-alpine"
    lang: yaml
```

```yaml Manifest Pod tối giản hoàn chỉnh (chuẩn v1)
apiVersion: v1              # 1. Nhóm và phiên bản API (v1, apps/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1...)
kind: Pod                   # 2. Loại đối tượng muốn tạo (Pod, Deployment, Service, Secret...)
metadata:                   # 3. Định danh: tên (name), không gian tên (namespace), nhãn (labels)
  name: hello-k8s
  labels:
    app: hello-k8s
spec:                       # 4. Đặc tả trạng thái mong muốn (cấu trúc bên trong tùy thuộc vào kind)
  containers:
    - name: web
      image: nginx:1.27-alpine
      ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

> [!WARNING] Legacy API Version Trap (K8s >= 1.30 standard in 2026)
> Many older pre-2020 tutorials still show the legacy draft group `extensions/v1beta1` for `Deployment` or `Ingress` — that draft API **was removed completely from Kubernetes long ago**!
> - For `Pod`, `Service`, `ConfigMap`, `Secret`, `Namespace`, `PersistentVolumeClaim`: always use **`apiVersion: v1`**.
> - For `Deployment`, `StatefulSet`, `DaemonSet`, `ReplicaSet`: always use **`apiVersion: apps/v1`** (and explicitly declare `spec.selector.matchLabels`).

steps.headingEn: First kubectl Commands & 2026 Local Cluster / TUI Toolkit
steps.bodyEn:
`kubectl` is the CLI remote control that talks directly to `kube-apiserver` over HTTPS:

```bash
# 1. Liệt kê Pod ở namespace mặc định (default):
kubectl get pods

# 2. Liệt kê TẤT CẢ Pod trên mọi namespace toàn cụm (gồm cả kube-system nơi coredns đang chạy):
kubectl get pods -A

# 3. Xem chi tiết trạng thái và sự kiện (Events) của Pod:
kubectl describe pod payment-pod
```

> [!TIP] Modern 2026 K8s Toolkit to Work 5x Faster!
> - **Spin up a free K8s cluster right on your laptop:** Use **`kind`** (*Kubernetes in Docker* — creates a multi-node cluster in 20 seconds inside Docker/OrbStack), **`minikube`**, or **`k3s`** (CNCF's ultra-lightweight K8s distribution using under 512MB RAM, ideal for small servers & Edge).
> - **Every SRE's Terminal Trio:** Install **`k9s`** (an interactive TUI dashboard right in your terminal to inspect logs/describe/shell with a single shortcut) along with **`kubectx`** & **`kubens`** (switch instantly between clusters and namespaces without repeatedly typing `-n`)!

> [!REMEMBER] Quick Takeaways
> - **What to use when:** 1 small server → `Docker Compose` · Serverless autoscaling → `Cloud Run / Fly.io` · Multi-service with multi-node self-healing → **Kubernetes**.
> - **6-layer chain:** `Container` → `Pod` → `ReplicaSet` → `Deployment` → `Service` → `Ingress / Gateway API`.
> - **Control Plane:** `kube-apiserver` (only gateway touching `etcd`), `etcd`, `kube-scheduler`, `kube-controller-manager` · **4 YAML root fields:** ==`apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata`, `spec`==.

readings.noteEn: Observe the 4 mandatory root fields (apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec) in a canonical Pod Manifest.
readings.taskEn: Identify the values of `apiVersion` and `kind` in this file, and explain why `metadata.labels` is separated from `spec`?
readings.answerEn: The file uses `apiVersion: v1` and `kind: Pod`. `metadata` holds object identification and classification info (such as `name`, `namespace`, `labels`), whereas `spec` describes the desired operational state of that resource (container image, ports, CPU/RAM limits).

readings.noteEn: Spot the deprecated draft API extensions/v1beta1 that has been removed from modern Kubernetes.
readings.taskEn: If you submit this file as-is to a Kubernetes 1.30+ cluster, what error occurs and which 2 things must be fixed to make it valid?
readings.answerEn: The API Server throws `no matches for kind "Deployment" in version "extensions/v1beta1"`. You must change `apiVersion` to `apps/v1` and add the required `spec.selector.matchLabels` matching `spec.template.metadata.labels`.

K07-Q1.qEn: In the Kubernetes Control Plane, which component serves as the distributed Key-Value database storing the entire state of the cluster?
choicesEn: `kube-proxy`
`etcd`
`kubelet`
`containerd`
K07-Q1.explainEn: `etcd` is the single source of truth for the entire K8s cluster, and only `kube-apiserver` is allowed to read from and write to `etcd` directly.

K07-Q2.qEn: On each **Worker Node**, which agent receives directives from `kube-apiserver` to instruct the Container Runtime to pull images and start Pods scheduled onto that Node?
choicesEn: `kube-scheduler`
`kubelet`
`etcd`
`kube-controller-manager`
K07-Q2.explainEn: `kubelet` runs on every Worker Node, continuously reports Node/Pod health back to `kube-apiserver`, and instructs `containerd` to start/stop containers.

K07-Q3.qEn: Under the Declarative Control Loop model, if you declare `replicas: 3` and 1 Worker Node loses power causing 1 Pod to die, Kubernetes automatically creates 1 replacement Pod on a healthy Worker Node to restore the count to 3.
K07-Q3.explainEn: Correct! Controllers continuously compare Actual State (`2`) against Desired State (`3`) and create a new Pod, which `kube-scheduler` assigns to a healthy Node.

K07-Q4.qEn: What are the four mandatory root fields required in every standard Kubernetes resource Manifest YAML?
choicesEn: `version`, `services`, `networks`, `volumes`
`apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata`, `spec`
`from`, `workdir`, `copy`, `cmd`
`name`, `on`, `jobs`, `steps`
K07-Q4.explainEn: `version`/`services` belong to Docker Compose; `name`/`on`/`jobs` belong to GitHub Actions; every standard Kubernetes Manifest is structured around `apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata`, `spec`.

K07-Q5.qEn: In modern Kubernetes (v1.16 through 2026), what is the standard `apiVersion` value for `kind: Deployment` (replacing the removed `extensions/v1beta1`)?
K07-Q5.explainEn: All workload management resources such as `Deployment`, `StatefulSet`, `DaemonSet`, and `ReplicaSet` belong to the stable `apps/v1` API group.

K07-Q6.qEn: When you run `kubectl get pods` with no extra flags, why don't you see system Pods like `coredns`?
choicesEn: Because `coredns` does not run as a Pod
Because `kubectl get pods` defaults to listing resources in the `default` namespace, whereas `coredns` lives in the `kube-system` namespace (use `-n kube-system` or `-A`)
Because you must SSH into the Control Plane machine to see them
Because `coredns` only runs when there is a network error
K07-Q6.explainEn: By default `kubectl` queries the `default` namespace. Passing `-A` (`--all-namespaces`) displays all Pods across every namespace in the cluster.

K07-Q7.qEn: What is the single-uppercase-letter shorthand flag (including the dash) in `kubectl get pods ____` to list Pods across **all namespaces**?
K07-Q7.explainEn: `-A` is shorthand for `--all-namespaces`, extremely handy for getting a cluster-wide overview in 1 second.

K07-FC1.frontEn: What are the four main components inside the Kubernetes **Control Plane**?

K07-FC2.frontEn: What are the three main components running on each **Worker Node**?

K07-FC3.frontEn: What are the four mandatory root fields in a Kubernetes YAML Manifest?

K07-FC4.frontEn: What is the core meaning of the **Reconciliation / Control Loop** in Kubernetes?
K07-FC4.backEn: Continuously observe **Actual State**, compare it with **Desired State** (declared in YAML), and automatically take corrective actions so the two always match.

K07-FC5.frontEn: What is the difference between `kubectl get pod X` and `kubectl describe pod X`?
K07-FC5.backEn:
- `get`: Displays a 1-line summary status table.
- `describe`: Displays a detailed profile including assigned Node, IP, Volumes, and especially the **`Events:`** history table at the bottom to diagnose errors.

K07-FC7.frontEn: What is the 6-layer hierarchy from inside out for a Web/API application on Kubernetes?
K07-FC7.backEn: **`Container`** → **`Pod`** (shared-localhost shell) → **`ReplicaSet`** (replica counter) → **`Deployment`** (rolling releases) → **`Service`** (internal IP/DNS switchboard) → **`Ingress / Gateway API`** (HTTPS gateway).
