K08.summaryEn: Understand the Pod isolation boundary sharing localhost, organize resources with Labels, separate environments with Namespaces, and authenticate private Registries via imagePullSecrets.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
When transitioning from Docker to Kubernetes, the first question almost every developer (**Python, Node.js, Go...**) asks is: *"Why doesn't Kubernetes just manage individual Containers directly instead of wrapping them inside a **Pod**?"*

Understanding the shared networking architecture of a ==Pod==, **Labels** for grouping, **Namespaces** for isolation, and `imagePullSecrets` for registry authentication will give you a rock-solid grasp of Kubernetes' fundamental unit of execution.

```visual
kind: illustration
diagram: "kube:k08"
alt: "Không gian mạng chia sẻ localhost bên trong Pod (Main + Sidecar), cơ chế khớp nhãn Labels/Selectors và ranh giới Namespace"
title: "Kiến Trúc Pod Sandbox, Cơ Chế Labels/Selectors & Phân Vùng Namespace"
subtitle: "Cách các container trong cùng 1 Pod chia sẻ địa chỉ IP/localhost và cách toàn cụm liên kết lỏng qua hệ thống nhãn động"
caption: "Cấu trúc không gian cô lập của Pod chia sẻ Network Namespace & ổ đĩa emptyDir, bộ lọc chọn lọc theo nhãn và ranh giới phân tách tài nguyên giữa các Namespace"
callouts:
  - num: 1
    label: "Pod Sandbox — Dùng chung IP & Loopback localhost"
    desc: "Container chính và Sidecar chia sẻ cùng một Network Namespace nên gọi nhau thẳng qua 127.0.0.1 và dùng chung ổ đĩa tạm emptyDir."
    tone: emerald
  - num: 2
    label: "Labels & Selectors — Cơ chế liên kết lỏng"
    desc: "Thay vì trỏ vào tên Pod ngẫu nhiên hay đổi, Service và Deployment quét tìm đúng nhóm Pod thông qua các cặp nhãn key: value."
    tone: sky
  - num: 3
    label: "Namespace — Ranh giới phạm vi tên & hạn mức"
    desc: "Tách biệt môi trường staging và production trên cùng một cụm vật lý; ConfigMap và Secret không tự động chia sẻ xuyên qua Namespace."
    tone: cyan
```

steps.headingEn: Why Is the Smallest Unit in K8s a Pod Instead of a Container?
steps.bodyEn:
> [!NOTE] Pod: The Smallest Deployable Unit in Kubernetes
> A **Pod** is a group of one or more containers deployed together on a single Worker Node, sharing one **Network Namespace** (same IP address and `localhost`) and optionally sharing temporary storage volumes (`emptyDir`):
> - In **95% of real-world cases**, a Pod wraps **exactly 1 main container** (such as your FastAPI or Node.js API).
> - In **5% of advanced cases**, the main application needs an auxiliary helper process called a **Sidecar Container** (such as a Fluent Bit log shipper, Envoy encryption proxy, or Cloud SQL Auth Proxy). Because they live in the same Pod, these two containers communicate via `localhost` and read shared files on local disk without routing out over the external network (the name *Pod* — like a pea pod — reflects wrapping one or more tightly coupled containers together).

```visual
kind: layers
title: Không Gian Chia Sẻ Bên Trong Cùng Một Pod vs Hai Pod Khác Nhau
subtitle: Mọi container trong cùng một Pod dùng chung Network Namespace (chung IP & localhost) và không được mở trùng cổng!
columns:
  - title: Bên Trong Cùng 1 Pod (Main + Sidecar)
    badge: Chung IP · Gọi qua localhost
    tone: emerald
    layers:
      - label: Container Chính (api :3000/:8000) + Sidecar (log-shipper)
        sub: Sidecar gọi thẳng localhost:3000 — hai container chung Pod KHÔNG ĐƯỢC mở trùng cùng một số cổng!
        note: Phối hợp sát sườn
        tone: emerald
      - label: Chung một Network Namespace (1 Địa chỉ IP + Loopback 127.0.0.1)
        sub: Toàn bộ container trong vỏ Pod chia sẻ cùng một địa chỉ IP nội bộ và một bảng cổng mạng duy nhất
        note: Không cần qua mạng ngoài
        tone: sky
      - label: Chung ổ đĩa tạm (Shared Volume emptyDir)
        sub: Container chính ghi tệp tạm ra đĩa, Sidecar đọc và xử lý ngay ở tốc độ ổ cứng cục bộ
        note: Chia sẻ tệp tức thì
        tone: cyan
    footer: Đơn vị nguyên tử nhỏ nhất được kube-scheduler xếp chỗ lên cùng một Worker Node
  - title: Hai Pod Khác Nhau Trên Cụm
    badge: Khác IP hoàn toàn · Cô lập mạng
    tone: cyan
    layers:
      - label: Pod A (shop-web — IP 10.244.1.12:80)
        sub: Sở hữu Network Namespace riêng, có thể mở cổng 80 hoặc 3000 hoàn toàn độc lập với Pod khác
        note: Vỏ Pod độc lập #1
        tone: cyan
      - label: Pod B (payment-api — IP 10.244.2.35:8000)
        sub: Có địa chỉ IP riêng biệt hoàn toàn — không bao giờ gọi sang Pod A qua localhost được
        note: Vỏ Pod độc lập #2
        tone: amber
      - label: Mạng ảo toàn cụm (Cluster CNI + Service DNS)
        sub: Hai Pod khác nhau giao tiếp thông qua mạng cụm (thực tế luôn gọi qua tên miền Service ổn định)
        note: Kết nối qua Service
        tone: slate
    footer: Có thể nằm trên cùng một Worker Node hoặc rải sang hai Worker Node khác nhau
```

```yaml Manifest Pod chuẩn đính kèm nhãn phân loại (metadata.labels)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: shop-web
  labels:
    app: shop-web
    tier: frontend
spec:
  containers:
    - name: nginx
      image: nginx:1.27-alpine
      ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

steps.headingEn: Labels & Selectors: Loose Coupling Between Kubernetes Objects
steps.bodyEn:
On a Kubernetes cluster running 500 diverse Pods (React Frontend, Node.js Order API, Python Recommendation AI, Redis...), Kubernetes **does not use hardcoded lists of names** to group them, because auto-generated Pod names change constantly on every update (`shop-api-7d9f8b-xk2lp`). Instead, K8s uses ==`metadata.labels`== — key-value tags (`key: value`) for dynamic querying:

```visual
kind: groups
title: Ba Chiều Nhãn (Labels) Phổ Biến & Cách Toàn Cụm Truy Vấn Chúng
subtitle: Labels + Selectors là cơ chế kết nối lỏng trung tâm giúp Service, Deployment và NetworkPolicy tìm đúng Pod
columns: 3
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: network
    title: "app (hoặc app.kubernetes.io/name)"
    badge: Định danh dịch vụ
    tone: sky
    bullets:
      - "Ví dụ giá trị: `shop-api`, `ai-recommender`, `redis`"
      - "**`Service`** dùng nhãn này để tìm các Pod nhận chia tải HTTP"
      - "**`Deployment`** dùng nhãn này để điểm danh đủ quân số bản sao"
  - num: 2
    icon: shield
    title: tier
    badge: Phân tầng kiến trúc
    tone: cyan
    bullets:
      - "Ví dụ giá trị: `frontend`, `backend`, `cache`"
      - "**`NetworkPolicy`** dựa vào đây để khóa tường lửa nội bộ (chỉ cho tầng `backend` gọi vào `cache`)"
  - num: 3
    icon: search
    title: env
    badge: Lọc theo môi trường
    tone: emerald
    bullets:
      - "Ví dụ giá trị: `dev`, `staging`, `production`"
      - "Lọc siêu tốc trên CLI bằng cờ `-l`:"
    code: |
      kubectl get pods -l env=staging,tier=backend
    codeLang: bash
```

> [!WARNING] `labels` Are NOT Mere Decoration!
> A single typo in `metadata.labels` (e.g., typing `app: shop-backned` instead of `app: shop-backend`) will immediately cause **`Service` to lose all connections to the Pod**!

steps.headingEn: Namespaces: Logical Resource Partitioning Inside a Cluster
steps.bodyEn:
If two project teams (`team-a` and `team-b`) or two environments (`staging` and `production`) share one physical cluster, how can both create a `Service` named `api-svc` without overwriting each other? The answer is **Namespaces** — independent logical scopes inside the same cluster (analogous to separate departments or zones within a single organization):

```visual
kind: groups
title: Phân Vùng Cụm Bằng Namespaces — Tránh Đụng Độ Tên & Khóa Hạn Ngạch
columns: 3
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: box
    title: default
    badge: Mặc định ban đầu
    tone: slate
    bullets:
      - "Không gian mặc định khi bạn không truyền cờ `-n` hoặc không khai báo `metadata.namespace`"
      - "Tiện cho việc học nhanh trên máy local, nhưng hạn chế nhét mọi dịch vụ Production chung vào đây"
  - num: 2
    icon: settings
    title: kube-system
    badge: Thành phần hệ thống
    tone: rose
    bullets:
      - "Nơi chạy các thành phần cốt lõi như **`coredns`**, **`kube-proxy`**, CNI mạng"
      - "**Tuyệt đối không** triển khai ứng dụng kinh doanh vào `kube-system`!"
  - num: 3
    icon: layers
    title: "Namespace Tự Tạo (staging, payments...)"
    badge: Chuẩn đa đội dự án
    tone: emerald
    bullets:
      - "Tên `Pod`, `Deployment`, `Service`, `ConfigMap`, `Secret` **chỉ cần duy nhất trong phạm vi 1 Namespace**"
      - "Dễ dàng áp hạn ngạch tổng CPU/RAM (`ResourceQuota`) và phân quyền RBAC riêng cho từng đội"
```

When combining multiple related resources into **a single YAML file**, we use a line of ==three dashes `---`== to separate the documents:

```yaml Gộp Namespace và Pod trong cùng 1 tệp YAML bằng dấu phân tách ---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: staging
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: worker-pod
  namespace: staging
spec:
  containers:
    - name: worker
      image: python:3.12-slim
      command: ["python", "-c", "import time; time.sleep(3600)"]
```

On the command line for quick testing, you can create a Namespace and run a Pod with the `-n` flag:

```bash
kubectl create ns payments
kubectl run fraud-check --image=node:22-alpine -n payments
```

> [!TIP] Save Hundreds of `-n payments` Keystrokes with `kubens`
> In daily work, you can switch your session's default Namespace straight to `payments` with `kubens payments` (or `kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=payments`), and pair it with `k9s` to inspect Pods visually per Namespace!

steps.headingEn: Pulling Images from a Private Registry with imagePullSecrets
steps.bodyEn:
Public images like `python:3.12-slim` or `node:22-alpine` can be pulled by anyone, but your company's product images always live in a private registry (**GitHub Container Registry `ghcr.io`**, **AWS ECR**, **Google Artifact Registry**, **Harbor**). Without credentials, the Pod gets stuck in ==`ErrImagePull` / `ImagePullBackOff`== (`401 Unauthorized`).

```visual
kind: flow
title: Quy Trình 2 Bước Xác Thực Kéo Image Riêng Tư Không Dính ImagePullBackOff
steps:
  - icon: key
    badge: Bước 1 · Tạo Secret
    title: Secret dockerconfigjson
    desc: Tạo Secret kiểu kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson chứa thông tin đăng nhập Registry
    code: "name: regcred"
    tone: amber
    edge: gắn vào Pod spec
  - icon: file-code
    badge: Bước 2 · Đính kèm
    title: spec.imagePullSecrets
    desc: Tham chiếu tên Secret vào mảng imagePullSecrets của Pod hoặc Deployment template
    code: "imagePullSecrets: [regcred]"
    tone: sky
    edge: kubelet xác thực
  - icon: container
    badge: Bước 3 · Tải thành công
    title: Running Container
    desc: kubelet gửi thông tin xác thực tới Private Registry, kéo Image mượt mà và khởi chạy Pod
    code: "1/1 Running"
    tone: emerald
```

```yaml Đính kèm spec.imagePullSecrets để kéo Image nội bộ
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: shop-private-api
spec:
  imagePullSecrets:
    - name: regcred
  containers:
    - name: api
      image: private.registry.local/shop/api:1.4.2
```

> [!REMEMBER] Quick Takeaways
> - Containers inside **the same Pod** share the same IP + `localhost` + port table (cannot bind duplicate ports!) and can share `emptyDir` volumes.
> - **`metadata.labels`** are loose-coupling tags so `Service`, `Deployment`, and `NetworkPolicy` target the right Pods; **`---`** separates multiple resources in a single YAML file.
> - Forgetting private Registry credentials causes **`ErrImagePull` / `ImagePullBackOff`** — fix it with ==`spec.imagePullSecrets`== referencing a `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` Secret.

readings.noteEn: Industry-standard labeling and image version pinning on a Pod.
readings.taskEn: Look at the `ports` section of container `api`: besides `containerPort: 3000`, how does adding `name: http` help other resources?
readings.answerEn: Naming the port (`name: http`) allows a `Service` or `readinessProbe` to reference it by name `port: http` instead of hardcoding `3000` — if the Pod's port later changes to `8080`, the `Service` manifest does not need to be edited.

readings.noteEn: Direct impact of separating Namespaces on inter-service network addresses.
readings.taskEn: Why can `CART_SERVICE_URL` within the same K8s cluster be written shortly as `cart-api`, whereas `DB_HOST` must be written in full as `postgres-primary.database.svc.cluster.local`?
readings.answerEn: `cart-api` resides in the same `storefront` namespace so the short name resolves directly; `postgres-primary` resides in a separate `database` namespace, so the fully qualified domain name including the namespace is required.

K08-Q1.qEn: If a `Pod` contains 2 containers (main container `api` listening on port `3000` and Sidecar container `log-shipper`), how do these two containers communicate over the network?
choicesEn: They must route out to the Internet through an Ingress
They share a single Network Namespace, so they have the same IP address and call each other directly over `localhost:3000`
They are never permitted to communicate with each other
You must create 2 separate cloud LoadBalancers
K08-Q1.explainEn: All containers within the same Pod share a single network namespace (IP + loopback `127.0.0.1`), so they reach each other via `localhost` and cannot bind the same port number.

K08-Q2.qEn: What is the primary role of `metadata.labels` on a Pod in Kubernetes?
choicesEn: Purely to display decorative colors in the Dashboard UI
To act as key-value identifying tags so `Service`, `Deployment`, and `NetworkPolicy` can dynamically query and group their target Pods
To store encrypted Database passwords
To determine the Pod's maximum RAM capacity
K08-Q2.explainEn: Labels + Selectors are Kubernetes' central loose-coupling mechanism: Services locate traffic-receiving Pods via labels, and Deployments count replicas via labels.

K08-Q3.qEn: Two different project teams can safely create a `Service` with the same name `api-svc` on the same Kubernetes cluster, as long as they place them in two separate `Namespaces` (for example `team-a` and `team-b`).
K08-Q3.explainEn: Correct! Resource names for most objects (`Pod`, `Deployment`, `Service`, `ConfigMap`, `Secret`) only need to be unique within a single `Namespace`.

K08-Q4.qEn: When combining multiple Kubernetes resources (e.g., 1 `Namespace` and 1 `Pod`) into **a single YAML file**, which 3-character sequence on its own line separates the documents?
K08-Q4.explainEn: Three dashes `---` is the standard document separator in the YAML specification (multi-document YAML stream).

K08-Q5.qEn: A Pod needs to pull an internal image `private.registry.local/shop/api:1.4.2` without declaring Registry credentials. Which error status will appear in the `STATUS` column of `kubectl get pods`?
choicesEn: `OOMKilled`
`ErrImagePull` / `ImagePullBackOff`
`Completed`
`Terminating`
K08-Q5.explainEn: When `kubelet` is denied permission to pull the image (or given an invalid tag), the Pod enters `ErrImagePull` and then backs off retries with `ImagePullBackOff`.

K08-Q6.qEn: Which field in a `Pod` spec attaches a Secret containing Private Registry login credentials?
choicesEn: `spec.envFrom`
`spec.imagePullSecrets`
`metadata.annotations`
`spec.volumes`
K08-Q6.explainEn: `spec.imagePullSecrets: [{ name: "regcred" }]` supplies `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` credentials to `kubelet` during the image pull step before creating containers.

K08-Q7.qEn: Two containers running in **the same Pod** can both bind and listen on port `3000` on `0.0.0.0` at the same time without a port conflict.
K08-Q7.explainEn: False! Because containers in the same Pod share a single Network Namespace (same IP and port table), two processes cannot both bind port `3000` inside the same Pod.

K08-FC1.frontEn: What do containers living inside **the same Pod** share with one another?
K08-FC1.backEn: They share a single **Network Namespace** (same IP address, communicate via `localhost`) and can mount shared Volumes (`emptyDir`, `PVC`).

K08-FC2.frontEn: What is the `kubectl` syntax to filter Pods by label `env=staging`?

K08-FC3.frontEn: What symbol separates multiple Kubernetes resources within a single `.yaml` file?

K08-FC4.frontEn: What lives in the `kube-system` Namespace, and should you deploy your own apps there?
K08-FC4.backEn: Core cluster components (`coredns`, `kube-proxy`, CNI...). **Never** deploy user applications into `kube-system`.

K08-FC5.frontEn: How do you allow a Pod to pull images from a Private Registry (GHCR, ECR, Harbor)?
K08-FC5.backEn: Create a Secret of type `kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson` and reference it in the Pod via **`spec.imagePullSecrets: [{ name: "<secret-name>" }]`**.

K08-FC6.frontEn: What is the CLI command to quickly create a Namespace named `payments`?
K08-FC6.backEn: **`kubectl create namespace payments`** (or shorthand `kubectl create ns payments`).

kube-ex-k08-1.titleEn: Write Pod shop-web with a pinned Image version and containerPort
kube-ex-k08-1.promptEn:
Complete the `shop-web` `Pod` Manifest so that:
1. Instead of `:latest`, explicitly pin `image: nginx:1.27-alpine` for the first container.
2. Declare the exposed port at `spec.containers[0].ports[0].containerPort: 80`.
hintsEn: Change `image: nginx:latest` to `image: nginx:1.27-alpine`.

Directly under the `image:` line, add:
```yaml
      ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

kube-ex-k08-2.titleEn: Add standard classification labels (app, tier, env) to metadata.labels
kube-ex-k08-2.promptEn:
So that `Service` and `NetworkPolicy` can identify Pod `shop-api-pod`, add a `metadata.labels` block containing all 3 standard labels:
- `app: shop-api`
- `tier: backend`
- `env: staging`
hintsEn: `labels:` goes inside `metadata:`, indented 2 spaces aligned with `name:`.
Inside `labels:`, indent 4 spaces for `app: shop-api`, `tier: backend`, and `env: staging`.

kube-ex-k08-3.titleEn: Multi-Document YAML: Create Namespace staging and place a Pod inside it
kube-ex-k08-3.promptEn:
Use the `---` separator in a single YAML file to declare 2 resources together:
1. A `Namespace` (`apiVersion: v1`, `kind: Namespace`) with `metadata.name: staging`.
2. A `Pod` named `worker-pod` placed inside `metadata.namespace: staging`, running image `node:22-alpine`.
hintsEn: The `Namespace` resource does not need a `spec:` field — only `apiVersion: v1`, `kind: Namespace`, and `metadata: { name: staging }`.
On the `Pod` resource below `---`, don't forget to add `namespace: staging` inside `metadata:`!

kube-ex-k08-4.titleEn: Create Namespace payments and launch a Pod via kubectl CLI
kube-ex-k08-4.promptEn:
Using two `kubectl` commands in the Terminal:
1. Create a new Namespace named `payments`.
2. Launch a Pod named `fraud-check` using image `node:22-alpine` inside the `payments` namespace (`-n payments`).
hintsEn: Create the namespace with `kubectl create ns payments` (or `kubectl create namespace payments`).
Create the Pod with `kubectl run fraud-check --image=node:22-alpine -n payments`.

kube-ex-k08-5.titleEn: Attach imagePullSecrets to pull Images from a Private Registry
kube-ex-k08-5.promptEn: A Registry authentication Secret named `regcred` already exists on the cluster. However, Pod `shop-private-api` below pulling internal image `private.registry.local/shop/api:1.4.2` is failing with `ImagePullBackOff` because it forgot to attach that Secret. Add `spec.imagePullSecrets` referencing `name: regcred`.
hintsEn: `imagePullSecrets` is an array placed directly under `spec:` (at the same level as `containers:`).

Syntax:
```yaml
  imagePullSecrets:
    - name: regcred
```

K09.summaryEn: Manage self-healing Pod lifecycles with Deployment and ReplicaSet, match selector.matchLabels, configure zero-downtime RollingUpdate strategies, and revert to previous versions using rollout undo.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
In lesson `K08`, you learned how to write a standalone `Pod`. However, there is an ironclad rule in real-world operations: ==in Production, never deploy applications as bare Pods (`naked Pods`)!==

To turn fragile Pods into a resilient service capable of **auto-recovering when a node crashes**, **scaling across multiple replicas**, and **upgrading to new versions without dropping traffic (`Zero-Downtime`)**, we delegate guardianship to a **`Deployment`** (`apiVersion: apps/v1`).

steps.headingEn: Three-Tier Hierarchy: Deployment → ReplicaSet → Pod
steps.bodyEn:
> [!NOTE] Roles of the 3 tiers: Deployment, ReplicaSet, and Pod
> Many newcomers wonder why a `Deployment` doesn't create `Pod` objects directly, instead placing a **`ReplicaSet`** in between. Each layer has a distinct responsibility:
> - **`Pod`:** The execution unit containing the application container (FastAPI, Node.js, Go, etc.) that directly serves HTTP requests.
> - **`ReplicaSet`:** The controller that maintains the exact number of replicas (`replicas`) for **one fixed Pod configuration version** (for example, `v1.2.0` must always have `3` Pods running). If a Pod fails, the ReplicaSet immediately creates a replacement Pod.
> - **`Deployment`:** The high-level management layer that orchestrates **version upgrades** (`RollingUpdate`) and stores **Revision** history. When upgrading to `v1.3.0`, the Deployment creates `ReplicaSet v2` and scales it up from `0 → 3` while scaling `ReplicaSet v1` down from `3 → 0` so the service experiences no interruption. (You can think of a `Pod` as a counter clerk, a `ReplicaSet` as the shift supervisor checking headcount for each shift, and a `Deployment` as the manager coordinating the handover between two shifts.)

steps.headingEn: Label Matching Rules Between selector.matchLabels and template.metadata.labels
steps.bodyEn:
In a `Deployment` (`apiVersion: apps/v1`), there are two label declaration locations that must match strictly:

```yaml Khớp nối selector.matchLabels (A) với template.metadata.labels (B)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shop-api
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: shop-api          # (A) Điều kiện lọc để Deployment/ReplicaSet nhận diện Pod thuộc quyền quản lý
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: shop-api        # (B) Bộ nhãn được gắn lên mỗi Pod khi khởi tạo
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: api
          image: ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:1.2.0
```

> [!WARNING] Common validation error when `(A)` and `(B)` labels diverge
> In the configuration above, `(B)` (`spec.template.metadata.labels`) is the label set attached to each Pod upon creation, while `(A)` (`spec.selector.matchLabels`) is the filter condition used by the Deployment to identify the Pods under its management. **Every key-value pair in `(A)` MUST appear identically in `(B)`!**
> If `(A)` specifies `{ app: "web" }` while `(B)` specifies `{ app: "frontend" }`, the Kubernetes API Server will immediately reject it with the error:
> ==`Invalid value: 'selector' does not match template 'labels'`==.

steps.headingEn: Zero-Downtime Upgrade Strategy: RollingUpdate (maxUnavailable: 0)
steps.bodyEn:
When you update `image` from `1.2.0` to `1.3.0`, Kubernetes defaults to the **`RollingUpdate`** strategy — gradually replacing old Pods one by one with new Pods instead of terminating them all at once. To guarantee ==absolute Zero-Downtime== without losing serving capacity during peak hours, combine the following pair of parameters (similar to opening a new checkout counter and verifying it runs smoothly before closing an old one):

- [x] **`maxUnavailable: 0`:** Throughout the upgrade, the number of `Ready` Pods **must never drop below the desired `replicas` count**, not even by 1 Pod! (With `replicas: 4`, the cluster always keeps at least `4 - 0 = 4` Ready Pods).
- [x] **`maxSurge: 1`:** Allows the cluster to temporarily spin up at most `1` extra new Pod above `replicas` (with `replicas: 4`, temporarily peaking at **`5` Pods**). Only after the new Pod reports `Ready` does K8s terminate 1 old Pod!


```yaml Cấu hình chiến lược RollingUpdate an toàn tuyệt đối trong Deployment.spec
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0
      maxSurge: 1
```

> [!TIP] When should you use the second strategy, `type: Recreate`?
> Unlike `RollingUpdate`, the `Recreate` strategy **terminates 100% of old Pods before starting any new Pods** (accepting a few seconds of downtime). Only use `Recreate` for legacy applications that cannot have two versions running concurrently and writing to the same single disk volume, or when upgrading specialized GPUs on nodes with limited hardware slots!

steps.headingEn: Scaling Replicas (scale) and Rolling Back (rollout undo)
steps.bodyEn:
Because `Deployment` retains old `ReplicaSet` objects (scaled down to `0` replicas) in its history according to `spec.revisionHistoryLimit` (defaulting to **10 revisions**), if a newly pushed `2.0.0-crash` release hits a code bug and enters `CrashLoopBackOff`, you don't have to wait 10 minutes for a CI/CD rebuild — you can ==immediately restore the previous stable version in seconds==:

```visual
kind: groups
title: Bảng Lệnh Điều Chỉnh Số Bản Sao & Khôi Phục Phiên Bản [!badge:emerald:Thực Chiến]
columns: 2
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: activity
    title: Co Giãn Quân Số Tức Thì (Scale)
    badge: Horizontal Scaling
    tone: sky
    bullets:
      - "Cập nhật ngay trạng thái mong muốn lên **5 Pod** khi lưu lượng tăng vọt"
      - "`ReplicaSet` lập tức tạo bù (hoặc cắt bớt) để hội tụ đúng **5 Pod** đang chạy"
    code: |
      kubectl scale deployment/shop-api --replicas=5
    codeLang: bash
  - num: 2
    icon: rollback
    title: Kiểm Tra Lịch Sử & Quay Lui 2 Giây (Undo)
    badge: Emergency Rollback
    tone: emerald
    bullets:
      - "`rollout status`: Theo dõi tiến trình xoay vòng trực tiếp tới khi hoàn tất 100%"
      - "`rollout history`: Xem danh sách các Revision đã lưu"
      - "**`kubectl rollout undo`**: Hạ `ReplicaSet` lỗi về `0` và nâng bản ổn định liền trước lên lại ngay lập tức (hoặc thêm `--to-revision=N`)"
    code: |
      kubectl rollout status deployment/checkout
      kubectl rollout history deployment/checkout
      kubectl rollout undo deployment/checkout
    codeLang: bash
```

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - Standard delegation chain: **`Deployment`** (manages versions & history) → **`ReplicaSet`** (counts and maintains Pod headcount) → **`Pod`**.
> - All labels in `spec.selector.matchLabels` must match labels inside `spec.template.metadata.labels`.
> - `maxUnavailable: 0` + `maxSurge: 1` ensures zero capacity drop during upgrades · Scale dynamically with `kubectl scale ... --replicas=5` · Emergency rollback with **`kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name>`**.

readings.noteEn: A production-grade High Availability Deployment blueprint with 3 replicas distributed across multiple Nodes.
readings.taskEn: Locate the parameter pair under `spec.strategy.rollingUpdate` and explain why those two numbers ensure serving capacity never drops during a deployment.
readings.answerEn: `maxUnavailable: 0` prevents terminating any old Pod before a new replacement is ready (always keeping at least 3 live Pods), while `maxSurge: 1` allows spinning up 1 extra new Pod first, waiting for it to become `Ready`, and only then removing 1 old Pod.

readings.noteEn: The most common logical syntax mistake that causes the API Server to reject a Deployment right at submission.
readings.taskEn: Compare `spec.selector.matchLabels` and `spec.template.metadata.labels` in this file: if you want to add a `v2` version label without breaking the Deployment, how should you edit it?
readings.answerEn: You must keep the original `app: checkout-api` label identical in both places, and only add the extra `version: v2` label inside `spec.template.metadata.labels` (since `matchLabels` only needs to be a subset of the Pod template's labels).

K09-Q1.qEn: Why do we always deploy web applications in Production through a `Deployment` instead of creating a standalone `Pod` directly?
choicesEn: Because a standalone `Pod` cannot run JavaScript

Because a bare `Pod` has no supervising controller (if its Node crashes, it is lost permanently), whereas a `Deployment` (via `ReplicaSet`) automatically recreates failed Pods, scales multiple replicas, and supports Rolling Updates / Rollbacks
Because `Deployment` provides free RAM on AWS while `Pod` costs money
Because only a `Deployment` can read environment variables
K09-Q1.explainEn: `Deployment` provides Self-Healing (automatic recovery when a Node fails), Horizontal Scaling (`replicas`), and Zero-Downtime version updates.

K09-Q2.qEn: When submitting a `Deployment` with `spec.selector.matchLabels: { app: "web" }` while `spec.template.metadata.labels` specifies `{ app: "frontend" }`, what happens?
choicesEn: Kubernetes automatically changes both to `{ app: "default" }`
The Kubernetes API Server immediately rejects it with a validation error: `'selector' does not match template 'labels'`
The Deployment is still created but runs double the number of Pods
The cluster automatically restarts the Control Plane
K09-Q2.explainEn: To prevent a Deployment from creating Pods that it cannot recognize or manage, the API Server requires every label in `selector.matchLabels` to match `template.metadata.labels`.

K09-Q3.qEn: For a `Deployment` with `replicas: 4`, what do `maxUnavailable: 0` and `maxSurge: 1` in `rollingUpdate` mean during a new version upgrade?
choicesEn: Terminate all 4 old Pods at once before starting 4 new Pods
Always keep at least **4 Ready Pods** serving traffic and allow the cluster to temporarily scale up to at most **5 Pods** while rotating replicas one by one
Allow at most 1 user to access the service during the upgrade
Prevent any further Image upgrades
K09-Q3.explainEn: Minimum available Pods = `4 - 0 = 4`; maximum total Pods existing simultaneously during handoff = `4 + 1 = 5`.

K09-Q4.qEn: When you perform a Rolling Update from version `1.0` to `2.0`, `Deployment` keeps the old `ReplicaSet` (scaled down to `0` replicas) in its history so it can instantly revert when you run `kubectl rollout undo`.
K09-Q4.explainEn: Correct! The number of historical `ReplicaSet` objects retained is controlled by `spec.revisionHistoryLimit` (default is `10`).

K09-Q5.qEn: To urgently roll back `deployment/checkout` to the immediately preceding stable version when a newly deployed release fails, what subcommand keyword goes after `kubectl rollout ____`?
K09-Q5.explainEn: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name>` immediately restores the Pod template to the previous Revision (or a specific one via `--to-revision=N`).

K09-Q6.qEn: Which intermediate resource is automatically created underneath by a `Deployment` to directly count and maintain the number of `Pod` instances for each version?
choicesEn: `StatefulSet`
`ReplicaSet`
`CronJob`
`Ingress`
K09-Q6.explainEn: The standard delegation chain is `Deployment` managing `ReplicaSet` objects, while each `ReplicaSet` manages its `Pod` count.

K09-Q7.qEn: You run the scaling command below on `deployment/shop-api`. Once the control loop converges, how many `shop-api` Pods are running?
K09-Q7.explainEn: `--replicas=5` updates the desired state to 5 replicas; the `ReplicaSet` immediately adds or removes Pods to maintain exactly 5.

K09-FC1.backEn: **`Deployment`** manages upgrades and rollbacks across versions by orchestrating multiple **`ReplicaSet`** objects; each **`ReplicaSet`** maintains the required **`Pod`** count for its version.

K09-FC2.frontEn: What is the mandatory requirement between `spec.selector.matchLabels` and `spec.template.metadata.labels`?
K09-FC2.backEn: Every label pair in `spec.selector.matchLabels` **must match exactly** inside `spec.template.metadata.labels`.

K09-FC3.frontEn: What do `maxUnavailable: 0` and `maxSurge: 1` mean in a `RollingUpdate`?
K09-FC3.backEn:
- `maxUnavailable: 0`: Never let Ready Pods drop below `replicas`.
- `maxSurge: 1`: Spin up 1 healthy new Pod first before terminating 1 old Pod.

K09-FC5.frontEn: What command urgently rolls back `deployment/checkout` to the previous stable version?

K09-FC6.frontEn: How do you view the list of past update revisions for a Deployment?

K10.summaryEn: Place a stable virtual IP (ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer) in front of ephemeral Pods, distinguish port vs targetPort, and call services across Namespaces via FQDN.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
In lesson `K09`, you saw the self-healing power of a `Deployment`: whenever a Pod dies, the `ReplicaSet` immediately spins up a replacement Pod. However, that constant "shift rotation" creates a tricky networking problem:

- [!] **Every time a Pod is recreated, it receives a brand-new internal IP address** (for example, the old Pod was `10.244.1.15`, while the new Pod scheduled on another Node gets `10.244.2.48`)!
- [>] If the Frontend or another service hardcodes Pod IPs, a single Rolling Update will break every connection.

> [!NOTE] Role of a `Service`: A Stable Network Entry Point in Front of Pods
> In Kubernetes, a **`Service` (`apiVersion: v1`)** creates a ==fixed virtual IP address (`ClusterIP`)== paired with an **immutable DNS name** in front of a group of Pods. The Service continuously watches Pods matching its `selector` labels and automatically load-balances traffic to healthy (`Ready`) Pods, letting applications call one another reliably regardless of Pod IP changes across redeployments (much like dialing a single main hotline number that automatically routes you to an available agent on duty).

```visual
    tone: emerald
```

steps.headingEn: Distinguishing the 3 Service Types: ClusterIP, NodePort, and LoadBalancer
steps.bodyEn:
Beginners often get confused about which `Service` type to pick. You can distinguish them by how broadly they expose traffic, from narrowest to widest:

```visual
kind: groups
title: So Sánh 3 Kiểu Service Cốt Lõi Trong Kubernetes (spec.type)
subtitle: Nếu bạn không ghi trường spec.type trong YAML, Kubernetes mặc định chọn kiểu ClusterIP an toàn nhất!
columns: 3
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: shield-check
    title: ClusterIP (Mặc định)
    badge: Chỉ gọi nội bộ cụm
    tone: emerald
    bullets:
      - "**Là gì:** Địa chỉ IP ảo nội bộ chỉ truy cập được từ bên trong cụm K8s (lưu lượng từ Internet bên ngoài không chạm trực tiếp vào được)"
      - "Kiểu mặc định khi bỏ trống `spec.type`"
      - "**Khi nào dùng:** **90% mọi dịch vụ** — FastAPI / Node.js Backend, PostgreSQL, Redis, Queue"
    footer: Mặc định vàng cho giao tiếp Đông-Tây (East-West) nội bộ
  - num: 2
    icon: server
    title: NodePort
    badge: Cổng 30000–32767 trên Node
    tone: amber
    bullets:
      - "**Là gì:** Đục thêm một cổng cố định trong dải ==`30000–32767`== trên vỏ mọi máy chủ Worker Node (`<NodeIP>:30080`)"
      - "**Khi nào dùng:** Thử nghiệm nhanh trên cụm local (`kind`, `minikube`, `k3s`) hoặc đấu nối bộ cân bằng tải phần cứng tại phòng máy riêng (On-Premise)"
    footer: Bao hàm sẵn tính năng của ClusterIP ở bên dưới
  - num: 3
    icon: cloud
    title: LoadBalancer
    badge: Thuê IP Public trên Cloud
    tone: sky
    bullets:
      - "**Là gì:** Tự động gọi API của AWS / GCP / Azure thuê một bộ cân bằng tải đám mây có địa chỉ IP Public thật ngoài Internet"
      - "**Khi nào dùng:** Thường chỉ cấp **1 chiếc duy nhất** cho cổng gác biên (Ingress / Gateway Controller) để dùng chung, tránh tốn tiền thuê hàng chục Cloud LB lẻ!"
    footer: Bao hàm cả NodePort + ClusterIP ở bên dưới
```

steps.headingEn: Clearly Distinguishing the 3 Port Numbers: port, targetPort, and nodePort
steps.bodyEn:
Countless `502 Bad Gateway` or `Connection Refused` incidents stem from mixing up the port fields inside a `Service`:

```visual
kind: anatomy
title: Cấu Trúc Bộ Lọc Nhãn & 3 Con Số Cổng Trong Manifest Service
subtitle: Quy tắc ngắn gọn — port là cổng mở trên Service VIP, còn targetPort là cổng ứng dụng đang lắng nghe bên trong Pod
items:
  - keyword: selector
    role: Bộ lọc tìm Pod đích
    tone: cyan
    summary: Quét tìm mọi Pod đang sẵn sàng (Ready = true) mang bộ nhãn khớp với selector này.
    bullets:
      - "Nếu gõ lệch nhãn so với Pod `metadata.labels`, danh sách đích sẽ trống rỗng (`ENDPOINTS = <none>`)"
    example: "selector:\n  app: shop-api"
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: port
    role: Cổng mặt tiền trên Service
    tone: sky
    summary: Cổng mở trên chính chiếc Virtual IP của Service để các dịch vụ khác gọi vào.
    bullets:
      - "Ví dụ đặt `port: 80` thì khách nội bộ gọi gọn gàng `http://shop-api-svc` (không cần nhớ cổng lẻ 3000 hay 8000 ở bên trong!)"
    example: "port: 80"
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: targetPort
    role: Cổng thực tế bên trong Pod
    tone: emerald
    summary: Cổng mà tiến trình Python/Node thực sự lắng nghe bên trong container của Pod.
    bullets:
      - "Phải khớp chính xác với `--port 8000` (Uvicorn/FastAPI) hoặc `app.listen(3000)` (Node.js)!"
    example: "targetPort: 3000"
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: nodePort
    role: Cổng vỏ máy Worker Node
    tone: amber
    summary: "Chỉ xuất hiện khi dùng `type: NodePort` (hoặc `LoadBalancer`), mở trên IP của các máy Worker."
    bullets:
      - "Bắt buộc nằm trong dải cổng mặc định **`30000–32767`** của Kubernetes"
    example: "nodePort: 30080"
    lang: yaml
```

```yaml Manifest Service hoàn chỉnh định tuyến từ cổng 80 vào cổng 3000 của Pod
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: shop-api-svc
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: shop-api         # Tìm mọi Pod khỏe mạnh (Ready) đang mang nhãn app=shop-api
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80            # 1) Cổng mặt tiền trên Service (khách gọi http://shop-api-svc)
      targetPort: 3000    # 2) Cổng mà code thực sự lắng nghe BÊN TRONG Pod (3000 hoặc 8000)
      # nodePort: 30080   # 3) (Chỉ có khi type: NodePort) Cổng mở trên vỏ máy Worker Node (30000-32767)
```

### Dynamic Wiring via `Endpoints` / `EndpointSlice`

Kubernetes does not forward packets blindly! When you create a `Service`, K8s continuously scans for Pods that satisfy **both conditions simultaneously**: (1) match every label in `spec.selector` **AND** (2) are in **`Ready = true`** state, then records their live `IP:targetPort` list in **`Endpoints` / `EndpointSlice`** objects.

```visual
kind: flow
title: Đường Đi Của Gói Tin Qua Service & Chốt Kiểm Tra Endpoints
steps:
  - icon: globe
    badge: 1. Gọi tên DNS
    title: Client Pod
    desc: Gọi tên miền cố định của Service ở cổng mặt tiền port 80
    code: "http://shop-api-svc:80"
    tone: sky
    edge: CoreDNS -> VIP
  - icon: network
    badge: 2. Cổng mặt tiền
    title: Service (ClusterIP)
    desc: Giữ Virtual IP bất biến, tra bảng định tuyến của kube-proxy / Cilium
    code: "port: 80"
    tone: cyan
    edge: lọc selector + Ready
  - icon: check
    badge: 3. Danh bạ đích sống
    title: Endpoints / EndpointSlice
    desc: Chỉ giữ danh sách IP:targetPort của các Pod khớp nhãn VÀ Ready = true
    code: "10.244.1.15:3000, 10.244.2.48:3000"
    tone: amber
    edge: cân bằng tải tới targetPort
  - icon: container
    badge: 4. Cổng trong Pod
    title: Backend Pod
    desc: Tiến trình Node.js / FastAPI nhận gói tin tại cổng thực tế bên trong
    code: "targetPort: 3000"
    tone: emerald
```

> [!WARNING] First thing to check when calling a Service fails: Inspect `ENDPOINTS = <none>` right away!
> Run `kubectl get endpoints shop-api-svc` first whenever a Service call fails! If the Pods are `1/1 Running` yet the `ENDPOINTS` column shows ==`<none>`==, the #1 culprit is a **typo or mismatch between the Service's `spec.selector` and the `metadata.labels` on the Pods**!

steps.headingEn: CoreDNS Naming Convention: Same Namespace vs Cross-Namespace
steps.bodyEn:
Every Kubernetes cluster runs an internal **CoreDNS** directory (in the `kube-system` namespace). The moment you create a `Service`, its Fully Qualified Domain Name (**FQDN**) immediately becomes resolvable using the standard 5-part format:
==`<service-name>.<namespace-name>.svc.cluster.local`==

```visual
kind: compare
title: Quy Tắc Gọi Tên Miền CoreDNS — Nội Bộ Namespace vs Xuyên Namespace
subtitle: Không bao giờ cần nhớ IP — chỉ cần gọi đúng tên Service và Namespace theo chuẩn CoreDNS
left:
  badge: "CÙNG NAMESPACE · Viết ngắn gọn"
  title: Gọi thẳng bằng <tên-service>
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    # Cả frontend và shop-api-svc cùng ở namespace "production":
    API_URL="http://shop-api-svc"
  lang: bash
  bullets:
    - "Chỉ cần gọi trực tiếp tên Service (`shop-api-svc`), CoreDNS tự động nối hậu tố namespace hiện tại"
    - "Vì Service mở `port: 80` (mặc định của HTTP) nên thậm chí không cần ghi `:80`"
right:
  badge: "XUYÊN NAMESPACE · Bắt buộc kèm Namespace"
  title: "<service>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local"
  tone: sky
  code: |
    # Web ở "frontend" gọi Redis ở namespace "cache":
    REDIS_HOST="redis-master.cache.svc.cluster.local"

    # FastAPI ở "ai-service" gọi Postgres ở namespace "database":
    DB_URI="postgresql://postgres-svc.database.svc.cluster.local:5432/app"
  lang: bash
  bullets:
    - "Khi gọi sang một Namespace khác, **bắt buộc phải ghi kèm tên Namespace đích**"
    - "Chuẩn đầy đủ (FQDN) luôn là `<tên-service>.<tên-namespace>.svc.cluster.local`"
```

steps.headingEn: Quickly Creating a Service with kubectl expose & Named Ports Tips
steps.bodyEn:
In the CKAD exam or when spinning up a quick test environment, you can publish a running `Deployment` as a `Service` with a single concise command:

```bash
kubectl expose deployment catalog \
  --name=catalog-svc \
  --port=80 \
  --target-port=4000
```

The **`kubectl expose`** command automatically copies the exact `selector` label set from `Deployment/catalog` onto `Service/catalog-svc`, completely eliminating the risk of manual label typos!

> [!TIP] Use `Named Ports` so language migrations never break networking
> Suppose you rewrite a service from Node.js (`containerPort: 3000`) to Python FastAPI (`containerPort: 8000`). If you name the port `name: http` on the Container and set **`targetPort: http`** on the `Service` (instead of hardcoding `3000`), then changing the port to `8000` in the `Deployment` causes the `Service` to reroute seamlessly with zero `502` errors!

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - **3 Service types:** `ClusterIP` (default, cluster-internal only) · `NodePort` (static port `30000–32767` on Nodes) · `LoadBalancer` (provisions a Cloud LB with a Public IP).
> - **3 ports:** `port` (Service front-end port) · `targetPort` (listening port inside the Pod) · `nodePort` (`30000–32767` on Worker Nodes).
> - **CoreDNS FQDN:** `<service>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local` · `selector` label mismatch leaves `kubectl get endpoints` showing `<none>` · Quickly expose with `kubectl expose`.

readings.noteEn: A standard Deployment + Service pairing using Named Ports.
readings.taskEn: In this file, `targetPort` is written as the word `http` instead of the number `3000`. How does Kubernetes know which port number `http` refers to?
readings.answerEn: Kubernetes matches the string `http` against the `ports[].name: http` field inside the Pod's container spec (where `containerPort: 3000` is assigned). Using a Named Port decouples network configuration from the application's internal port number.

readings.noteEn: Two classic configuration bugs that completely sever traffic to a Pod even while the Pod remains Running.
readings.taskEn: Find both bugs in `shop-api-svc` that prevent traffic from reaching the Express app on port 3000.
readings.answerEn: 1) `spec.selector.app: shop-backend` does not match the Pod's `app: shop-api` label, resulting in `Endpoints = <none>`; 2) `targetPort: 8080` points to the wrong port (the container actually listens on `3000`).

K10-Q1.qEn: Why do microservices in Kubernetes never connect directly via individual Pod IP addresses, instead always calling through a **`Service`**?
choicesEn: Because Pods do not have IP addresses
Because Pods are ephemeral and receive a new IP each time they are recreated; a `Service` provides a fixed virtual IP (VIP) and stable DNS name with automatic load balancing to healthy Pods
Because a `Service` compiles TypeScript faster
Because only a `Service` can write files to disk
K10-Q1.explainEn: Pod IPs are ephemeral; a `Service` keeps an immutable DNS name and Virtual IP while automatically updating its target Pod list via `EndpointSlice`.

K10-Q2.qEn: If you declare a `Service` without specifying `spec.type`, which Service type does Kubernetes choose by default?
choicesEn: `LoadBalancer`
`NodePort`
`ClusterIP` (internal cluster access only)
`ExternalName`
K10-Q2.explainEn: `ClusterIP` is the default and safest type — exposing connections only to components inside the Kubernetes cluster.

K10-Q3.qEn: In a `Service` declaration `ports: [{ port: 80, targetPort: 3000 }]`, what roles do the numbers `80` and `3000` play?
choicesEn: `80` is the port Node.js listens on inside the Pod, while `3000` is the port on the Service
`port: 80` is the port on the Service itself (clients call `http://my-svc:80`), while `targetPort: 3000` is the actual port the Node.js process listens on inside the Pod (`app.listen(3000)`)
Both are ports opened on the developer's personal laptop
`3000` is the maximum number of connections in `80` seconds
K10-Q3.explainEn: `port` is the Service's front-facing port; `targetPort` is the destination port inside the Pod's container.

K10-Q4.qEn: A web app in the `frontend` namespace needs to connect to a Service named `redis-master` in the `cache` namespace. The standard CoreDNS FQDN is `redis-master.____.svc.cluster.local` — what is the missing word?
K10-Q4.explainEn: The CoreDNS FQDN structure is always `<service-name>.<namespace-name>.svc.cluster.local`.

K10-Q5.qEn: When creating a `NodePort` `Service`, valid default `nodePort` values in Kubernetes must fall within the port range `30000` to `32767`.
K10-Q5.explainEn: Correct! Kubernetes reserves the `30000–32767` range on Worker Nodes for `NodePort` to avoid colliding with system service ports.

K10-Q6.qEn: You run `kubectl get endpoints shop-api-svc` and see `<none>` in the `ENDPOINTS` column even though all `shop-api` Pods are `1/1 Running`. What is the most likely cause?
choicesEn: The Control Plane disk is full
The labels in the `Service`'s `spec.selector` are mistyped and do not match the `metadata.labels` on the Pods
Helm is not installed on your local machine
The Image is based on Alpine instead of Debian
K10-Q6.explainEn: `ENDPOINTS = <none>` indicates the Service found zero `Ready` Pods matching its `spec.selector` label filter.

K10-Q7.qEn: In the imperative command below used to quickly create a Service from `deployment/catalog`, what subcommand keyword immediately follows `kubectl ____`?
K10-Q7.explainEn: `kubectl expose` automatically copies the Deployment's selector labels to create a Service routing to those exact Pods.

K10-FC1.frontEn: How do the three most common `Service` types (`ClusterIP`, `NodePort`, `LoadBalancer`) differ?
K10-FC1.backEn:
- **`ClusterIP`:** Cluster-internal only (default).
- **`NodePort`:** Opens port `30000–32767` on Worker Nodes.
- **`LoadBalancer`:** Provisions a Public IP load balancer from the Cloud provider.

K10-FC2.frontEn: What is the difference between `port`, `targetPort`, and `nodePort` in a `Service`?
K10-FC2.backEn:
- **`port`:** Port on the Service's Virtual IP.
- **`targetPort`:** Port the application listens on inside the Pod.
- **`nodePort`:** Static port opened externally on Worker Nodes (`30000–32767`).

K10-FC3.frontEn: What is the Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) pattern of a Service in CoreDNS?

K10-FC4.frontEn: When `kubectl get endpoints <svc>` returns `<none>`, what should you inspect immediately?
K10-FC4.backEn: Compare the Service's **`spec.selector`** against **`kubectl get pods --show-labels`** (and verify whether the Pods are `Ready 1/1`).

K10-FC5.frontEn: Does a Pod that is `Running` but failing its `readinessProbe` (`0/1 Ready`) receive traffic from a `Service`?
K10-FC5.backEn: **NO!** Kubernetes immediately removes unready Pod IPs from `Endpoints` so clients do not hit errors.

K10-FC6.frontEn: What command quickly creates a Service `catalog-svc` mapping port `80 -> 4000` for `deployment/catalog`?

kube-ex-k10-1.titleEn: Write a ClusterIP Service Routing Port 80 to Pod Port 3000
kube-ex-k10-1.promptEn:
Write a `ClusterIP` `Service` (`apiVersion: v1`) manifest named `shop-api-svc` such that:
1. It selects Pods carrying the label `app: shop-api`.
2. It exposes service port `port: 80` and forwards traffic to `targetPort: 3000` where Express is listening.
hintsEn: Under `selector:`, add `app: shop-api` (indented by 4 spaces).
In the first item under `ports:`, add `targetPort: 3000` at the same level as `port: 80`.

kube-ex-k10-2.titleEn: Configure a NodePort Service Opening Port 30080 on Worker Nodes
kube-ex-k10-2.promptEn: On an internal test cluster without a Cloud LoadBalancer, switch the `preview-web` `Service` below to `type: NodePort`, keeping `port: 80` and `targetPort: 3000`, and pin the static port on the Node to `nodePort: 30080`.
hintsEn: Change `type: ClusterIP` to `type: NodePort`.
Add `nodePort: 30080` (within the valid 30000–32767 range) directly below `targetPort: 3000`.

kube-ex-k10-3.titleEn: Properly Wire a Deployment + Service Pair in Multi-doc YAML
kube-ex-k10-3.promptEn: The two-resource YAML file below is broken at **both checkpoints**: the `Service` looks for the wrong label (`app: order-backend` instead of `app: order-api`) and targets the wrong port (`targetPort: 8080` while the container exposes `containerPort: 4000`). Fix the `Service` section so both label and port match the `Deployment` 100%!
hintsEn: In the `Service` resource in the lower half: change `app: order-backend` to `app: order-api`.
Also change `targetPort: 8080` to `targetPort: 4000` to match the Deployment's `containerPort: 4000`.

kube-ex-k10-4.titleEn: Expose a Running Deployment as a Service Using kubectl expose
kube-ex-k10-4.promptEn: The cluster already has `deployment/catalog` running 2 healthy Pods listening on internal port `4000`. Use `kubectl expose` to create a `Service` named `catalog-svc` listening on `--port=80` and forwarding to `--target-port=4000`.
hintsEn: Full syntax: `kubectl expose deployment catalog --name=catalog-svc --port=80 --target-port=4000`.
Once exposed, the Service will automatically pick up both Ready Endpoints from the 2 `catalog` Pods.

kube-ex-k10-5.titleEn: Write a CoreDNS FQDN to Call a Database Across Namespaces
kube-ex-k10-5.promptEn: Your application runs in the `storefront` namespace, while the PostgreSQL database sits behind a Service named `postgres-svc` inside the `database` namespace (port `5432`). Because they are in different namespaces, writing the short name `postgres-svc:5432` will fail with `ENOTFOUND`! Update the `DB_ADDRESS` key in the `ConfigMap` to the standard CoreDNS FQDN (`<svc>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local:5432`).
hintsEn: The FQDN pattern in K8s is `<service-name>.<namespace-name>.svc.cluster.local`.
Change it to `"postgres-svc.database.svc.cluster.local:5432"`.

K11.titleEn: HTTP/HTTPS Routing with Ingress, TLS & Kubernetes Gateway API
K11.summaryEn: Perform Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS routing with Ingress to save on Cloud LoadBalancers, terminate TLS, and navigate the 2026 shift from Ingress NGINX to Gateway API (Envoy, Cilium, Traefik).

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
In lesson `K10`, you learned that a `LoadBalancer` `Service` on AWS or Google Cloud provisions a public Internet IP address. Let's do some practical math:

- [!] Suppose your e-commerce platform has **20 microservices** (`auth`, `catalog`, `ai-search` in Python FastAPI, `orders` in Node.js, `web-ui`, etc.).
- [!] If every service opens its own `LoadBalancer` `Service`, you pay monthly for **20 separate cloud load balancers** (wasting hundreds of dollars), while also managing 20 scattered IP addresses and 20 SSL certificates!

The industry-standard solution is placing ==a single smart Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS gateway== at the edge of the cluster: rent **just 1 Cloud LoadBalancer**, terminate HTTPS in one central place, and route traffic to internal `ClusterIP` Services by domain name and URL path (`/api`, `/ai`, `/`). That is the job of **`Ingress`** and the modern standard **`Kubernetes Gateway API`**.

```visual
kind: illustration
diagram: "kube:k11"
alt: "Cơ chế Ingress và Gateway API tầng 7 giải mã TLS HTTPS tại 1 Cloud LoadBalancer duy nhất rồi rẽ nhánh Host và Path vào ClusterIP nội bộ"
title: "Cơ Chế Định Tuyến Tầng 7: Ingress / Gateway API, Giải Mã TLS & Rẽ Nhánh Đường Dẫn"
subtitle: "Dùng chung 1 địa chỉ IP công cộng duy nhất cho hàng chục Microservices để tiết kiệm tối đa chi phí Cloud LoadBalancer"
caption: "Luồng lưu lượng HTTPS từ Internet đi qua 1 Cloud LoadBalancer vào Ingress/Gateway Controller để giải mã TLS rồi phân luồng theo Hostname và URL Path"
callouts:
  - num: 1
    label: "1 Cloud LoadBalancer công cộng duy nhất"
    desc: "Thay vì thuê 20 bộ cân bằng tải đắt đỏ cho 20 dịch vụ, toàn bộ lưu lượng HTTPS hội tụ về một địa chỉ IP cửa ngõ duy nhất."
    tone: sky
  - num: 2
    label: "Giải mã TLS & Định tuyến thông minh Layer 7"
    desc: "Controller (Envoy Gateway / Cilium / Traefik / Nginx) đọc Secret để giải mã HTTPS rồi đọc luật Host và Path (/api, /) để rẽ nhánh."
    tone: cyan
  - num: 3
    label: "Chuyển tiếp an toàn vào các ClusterIP nội bộ"
    desc: "Các microservice phía sau nằm kín trong mạng nội bộ dưới dạng ClusterIP và hỗ trợ chia phần trăm Canary chuẩn gốc với Gateway API."
    tone: emerald
```

steps.headingEn: HTTP Routing Architecture on K8s: Declaration (Ingress / HTTPRoute) vs Execution (Controller)
steps.bodyEn:
> [!WARNING] Important note: YAML declarations will not work if the cluster lacks a Controller
> A `kind: Ingress` (or `kind: HTTPRoute`) resource is merely a **declarative routing specification** stored in `etcd`. To actually accept network traffic, terminate TLS, and forward requests according to those rules, your cluster must have a running **Controller Pod** (such as **`Envoy Gateway`**, **`Traefik`**, **`Cilium`**, or `AWS Load Balancer Controller`). If a cluster (such as a fresh `kind` or `minikube` cluster) has no Controller installed, `kubectl apply -f ingress.yaml` still succeeds, yet no port will open to receive external traffic (just like posting traffic rules without any traffic enforcement unit at the intersection).

```visual
kind: flow
title: Luồng Lưu Lượng Internet Qua 1 LoadBalancer & Bộ Điều Khiển Tầng 7
subtitle: Tiết kiệm chi phí tối đa — 1 IP Public duy nhất giải mã HTTPS rồi rẽ nhánh vào hàng chục ClusterIP nội bộ
steps:
  - icon: globe
    badge: 1. Khách hàng
    title: HTTPS Request
    desc: Trình duyệt gọi vào 1 Cloud LoadBalancer công cộng duy nhất của toàn cụm
    code: "https://shop.example.com/api"
    tone: sky
    edge: giải mã TLS (443)
  - icon: shield-check
    badge: 2. Bộ thực thi
    title: Ingress / Gateway Controller
    desc: Pod Envoy / Cilium / Traefik đọc Secret shop-tls-cert để giải mã HTTPS ở cửa ngõ
    code: "TLS Termination"
    tone: emerald
    edge: đọc luật định tuyến YAML
  - icon: workflow
    badge: 3. Rẽ nhánh URL
    title: Định Tuyến Layer 7
    desc: Khớp Hostname & Path — đường dẫn /api rẽ sang api-svc:3000, còn / rẽ sang web-svc:80
    code: "/api -> api-svc | / -> web-svc"
    tone: cyan
    edge: HTTP nội bộ gọn nhẹ
  - icon: boxes
    badge: 4. Đích nội bộ
    title: Pods Microservices
    desc: Ứng dụng FastAPI, Node.js & React chạy HTTP thuần an toàn đằng sau các ClusterIP Service
    code: "Pods :3000, :8000 & :80"
    tone: amber
```

steps.headingEn: Standard Structure of networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress
steps.bodyEn:
In most existing systems (and on CKAD/CKA certification exams), you will encounter the stable `apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1` `Ingress` manifest:

```yaml Manifest Ingress chuẩn hiện đại (networking.k8s.io/v1) kèm TLS HTTPS
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: shop-ingress
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx     # Chỉ định bộ điều khiển nào tiếp nhận bản luật này
  tls:
    - hosts:
        - shop.example.com
      secretName: shop-tls-cert
  rules:
    - host: shop.example.com
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /api
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: api-svc
                port:
                  number: 3000
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: web-svc
                port:
                  number: 80
```

```visual
kind: anatomy
title: 4 Chi Tiết Kỹ Thuật Bắt Buộc Trong networking.k8s.io/v1 Ingress
subtitle: Nắm chắc 4 trường này để không bao giờ vướng lỗi cú pháp từ các bài viết v1beta1 cũ trên mạng
items:
  - keyword: ingressClassName
    role: Chọn bộ điều khiển
    tone: sky
    summary: Đặt trực tiếp dưới `spec:` để chỉ định lớp Ingress Controller nào xử lý bản luật này.
    bullets:
      - "Thay thế chính thức cho kiểu viết cũ bằng annotation `kubernetes.io/ingress.class` trước đây"
    example: "spec:\n  ingressClassName: traefik"
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: pathType
    role: Kiểu khớp URL (Bắt buộc)
    tone: emerald
    summary: Trường BẮT BUỘC trong mỗi mục `paths[]` — thiếu nó API Server sẽ từ chối ngay!
    bullets:
      - "**`Prefix`:** Khớp theo phân đoạn `/` (`/api` khớp `/api`, `/api/v1`, `/api/orders`, nhưng **không** khớp nhầm `/apikeys`!)"
      - "**`Exact`:** Chỉ khớp chính xác tuyệt đối từng ký tự (`/healthz` chỉ khớp đúng `/healthz`)"
    example: "path: /api\npathType: Prefix"
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: backend.service
    role: Cấu trúc đích chuẩn v1
    tone: cyan
    summary: Tách tường minh tên Service và số cổng (hoặc tên cổng) bên dưới khóa `service:`.
    bullets:
      - "Không còn viết gộp `serviceName` / `servicePort` như bản nháp `v1beta1` ngày xưa nữa!"
    example: "backend:\n  service:\n    name: api-svc\n    port:\n      number: 3000"
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: spec.tls & secretName
    role: Giải mã HTTPS ở cửa ngõ
    tone: amber
    summary: Tham chiếu tới một Kubernetes `Secret` (cùng namespace với Ingress) kiểu `kubernetes.io/tls`.
    bullets:
      - "Secret này lưu cặp chứng chỉ công khai **`tls.crt`** và khóa riêng **`tls.key`** (thường được **`cert-manager`** tự động xin cấp & gia hạn miễn phí từ Let's Encrypt)"
      - "Nhờ TLS Termination ở cửa ngõ, code FastAPI / Node.js bên trong chỉ cần chạy HTTP thuần gọn nhẹ"
    example: "tls:\n  - hosts: [shop.example.com]\n    secretName: shop-tls-cert"
    lang: yaml
```

steps.headingEn: 2026 Industry Standard Shift: From Ingress NGINX to Kubernetes Gateway API
steps.bodyEn:
> [!NOTE] Major Kubernetes Ecosystem Shift in 2026
> For nearly a decade, the community **`Ingress NGINX` (`kubernetes/ingress-nginx`)** project was the most popular choice, but the Kubernetes community has officially announced **ending new feature development and placing `ingress-nginx` on a retirement roadmap** due to the security burden of cramming hundreds of custom `annotations`!
> In 2026, the industry is rapidly migrating to the next-generation official standard ==Kubernetes Gateway API (`gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1`)== powered by modern, secure, high-performance engines such as **`Envoy Gateway`**, **`Cilium`** (integrated directly with eBPF in the Linux kernel), and **`Traefik`**.

Why is **Gateway API** far superior to traditional `Ingress`?
- In legacy `Ingress`, everything (port 443, infrastructure TLS certificates, Dev team `/api` paths, plus Canary/Rate-Limit rules via a jungle of proprietary `annotations`) is stuffed into **1 single YAML file**.
- In **Gateway API**, responsibilities are cleanly separated into **2 distinct tiers matching real-world team roles**:
  1. **Infrastructure / Platform Team** manages network listeners & HTTPS certificates via **`GatewayClass`** + **`Gateway`**.
  2. **Application Dev Teams (Python, Node.js, etc.)** manage their own routes and Canary traffic splitting inside their Namespace via ==`HTTPRoute`== — completely native without a single awkward annotation!

```visual
kind: compare
title: So Sánh Ingress Truyền Thống vs Chuẩn Mới Kubernetes Gateway API (2026)
subtitle: Hiểu cả hai giúp bạn vừa vận hành tốt các cụm hiện hữu, vừa tự tin thiết kế kiến trúc mới chuẩn 2026!
left:
  badge: "HỆ THỐNG HIỆN HỮU · Ingress"
  title: networking.k8s.io/v1
  tone: sky
  code: |
    apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: Ingress
    metadata:
      annotations:
        nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/canary-weight: "10"
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "**Mô hình 1 tệp gom chung:** Hạ tầng TLS và đường dẫn ứng dụng nằm lẫn lộn trong 1 manifest"
    - "**Canary / Header Routing / Rewrite:** Phải phụ thuộc vào `annotations` riêng lẻ của từng hãng; dự án `ingress-nginx` cộng đồng đang rút lui"
    - "**Khi nào gặp:** Rất phổ biến trong các cụm hiện có và bài thi nền tảng — bắt buộc phải đọc/viết thành thạo"
right:
  badge: "CHUẨN MẶC ĐỊNH MỚI 2026 · Gateway API"
  title: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1 (Envoy / Cilium / Traefik)
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: HTTPRoute
    spec:
      parentRefs:
        - name: prod-gateway
      rules:
        - backendRefs:
            - { name: api-v1, port: 3000, weight: 90 }
            - { name: api-v2, port: 3000, weight: 10 }
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "**Phân quyền sạch sẽ:** Đội Infra nắm `Gateway` (TLS/IP), đội Dev tự chủ viết `HTTPRoute` (hoặc `GRPCRoute`)"
    - "**Tính năng chuẩn gốc trong `spec`:** Chia phần trăm Canary (`weight: 90` / `10`), khớp Header, sửa URL chạy đồng nhất trên **Envoy Gateway, Cilium, Traefik, Istio, GKE, EKS**"
    - "**Lời khuyên 2026:** Lựa chọn số 1 khi khởi tạo cụm Kubernetes mới!"
```

> [!TIP] Quick guide to choosing a gateway controller in 2026
> - Building a new cluster or replacing legacy `ingress-nginx` → Prefer **Gateway API** with **`Envoy Gateway`**, **`Cilium`**, or **`Traefik`**.
> - Maintaining a stable existing Cloud `Ingress` cluster → You can use Cloud-native Ingress (`AWS Load Balancer Controller` / `GKE Ingress`) or `Traefik` while planning your migration to `HTTPRoute`.

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - **1 gateway controller** + multiple `ClusterIP` Services means paying for **only 1 Cloud LoadBalancer** and centralizing HTTPS certificates (`cert-manager`).
> - `kind: Ingress` (`networking.k8s.io/v1`) does nothing without a running Controller Pod · Always specify `spec.ingressClassName`, `pathType` (`Prefix` / `Exact`), and `spec.tls[].secretName`.
> - The 2026 industry shift moves from `ingress-nginx` to ==Gateway API (`gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1`)== on **Envoy Gateway / Cilium / Traefik**: Infra owns `Gateway`, Devs write HTTP & Canary rules in **`HTTPRoute`**.

readings.noteEn: Production-ready Ingress manifest paired with cert-manager for automatic HTTPS certificate provisioning.
readings.taskEn: Locate the `cert-manager` annotation and the `spec.tls` block: in what resource type is the HTTPS private key actually stored?
readings.answerEn: The annotation `cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: "letsencrypt-prod"` instructs cert-manager to request a certificate from Let's Encrypt and store the `tls.crt` + `tls.key` pair inside a Kubernetes `Secret` named `shop-tls-cert`, referenced in `spec.tls[0].secretName`.

readings.noteEn: Comparing traditional Ingress against the next-generation Gateway + HTTPRoute architecture.
readings.taskEn: In the `HTTPRoute` file, how do you split 90% of traffic to the stable release and 10% to the Canary release without using any annotations?
readings.answerEn: Gateway API provides built-in standard `weight: 90` and `weight: 10` fields directly on each entry inside the `HTTPRoute` `backendRefs` array.

readings.noteEn: Legacy v1beta1 Ingress example commonly seen in pre-2021 docs so you know how to migrate it.
readings.taskEn: Identify 3 syntax fields in `ingress-legacy-beta.yaml` that no longer exist in `networking.k8s.io/v1`.
readings.answerEn: 1) `apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1beta1`; 2) The `kubernetes.io/ingress.class` annotation (now `spec.ingressClassName`); 3) `backend.serviceName` & `backend.servicePort` along with the missing required `pathType` field.

K11-Q1.qEn: What is the biggest cost and architectural benefit of placing **1 Ingress Controller** in front of 20 `ClusterIP` Services instead of creating 20 separate `LoadBalancer` Services?
choicesEn: It lets you skip using DNS domain names altogether
You only pay for **1 single Cloud LoadBalancer**, centralize all TLS HTTPS certificates in one place, and perform smart Layer 7 routing by Hostname / URL Path (`/api`, `/`)
It increases each Pod's disk capacity by 20x
You no longer need to run `kube-apiserver`
K11-Q1.explainEn: Ingress acts as a centralized Layer 7 Reverse Proxy, saving hundreds of dollars per month in Cloud LoadBalancer fees and simplifying HTTPS management.

K11-Q2.qEn: If a Kubernetes cluster (such as a brand-new `kind` or `kubeadm` cluster) does not have any **Ingress Controller** installed (like `ingress-nginx` or `Traefik`), running `kubectl apply -f ingress.yaml` will still automatically open ports to receive Internet traffic.
K11-Q2.explainEn: False! An `Ingress` object is only declarative routing data; a running **Ingress Controller** Pod is required on the cluster to read those rules and actually open ports and route traffic.

K11-Q3.qEn: In modern stable Kubernetes, what is the `apiVersion` value for a `kind: Ingress` resource?
K11-Q3.explainEn: `networking.k8s.io/v1` is the only standard version for `Ingress` since K8s 1.19+ (`extensions/v1beta1` and `networking.k8s.io/v1beta1` have both been removed).

K11-Q4.qEn: In each `paths[]` entry of a `networking.k8s.io/v1` Ingress, which field is **mandatory** to specify how the URL is matched?
choicesEn: `regexMode: true`
`pathType` (with common values like `Prefix` or `Exact`)
`method: GET`
`containerPort: 3000`
K11-Q4.explainEn: Without `pathType: Prefix` (or `Exact` / `ImplementationSpecific`), the Kubernetes API Server rejects the manifest for missing a required field.

K11-Q5.qEn: When configuring HTTPS decryption (TLS Termination) on an `Ingress` under `spec.tls`, what does `secretName` point to?
choicesEn: A `.pem` file stored on your local laptop
A Kubernetes `Secret` (in the same namespace as the Ingress) containing the `tls.crt` certificate and `tls.key` private key
Your PostgreSQL login password
Your Docker Hub account
K11-Q5.explainEn: The Ingress Controller reads the digital certificate from a `kubernetes.io/tls` Kubernetes Secret in the same namespace to complete the HTTPS handshake with client browsers.

K11-Q6.qEn: In the successor **Kubernetes Gateway API** (`gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1`), which resource is written by application developers to define HTTP path routing rules and Canary traffic weights?
choicesEn: `PodSecurityPolicy`
`HTTPRoute`
`StatefulSet`
`ReplicaSet`
K11-Q6.explainEn: Gateway API separates listener infrastructure into `Gateway` and per-application HTTP routing rules into `HTTPRoute`.

K11-Q7.qEn: In `networking.k8s.io/v1` Ingress, what is the standard field placed directly under `spec:` to designate the controller class (e.g., `nginx`) instead of the old annotation: `spec.____`?
K11-Q7.explainEn: `spec.ingressClassName: nginx` is the official field replacing the legacy `kubernetes.io/ingress.class` annotation.

K11-FC1.frontEn: What is the difference between an **Ingress Resource** and an **Ingress Controller**?
K11-FC1.backEn:
- **Ingress Resource:** A YAML manifest declaring routing rules (`host`, `path` -> `Service`).
- **Ingress Controller:** The actual reverse proxy system (Nginx, Traefik, Envoy) running in the cluster to enforce those rules.

K11-FC2.frontEn: What is the difference between `pathType: Prefix` and `pathType: Exact` in Ingress?
K11-FC2.backEn:
- **`Prefix`:** Matches any path starting with the path segment prefix `/api` (`/api`, `/api/users`).
- **`Exact`:** Matches only that exact character-for-character path, not sub-paths.

K11-FC3.frontEn: How is the target Service specified in `networking.k8s.io/v1` Ingress?
K11-FC3.backEn:
```yaml
backend:
  service:
    name: api-svc
    port:
      number: 80
```

K11-FC4.frontEn: How does **TLS Termination** at the Ingress reduce overhead for internal Node.js applications?
K11-FC4.backEn: Ingress decrypts HTTPS at the cluster edge using the certificate in the Secret; traffic forwarded to the Node.js Pod is lightweight internal HTTP, so individual apps don't need to manage SSL certificate files.

K11-FC5.frontEn: What are the two biggest advantages of **Gateway API (`HTTPRoute`)** over traditional `Ingress`?
K11-FC5.backEn:
1) Separates Infrastructure management (`Gateway`) from Developer ownership (`HTTPRoute`);
2) Natively standardizes Canary splitting (`weight`) and header manipulation without vendor-specific annotations.

K11-FC6.frontEn: What is the most popular open-source tool on K8s for automatically issuing and renewing Let's Encrypt HTTPS certificates for Ingress?

K11-FC7.frontEn: Why is the industry strongly migrating from community `Ingress NGINX` to **Kubernetes Gateway API** in 2026?
K11-FC7.backEn: The community `kubernetes/ingress-nginx` project entered its retirement roadmap; **Gateway API** (`gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1`) powered by **Envoy Gateway**, **Cilium**, or **Traefik** standardizes routing & Canary splits without relying on a sprawling set of custom annotations.

Convert the legacy K8s 1.18 `Ingress` manifest (`networking.k8s.io/v1beta1`) below to the modern `networking.k8s.io/v1` standard with all 4 changes:

K12.titleEn: Configuration & Sensitive Data Management: ConfigMap and Secret
K12.summaryEn: Decouple 12-Factor configuration from images using ConfigMap & Secret, inject via envFrom / secretKeyRef / read-only Volumes, and understand the truth about Base64.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
When developing a Python (`FastAPI`) or Node.js application locally, you typically store configuration in a `.env` file. However, when running 30 Pods on Kubernetes across Dev, Staging, and Production:

- [!] You **cannot** hardcode database connection strings or CORS origins inside the Container Image via a Dockerfile's `ENV` instruction (because every environment differs!).
- [!] Even more critically, you **must never** bake database passwords, JWT signing keys, or OpenAI API keys into a Dockerfile or Git repository!

> [!NOTE] Distinguishing `ConfigMap` and `Secret` under the 12-Factor App principle
> Following the **12-Factor App** methodology, Kubernetes separates configuration into two resource types so different security policies and access controls can be enforced:
> - **`ConfigMap`:** Stores non-sensitive runtime parameters (`LOG_LEVEL=info`, `PORT=8000`, `nginx.conf` files) as plain text — safe to commit directly to Git.
> - **`Secret`:** Dedicated to sensitive information (DB passwords, TLS private keys, API keys), mounted into volatile RAM (`tmpfs`, never written to Worker Node disks) by Kubernetes and tightly governed via RBAC (similar to keeping a public notice board separate from locked confidential records).

```visual
kind: groups
title: Phân Tách Cấu Hình Chuẩn 12-Factor App — ConfigMap vs Secret
subtitle: Tách riêng giúp áp quyền RBAC nghiêm ngặt và bật mã hóa phần cứng KMS riêng cho dữ liệu nhạy cảm
```

```yaml Manifest ConfigMap chuẩn chứa các thông số môi trường công khai
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: api-config
data:
  LOG_LEVEL: "info"
  CORS_ORIGIN: "https://shop.example.com"
```

There are two primary ways to deliver a `ConfigMap` into a Pod — pay close attention to the major difference in **hot-reload** behavior between them:

```visual
kind: compare
title: Hai Cơ Chế Nạp ConfigMap Vào Pod — Biến Môi Trường vs Gắn Tệp Volume
subtitle: Nắm rõ hành vi cập nhật khi bạn sửa ConfigMap trên cụm đang chạy!
left:
  badge: "CÁCH 1 · Nạp biến môi trường (envFrom)"
  title: Bất biến suốt vòng đời tiến trình
  tone: sky
  code: |
    containers:
      - name: api
        image: ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:1.4.0
        envFrom:
          - configMapRef:
              name: api-config
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "==`envFrom`== nạp trọn gói **tất cả** các khóa trong `api-config` thành biến môi trường `LOG_LEVEL`, `CORS_ORIGIN` cho cả Python lẫn Node.js"
    - "**KHÔNG tự động đổi** khi bạn sửa `ConfigMap`! Biến môi trường của Linux chỉ nạp đúng 1 lần lúc khởi tạo tiến trình"
    - "Muốn nhận giá trị mới, cần chạy **`kubectl rollout restart deployment/...`**"
```

steps.headingEn: Secret: Understanding Base64 and Protecting Sensitive Data
steps.bodyEn:
When authoring a `Secret` manifest, the convenient ==`stringData:`== field lets you write readable plain text, and the Kubernetes API Server automatically encodes it into `Base64` strings stored under `data:`:

```yaml Khai báo Secret với stringData & nạp lẻ từng khóa qua secretKeyRef
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: db-credentials
type: Opaque
stringData:
  DB_PASSWORD: "placeholder-change-me"
---
# Trích đoạn nạp vào một biến môi trường cụ thể trong Pod / Deployment:
#   env:
#     - name: DATABASE_PASSWORD
#       valueFrom:
#         secretKeyRef:
#           name: db-credentials
#           key: DB_PASSWORD
```

> [!WARNING] Important security note: `Base64` is NOT cryptographic encryption!
> Many people see strings like `cGxhY2Vob2xkZXI=` inside a `Secret`'s `data:` field and feel safe pushing `secret.yaml` straight to GitHub. That is a critical mistake: ==Base64 is merely a text-representation encoding==, so anyone who can read the YAML file can decode it back to the original password in seconds with `echo "..." | base64 -d` or `base64.b64decode(...)` (like converting text to Morse code for transmission—it provides zero security).
