```visual
  title: Mọi Namespace thông suốt không rào chắn
  tone: rose
  code: |
    # Chưa có NetworkPolicy:
    [Pod: landing-page (ns: marketing)]
           │  (Kết nối thẳng không ai chặn!)
           ▼
    [Pod: postgres:5432 (ns: production)]
  lang: text
  bullets:
    - "Tạo `Namespace` mới **KHÔNG tự động dựng tường lửa mạng** ngăn cách các Pod"
    - "Chỉ cần 1 container ngoại vi bị xâm nhập, kẻ tấn công tự do dò quét ngang (*Lateral Movement*) khắp toàn cụm"
right:
  badge: "ZERO-TRUST · Default Deny + Whitelist"
  title: Khóa cửa mặc định · Chỉ mở đúng luồng hợp lệ
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    spec:
      podSelector: {}       # Khớp TẤT CẢ Pod trong Namespace!
      policyTypes:
        - Ingress           # Bỏ trống ingress -> Chặn 100% chiều vào!
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "**Bước 1 (`default-deny`):** Dùng đối tượng rỗng ==`podSelector: {}`== khóa sạch 100% kết nối gọi vào mọi Pod trong Namespace"
    - "**Bước 2 (`Additive Whitelist`):** Thêm luật cho phép có chọn lọc — nhiều `NetworkPolicy` cùng nhắm tới 1 Pod sẽ **cộng gộp (hợp)** các nguồn hợp lệ!"
```

> [!WARNING] Two real-world pitfalls when enabling `NetworkPolicy` for the first time
> 1. **Requires a supporting CNI Plugin:** The API Server only stores the `NetworkPolicy` specification; actual packet filtering is enforced by the **CNI Plugin** (**`Cilium`** eBPF, **`Calico`**, `Antrea`). If your cluster uses a minimal network plugin without policy support (like plain `flannel`), rules are silently ignored!
> 2. **Don't lock yourself out of DNS port `53`:** If you enable `policyTypes: ["Egress"]` (controlling outbound traffic), always remember to open `UDP/TCP 53` to `kube-system` so Pods can still resolve names via `CoreDNS`!

### Two steps to configure standard Zero-Trust (`networking.k8s.io/v1`):

1. **Step 1 — Lock down all inbound traffic with `default-deny-ingress`:**

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny-ingress
spec:
  podSelector: {}         # Áp dụng cho toàn bộ Pod trong Namespace hiện tại
  policyTypes:
    - Ingress             # Không có mục ingress: -> Từ chối 100% kết nối gọi vào!
```

2. **Step 2 — Selectively allow traffic (Only allow `shop-api` to call `postgres:5432`):**

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-api-to-postgres
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: postgres       # Bảo vệ các Pod Database
  policyTypes:
    - Ingress
  ingress:
    - from:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: shop-api   # CHỈ nhận kết nối từ các Pod của shop-api
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 5432
```

steps.headingEn: Helm Charts: The Package Manager of Kubernetes
steps.bodyEn:
Instead of duplicating dozens of nearly identical YAML files across `staging` and `production`, **Helm** bundles all application resources into a single package called a **Helm Chart**, combining dynamic templates (`templates/`) with a parameter file (`values.yaml`)!

```visual
kind: groups
title: Cấu Trúc Một Gói Helm Chart Chuẩn [!badge:sky:Package Manager]
subtitle: "Ánh xạ trực tiếp sang tư duy quản lý gói quen thuộc (pyproject.toml / package.json)"
columns: 2
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: file-code
    title: Chart.yaml
    badge: Định danh gói Chart
    tone: sky
    desc: Khai báo siêu dữ liệu của gói giống pyproject.toml hay package.json.
    bullets:
      - "Chứa tên gói (`name`), phiên bản Chart (`version`), phiên bản ứng dụng (`appVersion`) và các gói phụ thuộc (`dependencies`)"
    code: |
      apiVersion: v2
      name: shop-api
      version: 1.2.0
      appVersion: "2.1.0"
    codeLang: yaml
  - num: 2
    icon: code
    title: "templates/*.yaml"
    badge: Khuôn mẫu động
    tone: cyan
    desc: Các tệp YAML chứa biểu thức nội suy Go Template.
    bullets:
      - "Đọc giá trị từ `.Values`, hỗ trợ hàm mặc định như `{{ .Values.replicaCount | default 2 }}`"
    code: |
      spec:
        replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount | default 2 }}
        image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"
    codeLang: yaml
  - num: 3
    icon: settings
    title: values.yaml
    badge: Cấu hình mặc định gốc
    tone: emerald
    desc: Bộ thông số mặc định đi kèm sẵn bên trong Chart.
    bullets:
      - "Cung cấp giá trị an toàn mặc định cho `replicaCount`, `image.repository`, `resources`..."
    code: |
      replicaCount: 3
      image:
        repository: ghcr.io/acme/shop-api
        tag: "2.1.0"
    codeLang: yaml
  - num: 4
    icon: rocket
    title: "values-staging.yaml / values-prod.yaml"
    badge: Ghi đè theo môi trường
    tone: amber
    desc: Truyền cờ -f lúc triển khai và hỗ trợ quay lui toàn bộ gói.
    bullets:
      - "Lệnh chuẩn idempotent (vừa cài mới nếu chưa có, vừa nâng cấp nếu đã có): ==`helm upgrade --install`=="
      - "Lưu lịch sử **Release Revision** để quay lui đồng bộ cả 8 tài nguyên bằng `helm rollback`"
    code: |
      helm upgrade --install shop ./chart -f values-prod.yaml
      helm rollback shop 1
    codeLang: shell
```

steps.headingEn: 2026 Perspective: Choosing Helm vs Kustomize (kubectl apply -k) & GitOps Workflows?
steps.bodyEn:
In the 2026 Kubernetes ecosystem, you aren't always forced to use Helm's `{{ ... }}` templates! The community uses **two complementary packaging approaches side by side**:

```visual
kind: compare
title: "So Sánh Hai Chuẩn Đóng Gói Cấu Hình K8s Năm 2026: Helm vs Kustomize"
subtitle: "Cả hai đều được hỗ trợ hạng nhất (first-class) bên trong ArgoCD và Flux GitOps!"
left:
  badge: "TEMPLATING + PACKAGE · Helm v3/v4"
  title: Khuôn mẫu động & Kho gói cộng đồng
  tone: sky
  code: |
    # Cài đặt gói bên thứ ba hoặc app đa biến số:
    helm upgrade --install shop ./chart \
      -f values-prod.yaml
  lang: shell
  bullets:
    - "**Cơ chế:** Dùng cú pháp khuôn mẫu `{{ .Values.xxx }}` để sinh ra YAML"
    - "**Mạnh nhất khi:** Cài đặt phần mềm hạ tầng bên thứ ba (`cert-manager`, `Envoy Gateway`, `Prometheus`, `CloudNativePG`) hoặc đóng gói sản phẩm phân phối cho nhiều khách hàng"
    - "Tích hợp sẵn quản lý vòng đời bản phát hành (`helm list`, `helm rollback`)"
right:
  badge: "NATIVE YAML OVERLAYS · Kustomize"
  title: Tích hợp sẵn trong kubectl apply -k
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    # Áp lớp ghi đè (overlay) không cần sửa YAML gốc:
    # base/deployment.yaml + overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml
    kubectl apply -k overlays/prod
  lang: shell
  bullets:
    - "**Cơ chế:** Giữ nguyên **100% tệp YAML thuần hợp lệ** ở `base/`, rồi đắp các bản vá nhỏ (`patches`, đổi `replicas`, nâng `newTag` image) ở từng thư mục `overlays/staging`, `overlays/prod`"
    - "**Mạnh nhất khi:** Quản lý các microservice nội bộ (Python, Node.js, Go) của công ty — đọc dễ hiểu, không sợ lỗi thụt lề Go Template, chạy sẵn bằng **`kubectl apply -k`** không cần cài thêm CLI!"
```

> [!TIP] Enterprise automation landscape: GitOps with `ArgoCD` / `Flux`
> In 2026 Production environments, engineers no longer manually run `kubectl apply` or `helm upgrade` from a personal laptop! Every change (Helm's `values-prod.yaml` or Kustomize's `kustomization.yaml`) is committed to Git, and an in-cluster **GitOps controller (`ArgoCD` or `Flux`)** automatically pulls and reconciles it — making Git the *Single Source of Truth*.
> *(You can open the **CI/CD & GitOps Mastery** app to practice that full automation workflow!)*

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - Default K8s networking is **Allow All across all Namespaces** · `NetworkPolicy` requires a **policy-capable CNI** (**Cilium / Calico / Antrea**) to actually drop packets!
> - **`podSelector: {}`** matches every Pod in the Namespace · Multiple `NetworkPolicy` rules operate as an **Additive Whitelist**.
> - Choose **`Helm`** (`Chart.yaml` + `values.yaml`, `helm upgrade --install`) when you need parameterized packaging or third-party charts; choose **`Kustomize`** (`base/` + `overlays/`, `kubectl apply -k`) when you prefer clean, template-free plain YAML overlays for GitOps.

readings.noteEn: Baseline Zero-Trust policy for every production Namespace: blocks all inbound traffic by default and opens UDP/TCP port 53 for CoreDNS resolution.
readings.taskEn: When blocking outbound traffic (Egress), why is it mandatory to add an exception for UDP and TCP port 53?
readings.answerEn: If you lock down all Egress without opening port 53 to CoreDNS (kube-system), a Node.js app cannot resolve any Service or API domain names (failing with EAI_AGAIN / ENOTFOUND), paralyzing all network communication!

readings.noteEn: Micro-segmentation firewall rule protecting PostgreSQL: accepts TCP 5432 traffic only from Pods labeled app: shop-api.
readings.taskEn: What happens if a Pod labeled app: marketing-landing attempts to open a connection to Postgres port 5432?
readings.answerEn: The CNI Plugin (such as Cilium/Calico) silently drops the SYN packets at the kernel networking layer, causing connections from marketing-landing to hang until Connection Timed Out without ever reaching the Database.

readings.noteEn: Enterprise-grade values-prod.yaml file overriding production settings on a Helm Chart without modifying any original template YAML files.
readings.taskEn: Compare managing 3 environments using 3 files (values-dev.yaml, values-staging.yaml, values-prod.yaml) versus copy-pasting 3 separate YAML directories.
readings.answerEn: With Helm, you maintain only 1 canonical templates/ directory; when adding a new field (like startupProbe), you update the template once and all 3 environments inherit it in sync, differing only in the parameterized values in each values file.

K17-Q1.qEn: Under Kubernetes' default behavior when you have NOT created any `NetworkPolicy`, how do Pods communicate with one another?
choicesEn: All Pods are completely blocked and cannot call each other even within the same Namespace
Only Pods in the same Namespace can call each other; cross-Namespace traffic is blocked automatically
Completely flat network: any Pod in any Namespace can connect directly to any other Pod across the entire cluster
Only LoadBalancer Services are allowed to send internal packets
K17-Q1.explainEn: Default K8s networking is "Allow All" across all Namespaces. To isolate tiers or environments, you must apply NetworkPolicy (backed by a supporting CNI like Calico/Cilium).

K17-Q2.qEn: In a `NetworkPolicy`, which `podSelector` syntax means **"Apply this policy to ALL Pods in the current Namespace"**?
K17-Q2.explainEn: An empty object `podSelector: {}` matches all Pods in the Namespace (whereas omitting the podSelector key entirely is a syntax error missing a required field).

K17-Q3.qEn: Kubernetes enforces `NetworkPolicy` natively without depending on any CNI network plugin: even if a cluster uses basic networking like plain `flannel`, port-blocking rules take effect immediately.
K17-Q3.explainEn: False! A NetworkPolicy object is merely a rule specification; actual packet filtering is handled by the CNI Plugin (such as Cilium, Calico, Antrea, or Weave Net). If the CNI doesn't support it, rules are silently ignored!

K17-Q4.qEn: In a standard **Helm Chart** structure, which file serves the equivalent role of `package.json` in Node.js (declaring the Chart name, `version`, `appVersion`, and `dependencies`)?
choicesEn: Chart.yaml
values.yaml
helmfile.lock
package-chart.json
K17-Q4.explainEn: Chart.yaml holds the Helm Chart's identifying metadata and dependencies, while values.yaml holds the default configuration variables.

K17-Q5.qEn: When rendering the Helm template expression `replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount | default 2 }}` with a `values.yaml` file containing `replicaCount: 5`, what numeric value is produced in the resulting YAML line?
K17-Q5.explainEn: The pipeline function `| default 2` only falls back to 2 when `.Values.replicaCount` is empty/missing; since values.yaml supplies 5, the rendered result is 5.

K17-Q6.qEn: When multiple `NetworkPolicy` objects target the same Database Pod, the resulting allow rules (`ingress`/`egress`) are additive (the union of all permitted sources).
K17-Q6.explainEn: True! NetworkPolicy in K8s has no Deny-overrides-Allow rule ordering like traditional firewalls: once a Pod is selected by at least one policy, traffic is allowed if it matches AT LEAST ONE allow rule.

K17-Q7.qEn: Which Helm command both installs a new release if it does not yet exist and smoothly upgrades it if it already exists, using the `values-prod.yaml` override file?
choicesEn: helm init shop ./chart --prod
helm upgrade --install shop ./chart -f values-prod.yaml
helm push shop ./chart --values values-prod.yaml
kubectl helm apply -f values-prod.yaml
K17-Q7.explainEn: `helm upgrade --install <release> <chart> -f values-prod.yaml` is the standard idempotent command used both manually and in CI/CD Pipelines.

K17-C1.frontEn: How do you write a `NetworkPolicy` that blocks all inbound traffic by default (Default Deny Ingress) for a Namespace?
K17-C1.backEn: Set `spec.podSelector: {}`, `spec.policyTypes: ["Ingress"]`, and intentionally OMIT the `spec.ingress` field.

K17-C2.frontEn: What is the difference between two separate list items vs combining them in one item under `ingress[].from` in a NetworkPolicy?
K17-C2.backEn: Two separate `- namespaceSelector` and `- podSelector` items form a logical `OR`; placing both inside a single list item `- namespaceSelector: ... podSelector: ...` forms a logical `AND` (much stricter!).

K17-C3.frontEn: What are the three core components inside a Helm Chart directory?
K17-C3.backEn: 1) `Chart.yaml` (package metadata), 2) `values.yaml` (default configuration values), 3) `templates/` (templated YAML files containing `{{ .Values... }}`).

K17-C4.frontEn: How can you preview the YAML output Helm will generate locally without actually deploying to a K8s cluster?
K17-C4.backEn: Run `helm template shop ./chart -f values-prod.yaml` (or add `--dry-run` to `helm upgrade --install`).

K17-C5.frontEn: What risk occurs if you create a `NetworkPolicy` restricting `policyTypes: ["Egress"]` and forget to allow port 53?
K17-C5.backEn: The Pod completely loses the ability to query CoreDNS (port 53 UDP/TCP), preventing it from resolving any internal or external domain names.

K17-C6.frontEn: How does GitOps (with ArgoCD / Flux) integrate with Helm in 2026 architectures?
K17-C6.backEn: After CI builds the image, it only updates the new tag in `values-prod.yaml` in Git; ArgoCD running inside the K8s cluster detects the Git change and renders & syncs the Helm Chart into the cluster.

K17-C7.frontEn: When should you prefer **Kustomize (`kubectl apply -k`)** over **Helm**?
K17-C7.backEn: When managing internal microservices and wanting to keep **100% valid plain YAML files** in `base/` with layered overlays (`overlays/staging`, `overlays/prod`) without learning Go Template `{{ ... }}` syntax.

kube-ex-k17-1.titleEn: Configure a Default-Deny Ingress firewall for the entire Namespace
kube-ex-k17-1.promptEn:
The first step of Zero-Trust networking is blocking all inbound connections by default for every Pod in the current Namespace.

Write a `NetworkPolicy` (`apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1`) named `default-deny-ingress` with:
1. `spec.podSelector: {}` (applies to all Pods).
2. `spec.policyTypes` containing `"Ingress"`.
3. No `spec.ingress` field declared (remove any existing open-all rules if present).
hintsEn: Delete the `ingress:` block at the bottom of the starter file and change `podSelector:` to `podSelector: {}`.
Add `policyTypes: ["Ingress"]` right below `podSelector: {}`.

kube-ex-k17-2.titleEn: Write a NetworkPolicy allowing only shop-api to connect to PostgreSQL port 5432
kube-ex-k17-2.promptEn:
After locking down with Default-Deny, open a single connection path allowing the Backend tier to reach the database using a `NetworkPolicy` named `allow-api-to-postgres` (`networking.k8s.io/v1`):

1. Protect the Database Pods: `spec.podSelector.matchLabels` is `{ app: postgres }`.
2. `spec.policyTypes: ["Ingress"]`.
3. Inside `spec.ingress[0]`: allow only source `from[0].podSelector.matchLabels: { app: shop-api }` to reach `ports[0].port: 5432` (`protocol: TCP`).
hintsEn: The outer `spec.podSelector` selects the target to protect (`app: postgres`), while `from[0].podSelector` inside `ingress` selects the allowed caller (`app: shop-api`).

kube-ex-k17-3.titleEn: Configure values.yaml to render a Helm Chart for the shop-api service
kube-ex-k17-3.promptEn:
The Platform team has packaged a company-wide standard Helm Chart. You only need to edit **`values.yaml`** (no manual Deployment writing!) so Helm renders the exact desired configuration:

1. `replicaCount: 3`
2. `image.repository: ghcr.io/acme/shop-api`
3. `image.tag: "2.1.0"`
4. `service.port: 80`
hintsEn: Click Dry Run to immediately inspect both the `Deployment` and `Service` resources rendered by Helm from your `values.yaml`!

kube-ex-k17-4.titleEn: Override Resource & Security parameters in values-prod.yaml
kube-ex-k17-4.promptEn:
To deploy the release to Production (`helm upgrade --install shop ./chart -f values-prod.yaml`), complete the **`values-prod.yaml`** override file to meet operational standards:

1. `replicaCount: 4`
2. `resources.requests.cpu: "250m"` and `resources.requests.memory: "256Mi"`
3. `resources.limits.memory: "512Mi"`
4. `securityContext.runAsNonRoot: true`
hintsEn: Update all 4 settings in `values-prod.yaml`: `replicaCount: 4`, `cpu: "250m"`, `limits.memory: "512Mi"`, and `runAsNonRoot: true`.

K18.summaryEn: Practice terminal-based diagnostics and hotfix 4 classic Kubernetes startup failures: Pending, ImagePullBackOff, CreateContainerConfigError, and CrashLoopBackOff.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
In theory, every YAML file you write transitions smoothly to a healthy green `Running` state. In reality, during an on-call shift as a Backend or DevOps engineer, 80% of your expertise shines the moment you run `kubectl get pods` and see alarming statuses: `Pending`, `ImagePullBackOff`, `CreateContainerConfigError`, or ==`CrashLoopBackOff`==!

When an incident hits, beginners often rush to delete and recreate the Pod or tweak the YAML file by guesswork. Experienced engineers, on the other hand, systematically follow the **3-Step K8s Triage** workflow.

```visual
kind: illustration
diagram: "kube:k18"
alt: "Cây quyết định chẩn đoán sự cố khởi động Pod từ Pending, ImagePullBackOff, CreateContainerConfigError đến CrashLoopBackOff --previous"
title: "Sơ Đồ Quyết Định Chẩn Đoán Lỗi Khởi Động Pod: Đọc Events Hạ Tầng vs Logs Phiên Cũ"
subtitle: "Rẽ nhánh chính xác ngay từ giây thứ 5 dựa trên việc tiến trình ứng dụng đã từng được chạy hay chưa"
caption: "Sơ đồ phân nhánh chẩn đoán SRE giữa 3 lỗi kẹt trước vạch xuất phát (xem describe pod) và lỗi sập sau khi chạy (xem logs --previous)"
callouts:
  - num: 1
    label: "Bước 1: Nhìn cột STATUS & RESTARTS trên get pods"
    desc: "Xác định nhanh tên trạng thái báo lỗi và con số RESTARTS để biết container đã từng thực thi dòng code nào hay chưa."
    tone: sky
  - num: 2
    label: "Nhánh chưa kịp chạy: Pending / ImagePull / ConfigError"
    desc: "Ứng dụng chưa bật nên log trống trơn; 100% nguyên nhân (thiếu RAM/PVC, sai tag ảnh, thiếu Secret) nằm ở Events của describe pod."
    tone: amber
  - num: 3
    label: "Nhánh chạy rồi sập: CrashLoopBackOff (logs --previous)"
    desc: "Tiến trình Python / Node.js đã chạy nhưng văng lỗi thoát != 0; dùng cờ --previous để đọc trọn vẹn Traceback của phiên vừa sập."
    tone: rose
```

steps.headingEn: The Standard 3-Step Pod Triage Workflow (get → describe → logs)
steps.bodyEn:
Whenever a Pod fails to reach `READY 1/1` and `Running`, inspect it from the outside in and **branch accurately based on whether the container has ever executed a single line of code**:

```visual
kind: flow
title: Quy Trình Chẩn Đoán 3 Bước Chuẩn SRE (3-Step K8s Triage)
subtitle: Phân nhánh rõ ràng giữa lỗi hạ tầng TRƯỚC khi bật container và lỗi mã nguồn BÊN TRONG container
footer: "Chỉ duy nhất CrashLoopBackOff (trong 4 trạng thái kẹt đầu) là tiến trình code đã chạy thật sự nên mới có dữ liệu trong kubectl logs!"
steps:
  - icon: search
    badge: Bước 1 · Toàn cảnh
    title: Kiểm Tra Trạng Thái Pod
    desc: Xác định chính xác chữ báo lỗi ở cột STATUS và số lần RESTARTS
    code: "kubectl get pods -n <ns>"
    tone: sky
    edge: nếu kẹt TRƯỚC khi chạy
  - icon: doctor
    badge: Bước 2 · Sự kiện Hạ tầng
    title: Đọc Events Cuối Trang
    desc: Dùng cho Pending, ImagePullBackOff, CreateContainerConfigError (chưa có log!)
    code: "kubectl describe pod <pod>"
    tone: amber
    edge: nếu code ĐÃ chạy rồi sập
  - icon: terminal
    badge: Bước 3 · Nhật ký Code
    title: Đọc Traceback Phiên Cũ
    desc: Dùng cho CrashLoopBackOff, Error hoặc RESTARTS > 0 để bắt ngoại lệ Python/JS
    code: "kubectl logs <pod> --previous"
    tone: rose
```

> [!WARNING] Golden rule that saves 90% of your on-call time!
> If a Pod is in **`Pending`**, **`ImagePullBackOff`**, or **`CreateContainerConfigError`**, your application container **has never started for even 1 millisecond**! Running `kubectl logs` or `kubectl exec` at that point is completely useless — 100% of the answer lives in the ==`Events:`== section at the bottom of **`kubectl describe pod <pod-name>`**! Out of these 4 states, **only `CrashLoopBackOff`** proves that the application container actually started.

steps.headingEn: Analyzing the 4 Common Startup Error States
steps.bodyEn:
Map each error state to the exact bottleneck in the Pod startup lifecycle so you can pinpoint the root cause within seconds:

```visual
kind: troubleshoot
title: Bảng Chẩn Đoán 4 Trạng Thái Lỗi Khởi Động Phổ Biến [!badge:rose:On-Call Playbook]
subtitle: Triệu chứng trên get pods -> Thủ phạm gốc rễ -> Câu lệnh chẩn đoán quyết định
items:
  - symptom: "1. Pending (Tắc ở khâu Lập lịch & Gắn đĩa — kube-scheduler / CSI)"
    badge: Chưa xếp được Node
    tone: amber
    cause: "PVC chưa `Bound` được ổ đĩa (`Warning FailedScheduling: pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims` do gõ sai tên `storageClassName` kiểu `fast-ssd-typo`), hoặc toàn cụm cạn sạch CPU/RAM không Node nào đủ đáp ứng `resources.requests`."
    fix: "Đọc Events của Pod, sau đó kiểm tra trạng thái PVC và đối chiếu danh sách StorageClass có thật trên cụm."
    cmd: kubectl describe pod <name> && kubectl get pvc && kubectl get storageclass
  - symptom: "2. ErrImagePull / ImagePullBackOff (Tắc ở khâu Kéo ảnh — containerd)"
    badge: Không tải được Image
    tone: rose
    cause: "Gõ sai tên Image hoặc sai tag phiên bản không tồn tại trên GHCR/Docker Hub (ví dụ `1.4.0-typo`), hoặc kéo từ kho ảnh riêng tư (Private Registry) nhưng quên gắn `imagePullSecrets` (bị từ chối 401/403 Unauthorized)."
    fix: "Đọc dòng `Failed to pull image ... not found / unauthorized` ở mục Events của `describe pod`, sửa lại đúng tag hoặc bổ sung `imagePullSecrets`."
    cmd: kubectl describe pod <name>
  - symptom: "3. CreateContainerConfigError (Tắc ở khâu Lắp ráp Env/Mount — kubelet)"
    badge: Thiếu ConfigMap / Secret
    tone: cyan
    cause: "Xảy ra TRƯỚC KHI container chạy: Pod tham chiếu tới một `Secret` hoặc `ConfigMap` chưa từng được tạo trong cùng Namespace, hoặc gõ lệch tên khóa trong `secretKeyRef` / `configMapKeyRef`."
    fix: "Xem Events để biết thiếu chính xác tên Secret/ConfigMap hay key nào, rồi đối chiếu danh sách thực tế trong Namespace."
    cmd: kubectl describe pod <name> && kubectl get secrets,cm
  - symptom: "4. CrashLoopBackOff (Tắc ở khâu Thực thi mã nguồn — Tiến trình Python / Node.js)"
    badge: Code chạy lên rồi sập!
    tone: rose
    cause: "Image đã tải xong, cấu hình đã nạp đủ, container chạy `uvicorn` / `node` nhưng văng lỗi thoát mã `!= 0` ngay lập tức (như `ModuleNotFoundError`, `ValidationError` hay `TypeError`)! kubelet khởi động lại theo chu kỳ lùi lũy thừa."
    fix: "Đọc bản ghi stdout/stderr kèm dòng Traceback của phiên container vừa chết ngay trước đó bằng cờ `--previous` (`-p`)."
    cmd: kubectl logs <name> --previous
```

steps.headingEn: Exponential Backoff & Reading Logs with --previous (-p) in CrashLoopBackOff
steps.bodyEn:
When an application crashes on startup (for example, a missing environment variable causing FastAPI's `pydantic-settings` to fail or a `TypeError` in Node.js), the container starts for `0.2 seconds` and exits. To prevent a failing container from continuously burning 100% CPU on a Worker Node, `kubelet` applies **Exponential Backoff**:

```visual
kind: flow
title: Quy Luật Lùi Lũy Thừa (Exponential Backoff) & Cách Bắt Trọn Stack Trace
subtitle: "Thời gian chờ khởi động lại nhân đôi liên tiếp và chạm trần tối đa ở 5 phút (300 giây)"
steps:
  - icon: flame
    badge: 0.2s đầu tiên
    title: Tiến Trình Sập (Exit != 0)
    desc: Ứng dụng văng ngoại lệ chưa bắt (Traceback / Uncaught Exception) và thoát lỗi ngay
    code: "Exit Code: 1"
    tone: rose
    edge: kubelet hãm phanh
  - icon: refresh
    badge: Nhân đôi chu kỳ nghỉ
    title: Exponential Backoff
    desc: Nghỉ tăng dần lũy thừa 10s -> 20s -> 40s -> 80s -> 160s...
    code: "10s -> 20s -> 40s..."
    tone: amber
    edge: khóa trần tối đa
  - icon: shield
    badge: Trần chờ 300s
    title: Chạm Trần 5 Phút
    desc: Thời gian chờ tối đa giữ ở mức 5 phút (300s) giữa mỗi lần thử bật lại
    code: "Max delay: 5m (300s)"
    tone: cyan
    edge: truy xuất phiên cũ
  - icon: terminal
    badge: Cờ quan trọng --previous
    title: Bắt Tận Tay Stack Trace
    desc: Lấy trọn vẹn stdout/stderr của phiên bản container vừa mới chết ngay trước đó!
    code: "kubectl logs <pod> --previous"
    tone: emerald
```

If you run `kubectl logs <pod>` right as `kubelet` spins up a new container before it prints the error, the output may be blank. Adding the ==`--previous`== flag (shorthand `-p`) is essential:

```bash
kubectl logs order-worker-10001 --previous
```

> [!TIP] Speed up real-world terminal diagnostics with `k9s` & `kubectl debug`
> - In the **`k9s`** TUI, simply highlight the failing Pod and press **`d`** (equivalent to `describe`), **`l`** (view `logs`), or **`p`** (immediately view `logs --previous`!) in half a second!
> - If you run into a minimal container (such as Distroless) that lacks `/bin/sh` for `exec`, modern K8s provides **`kubectl debug -it <pod> --image=busybox:1.36`** to attach an ephemeral diagnostic container sharing the same network namespace as that Pod!

steps.headingEn: Hands-On Troubleshooting Guide
steps.bodyEn:
In the 4 on-call drills `K18.1` → `K18.4` right after this lesson:

- [x] **Step 1 — Diagnose with the real Terminal:** You are given a **Diagnostic Terminal** connected directly to a simulated cluster experiencing an incident. Run diagnostic commands first (`kubectl get pods`, `kubectl describe pod ...`, `kubectl get pvc`, `kubectl logs ... --previous`) to uncover concrete evidence instead of guessing!
- [x] **Step 2 — Submit your YAML patch:** Once you identify the root cause, fix the YAML configuration in the editor below and click Grade — the simulator will automatically `apply` your patch and verify that the Pods turn green (**`Running` (`Ready`)**).

> [!REMEMBER] Pocket Takeaways
> - **`Pending`**, **`ImagePullBackOff`**, and **`CreateContainerConfigError`** happen **BEFORE the container runs** → Always use **`kubectl describe pod <pod>`** and read **`Events`** (there are no `logs`!).
> - **`CrashLoopBackOff`** is the only state among the 4 where **code actually ran and crashed** → Exponential backoff **`10s → 20s → 40s...` (capped at `5m` / `300s`)** → Use **`kubectl logs <pod> --previous`**!
> - When you see `pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims` → Immediately check `kubectl get pvc` and `kubectl get storageclass`.

readings.noteEn: A real-world scenario where a Pod stays stuck in Pending: not due to insufficient CPU/RAM, but because its referenced PVC cannot be Bound.
readings.taskEn: Which command lets you quickly distinguish whether a Pod is Pending due to insufficient CPU/RAM on Nodes or a stuck PVC volume?
readings.answerEn: Run `kubectl describe pod <pod-name>` and read the Events section at the bottom: if resources are lacking, the Scheduler reports `Insufficient cpu/memory`, whereas a stuck volume reports `pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims`.

readings.noteEn: The most common cause of CreateContainerConfigError before even the first line of Node.js code executes.
readings.taskEn: Why does running `kubectl logs` on the failing Pod in this manifest return no useful output?
readings.answerEn: Because kubelet failed while assembling environment variables from the Secret before creating the container, so the Node.js process never ran! You must use `kubectl describe pod` to see the missing Secret or key name.

K18-Q1.qEn: When you run `kubectl get pods` and see a Pod stuck in `ImagePullBackOff`, what is the most accurate next command to find the specific reason?
choicesEn: kubectl logs <pod-name> --previous
kubectl describe pod <pod-name> (to read the detailed messages in the Events section at the bottom)
kubectl exec -it <pod-name> -- sh
kubectl top pod <pod-name>
K18-Q1.explainEn: In ImagePullBackOff, the container was never created or started, so both `logs` and `exec` are useless. All details (wrong tag, missing registry permissions) are in the Events section of `kubectl describe pod`.

K18-Q2.qEn: The `CreateContainerConfigError` state indicates that the Node.js process ran for 5 seconds and then threw a JavaScript syntax exception.
K18-Q2.explainEn: False! `CreateContainerConfigError` occurs BEFORE the container runs, because kubelet cannot find a `ConfigMap` or `Secret` (or a specific key) that the Pod requires.

K18-Q3.qEn: Which full CLI flag of `kubectl logs` lets you view the error logs (stack trace) of the previous container instance that just crashed in a `CrashLoopBackOff` loop?
K18-Q3.explainEn: The `--previous` flag (or shorthand `-p`) retrieves the stdout/stderr output of the failed container run immediately preceding the new container created by kubelet.

K18-Q4.qEn: You run `kubectl describe pod upload-worker` and see the event: `Warning FailedScheduling: pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims`. Which object should you inspect next?
choicesEn: Check `kubectl get pvc` and `kubectl get storageclass` to see if the PVC has a mismatched `storageClassName`
Check the Ingress TLS certificate
Check the CronJob schedule
Double the Deployment `replicas`
K18-Q4.explainEn: This message points directly to the culprit: the PVC mounted by the Pod has not been bound to an actual volume, usually due to a wrong `storageClassName` or mismatched `accessModes`.

K18-Q5.qEn: How does the restart wait time (back-off delay) between consecutive crashes in Kubernetes `CrashLoopBackOff` increase?
choicesEn: Fixed at exactly 1 second forever
Doubles exponentially (`10s → 20s → 40s → 80s...`) and caps at a maximum of 5 minutes (`300s`)
Waits exactly 24 hours after each crash
Automatically deletes the Pod permanently after the 3rd crash
K18-Q5.explainEn: kubelet applies an Exponential Backoff algorithm that doubles the delay up to a 5-minute cap to prevent a continuously crashing container from consuming 100% of a Worker Node's CPU.

K18-Q6.qEn: If a Pod pulls an image from a private registry (such as `private.registry.local/shop/api:1.0.0`) without `imagePullSecrets` configured, the Pod will enter `ErrImagePull` / `ImagePullBackOff`.
K18-Q6.explainEn: True! containerd on the Worker Node is rejected by the Registry server with an authentication error (401/403 Unauthorized) and cannot download the image layers, causing `ErrImagePull` followed by `ImagePullBackOff`.

K18-Q7.qEn: Among the 4 error states `Pending`, `ImagePullBackOff`, `CreateContainerConfigError`, and `CrashLoopBackOff`, which ONE state proves that the application container actually started?
K18-Q7.explainEn: Only `CrashLoopBackOff` means the image was pulled, configuration was mounted, and the process inside the container actually ran before repeatedly exiting with an error!

K18-C1.frontEn: What is the standard 3-step workflow to diagnose any failing Pod in K8s?
K18-C1.backEn: 1) `kubectl get pods` (identify the status), 2) `kubectl describe pod <name>` (read the `Events` section at the bottom), 3) `kubectl logs <name> --previous` (if the app actually started and crashed).

K18-C2.frontEn: What are the two main categories of causes that keep a Pod stuck in `Pending`?
K18-C2.backEn: 1) No Node has enough available CPU/RAM to satisfy `resources.requests` (or a Taint/NodeSelector blocks scheduling), 2) A `PVC` attached to the Pod is stuck and not yet `Bound`.

K18-C3.frontEn: What are the top three causes of `ErrImagePull` / `ImagePullBackOff`?
K18-C3.backEn: 1) A typo in the repository name or image `tag`, 2) The image was never pushed to the Registry, 3) A private registry is missing or has invalid `imagePullSecrets`.

K18-C4.frontEn: When does a Pod get blocked in `CreateContainerConfigError`?
K18-C4.backEn: When a container references a `Secret` or `ConfigMap` that does not exist in the same Namespace, or when the `key` specified in `secretKeyRef`/`configMapKeyRef` is missing.

K18-C5.frontEn: Why is the `--previous` flag so important when debugging `CrashLoopBackOff`?
K18-C5.backEn: Because the newly recreated container may not have written logs yet or may be waiting in backoff; `--previous` reads the intact stack trace from the container instance that just crashed.

K18-C6.frontEn: How can you quickly tell a K8s infrastructure/config error from a Node.js source code error just from the `STATUS` column?
K18-C6.backEn: `Pending`, `ImagePullBackOff`, `CreateContainerConfigError` = blocked at the K8s infrastructure/configuration layer; `CrashLoopBackOff` / `Error` = the application code (or `CMD`) exited with an error.

kube-ex-k18-1.titleEn: Drill #1 — Rescue the upload-worker Pod stuck in Pending
kube-ex-k18-1.promptEn:
The `upload-worker` Pod deployed earlier today is still stuck in **`Pending`**!

- **Diagnostic tip:** Try running `kubectl describe pod upload-worker` and `kubectl get pvc` in the **Diagnostic Terminal** to find the root cause.
- The cluster currently supports two valid storage classes: `standard` and **`gp3`**.
- **Task:** Update the `PersistentVolumeClaim` `upload-claim` manifest below to use the **`gp3`** SSD class so the volume becomes `Bound` and Pod `upload-worker` transitions to **`Running`**!
hintsEn: In the Diagnostic Terminal, `kubectl describe pod upload-worker` clearly reports `storageClass "fast-ssd-typo" not found`.
Change `storageClassName: fast-ssd-typo` to `storageClassName: gp3` in the YAML file below.

kube-ex-k18-2.titleEn: Drill #2 — Fix ImagePullBackOff on Deployment payment-api
kube-ex-k18-2.promptEn:
After the latest release, both Pods of `Deployment/payment-api` are failing in red **`ImagePullBackOff`**!

- Run `kubectl get pods` and `kubectl describe pod payment-api` in the **Diagnostic Terminal** to read the error message from the Container Registry.
- The internal image registry confirms that the valid newly released version is **`ghcr.io/acme/payment-api:1.4.0`**.
- **Task:** Fix the Image tag in the `Deployment` manifest below so both Pods transition to **`Running`**!
hintsEn: Remove the accidental `-typo` suffix from the `image:` field so it becomes `ghcr.io/acme/payment-api:1.4.0`.

kube-ex-k18-3.titleEn: Drill #3 — Resolve CreateContainerConfigError caused by a missing Secret
kube-ex-k18-3.promptEn:
Pod `auth-api` is blocked right at the starting line with **`CreateContainerConfigError`**!

- Run `kubectl describe pod auth-api` and `kubectl get secrets` in the **Diagnostic Terminal** to check the exact Secret name the Pod expects.
- **Task:** The `Secret` manifest below has a mismatched name (`auth-secret-wrong`) and is missing the `JWT_PUBLIC_KID` key. Fix `metadata.name` to match what Pod `auth-api` requires, and add `stringData.JWT_PUBLIC_KID: "kid-prod-2026"` so the Pod starts successfully!
hintsEn: `kubectl describe pod auth-api` clearly reports: `Error: secret "auth-jwt-secret" not found`.
Update `metadata.name: auth-jwt-secret` and set `JWT_PUBLIC_KID: "kid-prod-2026"` under `stringData:`.

kube-ex-k18-4.titleEn: Drill #4 — Read logs --previous to diagnose CrashLoopBackOff on order-worker
kube-ex-k18-4.promptEn:
Pod `order-worker-10001` belonging to `Deployment/order-worker` is restarting repeatedly in **`CrashLoopBackOff`** (5 crashes so far)!

Complete these **2 required steps**:
- **Step 1 (Required in the Diagnostic Terminal):** Run `kubectl logs order-worker-10001 --previous` in the **Diagnostic Terminal** above to read the stack trace from the previous crash and find the last known stable version number!
- **Step 2:** Update the `image` field in the `Deployment` manifest below to the stable version you found in Step 1 (`acme/order-worker:<version>`), then click Grade!
hintsEn: Don't forget to run `kubectl logs order-worker-10001 --previous` in the Diagnostic Terminal before clicking Grade!
The previous crash log indicates the stable tag is `1.9.4` → update `image: acme/order-worker:1.9.4`.

K19.titleEn: K8s Troubleshooting (Part 2): OOMKilled (137), 502 Bad Gateway & Rollback
K19.summaryEn: Tackle the 4 most common production incidents head-on: OOMKilled 137 memory exhaustion, empty Endpoints causing 502s, fast CLI Rollbacks, and Zero-Downtime configuration.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
In `K18`, you mastered diagnosing issues that prevent a Pod from ever starting. However, the most intense late-night on-call incidents happen when **all Pods appear to be `Running` smoothly**, or erupt **right in the middle of deploying a new release during peak traffic**!

In this capstone module, you will directly resolve the 4 most common production-grade operational incidents: memory exhaustion ==`OOMKilled` (`Exit Code 137`)==, broken service routing ==`502 Bad Gateway` (`Endpoints: <none>`)==, **rapid recovery with `kubectl rollout undo`**, and **eliminating dropped requests during Rolling Updates**.

```visual
kind: troubleshoot
title: Bảng Xử Lý Nhanh 3 Sự Cố Phổ Biến Khi Hệ Thống Đang Chạy [!badge:rose:SRE Playbook]
subtitle: Khi Pod vẫn hiển thị Running nhưng người dùng gặp lỗi — kiểm tra đúng bằng chứng thực tế trong vài giây
items:
  - symptom: "Sự cố #5 · Pod bị dừng đột ngột lúc tải nặng: OOMKilled (Exit Code: 137)"
    badge: "128 + 9 (SIGKILL) = 137"
    tone: rose
    cause: "Tiến trình Python / Node.js nạp cả tệp lớn hoặc DataFrame lên RAM vượt quá trần `resources.limits.memory` (ví dụ đặt quá chật `32Mi`), khiến cgroups OOM Killer bắn tín hiệu `SIGKILL (9)`."
    fix: "1) Trước mắt: Nâng `limits.memory` / `requests.memory` lên mức an toàn (`256Mi`–`512Mi`). 2) Căn cơ: Đổi code sang xử lý từng khúc luồng (Python Generator / `StreamingResponse` hoặc Node.js `stream.pipeline`)!"
    cmd: kubectl describe pod pdf-exporter-xxx
  - symptom: "Sự cố #6A · Pod 1/1 Running nhưng trả về lỗi 502 — ENDPOINTS hiện <none>"
    badge: Lệch nhãn selector
    tone: amber
    cause: "Trường `spec.selector` trên `Service` gõ lệch (ví dụ `app: checkout-backend`) không khớp với bộ nhãn `metadata.labels` thực tế trên các Pod (`app: checkout-api`), làm danh sách Endpoints rỗng không có IP nào!"
    fix: "Đối chiếu nhãn thật của Pod với `Selector` của Service và sửa lại `spec.selector` khớp khít 100% — mạng thông tức thì không cần restart Pod."
    cmd: kubectl get endpoints checkout-svc && kubectl get pods --show-labels
  - symptom: "Sự cố #6B · Pod 1/1 Running, Endpoints đã có IP nhưng vẫn 502 / Connection Refused"
    badge: Lệch cổng targetPort
    tone: cyan
    cause: "`selector` đã khớp nhưng `Service` cấu hình `targetPort: 8080` trong khi Uvicorn lắng nghe `8000` (hoặc Express lắng nghe `3000`). Gói tin bay tới đúng Pod nhưng đập vào cổng đóng kín!"
    fix: "Kiểm tra cổng mở thực tế trên container và chỉnh `spec.ports[].targetPort` của `Service` về đúng cổng ứng dụng đang mở."
    cmd: kubectl describe svc checkout-svc
```

steps.headingEn: Incident #5 — Pod Terminated for Exceeding RAM Limits: OOMKilled (Exit Code 137)
steps.bodyEn:
```visual
kind: illustration
diagram: "kube:k19"
alt: "Bản đồ xử lý sự cố Production gồm OOMKilled (Exit Code 137), đứt mạng 502 do Endpoints rỗng hoặc sai targetPort và khôi phục Rollout Undo"
title: "Quy Trình Xử Lý Sự Cố Production: OOMKilled (137), Lỗi 502 & Rollout Undo"
subtitle: "Quy trình xử lý nhanh 3 kịch bản sự cố xảy ra khi hệ thống đang phục vụ lưu lượng thực tế"
caption: "Ba quy trình xác định nguyên nhân và khôi phục tức thì cho lỗi tràn RAM (137), đứt cầu nối Service Endpoints (<none> / lệch cổng) và lỗi bản phát hành mới"
callouts:
  - num: 1
    label: "Lỗi tràn bộ nhớ OOMKilled (Exit 137 = 128 + SIGKILL 9)"
    desc: "Bắt bằng chứng trong Last State của describe pod; nâng trần limits.memory trước mắt và chuyển code đọc tệp lớn sang Streaming."
    tone: rose
  - num: 2
    label: "Pod Running nhưng khách nhận 502 (Endpoints: <none>)"
    desc: "Soi ngay kubectl get endpoints để phát hiện lệch nhãn selector hoặc lệch số cổng targetPort so với cổng thực tế."
    tone: amber
  - num: 3
    label: "Khôi phục bản phát hành lỗi trong vài giây"
    desc: "Nhờ maxUnavailable: 0 giữ bản cũ sống sót, chạy kubectl rollout undo để kéo toàn bộ hệ thống về Revision ổn định trước khi sửa lỗi."
    tone: emerald
```

Normally, the `pdf-exporter` invoice service stays `Running`. Yet whenever a customer requests a large report export, the connection drops abruptly, the `RESTARTS` count spikes, or `STATUS` flashes **`OOMKilled`**. Running `kubectl describe pod pdf-exporter-...` reveals the exact reason:

```text
Last State:   Terminated (Reason: OOMKilled, Exit Code: 137)
Limits:       memory=32Mi
```

> [!TIP] A 2-step workflow to permanently resolve `Exit Code 137` (`128 + 9 SIGKILL`) for both Python & Node.js
> - **Step 1 — Infrastructure (Immediate mitigation):** Raise `resources.limits.memory` (and `requests.memory`) in the `Deployment` to a realistic safe ceiling (`256Mi` or `512Mi`).
> - **Step 2 — Application Code (Root-cause fix):** Never load an entire 300MB file into a single in-memory variable!
>   - In **Python (`FastAPI` / `Pandas`):** Use chunked **`yield` generators + `StreamingResponse`** or `pd.read_csv(..., chunksize=5000)`.
>   - In **Node.js:** Switch from `fs.readFileSync` to **`fs.createReadStream` + `stream.pipeline`** with backpressure control to keep RAM usage flat at just a few dozen MB!

steps.headingEn: Incident #6 — Pods Are 1/1 Running, Yet the Service Returns 502 Bad Gateway
steps.bodyEn:
This is one of the most misleading failures: both `checkout-api` replicas show `1/1 Running`, logs print `Listening on 0.0.0.0:3000` with zero errors, yet every request sent through the Ingress/Gateway to `Service/checkout-svc` returns **`502 Bad Gateway`** or `Connection Refused`!

Don't stop at checking the Pods — inspect the **`Endpoints`** bridge immediately with these 3 quick checks in 5 seconds:

```bash
kubectl get endpoints checkout-svc
kubectl get pods --show-labels
kubectl describe svc checkout-svc
```

- [!] **If `ENDPOINTS` shows `<none>`:** It is 100% certain that the `Service`'s `spec.selector` has a mismatch with the Pods' `metadata.labels` (or every Pod's `readinessProbe` is failing)!
- [!] **If `ENDPOINTS` lists Pod IPs but you still get `502` / `Connection Refused`:** The `Service` is pointing to the wrong `targetPort` (e.g., `targetPort: 8080` while the app listens on port `3000` or `8000`, or the app forgot to bind to `0.0.0.0`!). Align `selector` and `targetPort`, and traffic recovers immediately!

steps.headingEn: Incident #7 — Rapid Service Recovery with kubectl rollout undo
steps.bodyEn:
Suppose at 8:00 PM during a peak promotional sale, a newly deployed `v3.0.0` release in the `production` namespace sends the `frontend` UI into `CrashLoopBackOff`.

> [!WARNING] SRE Principle for Bad Deployments: Mitigate First, Investigate Later
> Never open your IDE to debug code and wait 15 minutes for CI/CD to rebuild a Docker image while customers stare at a broken error page! Your top priority is slashing **Mean Time to Recovery (`MTTR`)** down to seconds using ==`kubectl rollout undo`==!

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Quy Trình Xử Lý Khi Đẩy Bản Lỗi Lên Production Giờ Cao Điểm (Tối Ưu MTTR)"
subtitle: "Ưu tiên hàng đầu của SRE là khôi phục dịch vụ cho khách hàng trong vài giây trước khi phân tích nguyên nhân"
left:
  badge: "PHẢN ỨNG SAI · Chậm 15 Phút"
  title: Sửa code trực tiếp khi sự cố đang diễn ra
  tone: rose
  code: |
    # Khách hàng gặp lỗi trắng trang suốt 15 phút:
    1. Đọc log tìm nguyên nhân (5 phút)
    2. Sửa vội code -> git push (2 phút)
    3. Chờ CI test & build lại Docker Image (8 phút)
  lang: text
  bullets:
    - "Hàng ngàn khách hàng thoát giỏ hàng trong lúc chờ pipeline CI chạy lại"
    - "Sửa code trong tâm lý áp lực rất dễ phát sinh lỗi mới chồng lên lỗi cũ"
right:
  badge: "CHUẨN SRE · Khôi Phục Trong 3 Giây"
  title: Quay lui tức khắc bằng kubectl rollout undo
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    # Xem nhanh lịch sử các bản phát hành:
    kubectl rollout history deployment/frontend -n production

    # Khôi phục nhanh về bản ổn định liền trước!
    kubectl rollout undo deployment/frontend -n production
  lang: shell
  bullets:
    - "Tận dụng ngay bản **ReplicaSet Revision ổn định liền trước** được K8s lưu sẵn để khôi phục dịch vụ trong **3 giây**"
    - "Sau khi hệ thống đã xanh trở lại và khách mua hàng bình thường, mới bình tĩnh kéo log về Staging sửa code căn cơ!"
```

steps.headingEn: Incident #8 — 3 Core Mechanisms for Zero-Downtime Rolling Updates
steps.bodyEn:
Finally, for an API service to achieve true **100% Zero-Downtime** — deploying multiple times a day without dropping a single customer connection — you must combine all **3 core mechanisms** below in the same `Deployment`:

```visual
kind: groups
title: 3 Cơ Chế Đảm Bảo 100% Zero-Downtime Rolling Update [!badge:emerald:Tổng Kết Khóa Học]
subtitle: Thiếu bất kỳ 1 trong 3 chốt chặn này đều sẽ gây rớt request (502/503) trong vài giây chuyển giao phiên bản!
columns: 3
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: layers
    title: Chiến Lược RollingUpdate
    badge: "maxUnavailable: 0"
    tone: sky
    desc: Chống sụt giảm năng lực chịu tải khi thay ca Pod.
    bullets:
      - "Nếu để `maxUnavailable: 25%` hay `50%`, K8s giết bớt Pod cũ ngay lập tức trước khi Pod mới kịp chạy"
      - "Bắt buộc đặt **`maxUnavailable: 0`** và **`maxSurge: 1`** (bật thêm 1 Pod mới khỏe hẳn rồi mới tắt 1 Pod cũ!)"
    code: |
      strategy:
        type: RollingUpdate
        rollingUpdate:
          maxUnavailable: 0
          maxSurge: 1
    codeLang: yaml
  - num: 2
    icon: shield-check
    title: Kiểm Tra readinessProbe
    badge: Chặn bơm khách quá sớm
    tone: emerald
    desc: Chỉ mở cổng đón khách khi FastAPI / Node.js & DB Pool đã sẵn sàng.
    bullets:
      - "Nếu thiếu `readinessProbe`, Pod mới vừa tạo container đã bị bơm khách vào dù cổng HTTP chưa mở xong"
      - "Kiểm tra `/readyz` định kỳ (`periodSeconds: 5`)"
    code: |
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /readyz
          port: 3000
        periodSeconds: 5
    codeLang: yaml
  - num: 3
    icon: shield
    title: Hook lifecycle.preStop
    badge: Đồng bộ hóa trước khi tắt Pod
    tone: amber
    desc: Chờ mạng cụm gỡ sạch IP trước khi đóng cổng HTTP.
    bullets:
      - "Ngủ đệm 5 giây để Gateway/Ingress & `kube-proxy` kịp xóa IP Pod (1–3s) trước khi gửi `SIGTERM`"
      - "Đi kèm `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30` để xả êm giao dịch dở dang"
    code: |
      lifecycle:
        preStop:
          exec:
            command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 5"]
    codeLang: yaml
```

Congratulations on reaching the final challenge of the **Hands-On Docker & Kubernetes** journey — complete the last 4 incident drills to prove your mastery of production clusters!

> [!REMEMBER] Pocket Takeaways
> - **`OOMKilled` (`Exit Code 137` = `128 + 9 SIGKILL`)** → Increase `limits.memory` + switch to streaming (**Python `StreamingResponse`/Generator** or **Node.js `stream.pipeline`**).
> - Pods `1/1 Running` but `502` errors: check `kubectl get endpoints <svc>` → If `<none>`, it's a **mismatched `selector`**; if IPs are present, it's a **mismatched `targetPort`**.
> - Broken release during peak hours → Prioritize lowering MTTR with **`kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name> -n <namespace>`** first, fix code later!
> - The inseparable Zero-Downtime trio: **`maxUnavailable: 0` (`maxSurge: 1`)** + **`readinessProbe`** + **`lifecycle.preStop` (`sleep 5`)**.

readings.noteEn: A classic incident that fools engineers: Pods report Running 1/1 normally, yet every external user behind the Ingress receives 502 Bad Gateway.
readings.taskEn: Find both mismatches between the Deployment and the Service in this manifest.
readings.answerEn: 1) The Service sets selector `app: shop-backend`, which mismatches the Pod label `app: shop-api`, leaving Endpoints empty (<none>); 2) The Service forwards to `targetPort: 8080`, whereas the container only listens on port `3000`.

readings.noteEn: A complete blueprint preventing dropped packets during Rolling Updates for a high-traffic Node.js application.
readings.taskEn: List the 3 mechanisms working together in this manifest to ensure customers never experience 502 errors during a new release.
readings.answerEn: 1) RollingUpdate with maxUnavailable: 0 & maxSurge: 1, 2) readinessProbe checking /readyz before allowing traffic, and 3) lifecycle.preStop sleeping 5 seconds along with terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30 before closing the TCP port.

K19-Q1.qEn: When a Node.js container allocates RAM beyond `resources.limits.memory` and is killed by the Linux kernel with `SIGKILL (9)` (`OOMKilled`), what `Exit Code` is displayed in `kubectl describe pod`?
K19-Q1.explainEn: By Unix/Linux convention, the exit code for a process terminated by signal N is 128 + N = 128 + 9 (SIGKILL) = 137.

K19-Q2.qEn: You observe that all 3 Pods of `checkout-api` are `1/1 Running`, yet running `kubectl get endpoints checkout-svc` shows `<none>` in the `ENDPOINTS` column. What is the most likely cause?
choicesEn: The Worker Node's disk is full
The `spec.selector` field of `Service/checkout-svc` does not match the actual `labels` on the Pods
HorizontalPodAutoscaler has not been installed on the cluster
Docker Hub is undergoing scheduled maintenance
K19-Q2.explainEn: If Pods are `1/1` (meaning `Ready=true`) while the Service's `Endpoints` is still `<none>`, the Service's `spec.selector` definitely does not match the Pods' `metadata.labels` (or they were accidentally created in different Namespaces)!

K19-Q3.qEn: When a new release causes severe errors in `production` during peak hours, the standard SRE response is to immediately run `kubectl rollout undo` to restore service within seconds before calmly analyzing and fixing the code.
K19-Q3.explainEn: True! The highest priority during a production outage is minimizing downtime (MTTR) via an instant rollback, never making customers wait while you debug and patch code live.

K19-Q4.qEn: What happens if a `Service` has a `selector` matching the Pods and `Endpoints` contains IP addresses, but `targetPort` on the Service is `8080` while the Express app actually calls `app.listen(3000)`?
choicesEn: Kubernetes automatically changes the Express app port to 8080 without code changes
Traffic reaches the right Pod but hits port 8080 where nothing is listening, causing `Connection Refused` / `502 Bad Gateway`
The Pod is immediately OOMKilled
The Deployment automatically scales replicas down to 0
K19-Q4.explainEn: kube-proxy forwards traffic to `PodIP:8080`, but port 8080 inside the Pod's Network Namespace is closed (since Node.js listens on 3000), so the Linux kernel replies with TCP RST (`Connection Refused`), causing the Ingress to return `502 Bad Gateway`.

K19-Q5.qEn: Complete the CLI command to urgently roll back `deployment/frontend` in the `production` namespace to its immediately preceding stable revision:
K19-Q5.explainEn: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name> -n <namespace>` immediately restores the Pod Template to the previous stable Revision.

K19-Q6.qEn: If a `Deployment` sets `maxUnavailable: 50%` and has no `readinessProbe`, half of the old Pods are terminated immediately during a Rolling Update while new Pods receive customer traffic before Node.js has finished starting.
K19-Q6.explainEn: True! That is precisely what causes capacity drops and failed requests during deployments. You should set `maxUnavailable: 0` together with `readinessProbe` and `preStop`.

K19-Q7.qEn: Besides raising `limits.memory` in YAML, what is the core engineering solution in Node.js application code to process hundreds of megabytes of CSV/PDF files without triggering `OOMKilled`?
choicesEn: Use `fs.readFileSync` to load the entire file into a single String
Use Node.js `Streams` (`fs.createReadStream` with `stream.pipeline`) to process small chunks using only a few MB of constant RAM
Completely disable the V8 Garbage Collector
Change the listening port from 3000 to 80
K19-Q7.explainEn: Streaming with backpressure control via `stream.pipeline` keeps RAM consumption flat at a few dozen MB whether the input file is 50MB or 5GB!

K19-C1.frontEn: What does `Reason: OOMKilled, Exit Code: 137` mean in `kubectl describe pod`?
K19-C1.backEn: The container consumed more RAM than its `resources.limits.memory` ceiling and was terminated by the Linux kernel with `SIGKILL (9)` (`128 + 9 = 137`).

K19-C2.frontEn: What are the first two commands to run when Pods are `Running` yet the Service/Ingress returns `502 Bad Gateway`?
K19-C2.backEn: `kubectl get endpoints <svc-name>` and `kubectl get pods --show-labels` to verify whether `Service.spec.selector` and `targetPort` match the Pods.

K19-C3.frontEn: How do you view rollout history and perform an emergency rollback for a Deployment in the `production` namespace?
K19-C3.backEn: View history: `kubectl rollout history deployment/<name> -n production`; Roll back: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name> -n production`.

K19-C4.frontEn: What trio of configurations is required for 100% Zero-Downtime Rolling Updates on a Node.js API?
K19-C4.backEn: 1) `rollingUpdate: { maxUnavailable: 0, maxSurge: 1 }`, 2) an accurate `readinessProbe`, 3) `lifecycle.preStop: sleep 5` + graceful `SIGTERM` handling in code.

K19-C5.frontEn: How is the SRE principle "Mitigate first, investigate later" applied in Kubernetes?
K19-C5.backEn: When a new deployment breaks Production, immediately run `rollout undo` in seconds to restore service for users, then collect logs and fix the bug in a development environment.

K19-C6.frontEn: If `kubectl get endpoints <svc>` is completely empty (`<none>`) even though the `selector` matches the Pods identically, what else could be happening?
K19-C6.backEn: All Pods are failing their `readinessProbe` (`READY 0/1`), so Kubernetes has temporarily removed them from the `Endpoints` list!

kube-ex-k19-1.titleEn: Drill #5 — Fix OOMKilled (Exit Code 137) for pdf-exporter
kube-ex-k19-1.promptEn:
The `pdf-exporter` invoice service crashes abruptly every time customers download a PDF!

Complete both **2 steps**:
- **Step 1 (Required in the Diagnostic Terminal):** Run `kubectl describe pod pdf-exporter-10001` in the **Diagnostic Terminal** above to confirm the `OOMKilled` (`Exit Code: 137`) status and the current tight RAM limit.
- **Step 2:** Increase `resources.requests.memory` to `"128Mi"` and `resources.limits.memory` to at least **`"256Mi"`** in the `Deployment` manifest below so the Pods remain stably **`Running`**!
hintsEn: Run `kubectl describe pod pdf-exporter-10001` in the Diagnostic Terminal first.
Then update `requests.memory: "128Mi"` and `limits.memory: "256Mi"` in the YAML file.

kube-ex-k19-2.titleEn: Drill #6 — Fix 502 Bad Gateway (Endpoints: <none>) on checkout-svc
kube-ex-k19-2.promptEn:
Red alert from the Cart page: customers clicking Checkout are all getting **`502 Bad Gateway`**, even though `kubectl get pods` shows both Pods healthy at `1/1 Running`!

- Run `kubectl get endpoints checkout-svc`, `kubectl get pods --show-labels`, and `kubectl describe pod checkout-api-1` in the **Diagnostic Terminal** to inspect the actual Pod labels and container port.
- **Task:** Fix both configuration errors (`spec.selector` and `targetPort`) in the `checkout-svc` `Service` manifest below so `checkout-svc` connects to **2 Ready Endpoints**!
hintsEn: `kubectl get pods --show-labels` shows the Pods carry the label `app=checkout-api` (not `checkout-backend`).
`kubectl describe pod checkout-api-1` shows `Ports: 3000` → change `targetPort: 3000`.

kube-ex-k19-3.titleEn: Drill #7 — Emergency Rollback via CLI in the production namespace
kube-ex-k19-3.promptEn:
9:00 PM emergency! Revision 3 (`acme/frontend:3.0.0-crash`) was just pushed to the **`production`** namespace, sending all 3 Pods of `deployment/frontend` into `CrashLoopBackOff`!

- You can inspect the rollout history with `kubectl rollout history deployment/frontend -n production`.
- **Task:** Write a `kubectl rollout undo` command in the Shell script box below to immediately roll back `deployment/frontend` in the **`production`** namespace to the previous stable version (`acme/frontend:2.8.1`)!
hintsEn: Don't forget the namespace flag `-n production`! Without it, `kubectl` searches the `default` namespace and returns NotFound.
Full syntax: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/frontend -n production`.

kube-ex-k19-4.titleEn: Drill #8 — Full Zero-Downtime Rolling Update Hardening for gateway-api
kube-ex-k19-4.promptEn:
Course capstone! Every time the team deploys a new release of `Deployment/gateway-api`, monitoring records roughly 150 dropped customer requests returning `502` due to 3 simultaneous configuration gaps:
- `maxUnavailable` is set to `50%` (terminating 2 of 4 old Pods immediately!)
- Completely missing `readinessProbe`
- Completely missing the graceful shutdown hook `lifecycle.preStop`

Harden the `Deployment` to achieve **100% Zero-Downtime**:
1. Set `spec.strategy.rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable: 0` and `maxSurge: 1`.
2. Add `readinessProbe` (`httpGet.path: /readyz`, `httpGet.port: 3000`, `periodSeconds: 5`).
3. Add `lifecycle.preStop.exec.command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 5"]` and set `spec.template.spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30`.
hintsEn: Change `maxUnavailable: 50%` to the integer `0`.
Add `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30` under `spec.template.spec` (at the same indentation level as `containers:`).
Add both `readinessProbe` (`/readyz`, `port: 3000`, `periodSeconds: 5`) and `lifecycle.preStop.exec.command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 5"]` inside the `- name: api` container.
